We should conduct a review of the data store. It is important that we store precisely what we say we store. Especially for linked issues/bound fields - we only store the _result_, not all of the data pulled from the source.

history.text:
Plan (2026-09-17), from live discussion with Tom:

PROBLEM: pickGithubFields/pickJiraFields/pickSalesforceFields build a
"maximalist" cache (labels, description, status, assignees, dates,
resolution, fixVersions -- and for Salesforce, the entire flattened
Compact Layout as a field map) and persist ALL of it into every linked
field's fieldRef, into the shared git-synced tracker.jsonl. Checked what
the linked field's own pill actually renders (buildTextCell's ref
branches): only key/owner/repo/num (GitHub), key/browseUrl (Jira),
id/name/url (Salesforce). Everything else is cached purely so a bound
field's rule can read source.<system>.foo -- and it's persisted whether
or not any rule ever reads it. In the real tracker today exactly one rule
exists, reading exactly one field. Risk: accidentally shipping unrelated
bridged-source material (e.g. a Salesforce record's other fields) into a
file other people can read, just because a link exists.

DECISION: store nothing from the linked field beyond what's needed to
display it. Bound fields store only their computed result, same as
today's values[colId] -- never the source snapshot.

CONSEQUENCE, agreed: recompute of a bound field currently happens live,
on every render, straight from the persisted fieldRef (offline, instant,
reconstructable from the file alone -- FORMAT.md's own stated goal).
Once fieldRef stops carrying the maximalist payload, that's no longer
possible -- recompute can only happen at refresh time (when we have a
live payload in hand), not on every render or on a bare rule edit. A
collaborator with no GitHub/Jira/SF credentials of their own can no
longer independently verify or reconstruct why a bound field has its
value -- only see whatever result someone else's refresh produced.
Confirmed desirable.

MECHANISM (covers tracker #66's null-unlock behavior too, which also
currently depends on a live per-render rule re-evaluation):
- fieldRef trimmed to display-only shape: {system, owner, repo, num} for
  GitHub, {system, key, browseUrl} for Jira, {system, id, name, url} for
  Salesforce. pickGithubFields/pickJiraFields/pickSalesforceFields and
  the "maximalist" object are used ONLY in-memory at fetch/refresh time,
  never persisted.
- At fetch/refresh time, with the live payload in hand: evaluate every
  bound field whose linkedSourceId points at the field being
  fetched/refreshed, against the live (in-memory only) source object.
  Persist only the computed result via applyComputedToField, tagged with
  an explicit origin: 'derived' marker on that field's history entry when
  the rule computed a real (non-null) value -- distinct from a plain user
  edit or a null-computation (which logs a normal/non-derived entry,
  matching "let the field be overridden" from #66).
- Render-time locking (isFieldLocked, and every computeBoundValue call
  site: text/select/multiselect cells, bulk-edit gating, kanban card
  resolution -- ~8 places) stops evaluating the rule at all. Locked
  becomes "does this field's most recent history entry have
  origin: 'derived'" -- cheap, no rule eval, no source data needed,
  preserves the null-unlock behavior (a manual edit after a null
  computation is a non-derived entry, stays unlocked until the next
  refresh re-decides).
- applyLinkedRules (today's offline recompute-on-merge/hydrate path)
  goes away in its current form -- nothing left to recompute from
  offline. Replaced by whatever the fetch/refresh flow now does directly.

Will update docs/FORMAT.md's "Field provenance" section, wigwag-core.js
(+ its hand-synced copy in wigwag.html's WigwagCore IIFE), the encoded
app source's fetch/refresh methods and the ~8 render-time call sites,
check wigwag-cli.js/wigwag-client.js/wigwag-agent.js for any fieldRef-
shape assumptions, add regression coverage, then run the full suite
before calling this done.

Shipped (2026-09-18):

FIELDREF SHAPE: a linked GitHub/Jira/Salesforce field's persisted fieldRef
is now display-only -- {system, owner, repo, num} for GitHub, {system,
key, browseUrl} for Jira, {system, id, name, url} for Salesforce. That's
all the pill rendering ever reads. The old "maximalist" picked field set
(labels, description, status, assignees, dates, resolution, fixVersions,
and for Salesforce the record's entire Compact Layout as a field map) is
no longer persisted anywhere, whether or not any rule ever used it.

BOUND FIELDS: a new applyLiveLinkedRules (wigwag-core.js, hand-synced into
wigwag.html's WigwagCore IIFE) recomputes every field bound to a
just-fetched/refreshed link against the real, live payload -- used
in-memory only, right there in applyGithubLinkToField/
applyJiraLinkToField/applySalesforceLinkToField, and discarded the moment
that call finishes. Nothing about the live payload reaches setState,
history, or disk beyond the computed result itself.

Consequence, agreed on before starting: a bound field can no longer
recompute live on every render (or on a bare rule edit) from an
already-linked source -- only a refresh of that source now recomputes it,
using whatever's actually in hand at that moment. A collaborator with no
GitHub/Jira/Salesforce credentials can no longer independently
reconstruct why a bound field has its value from the file alone, only see
whatever a refresh already produced.

LOCK STATE: render-time locking (isFieldLocked/computeBoundValue, now
taking colId) still live-evaluates for a field bound to a plain or
wigwag-linked source (never given the maximalist treatment, nothing
trimmed there). For a github/jira/salesforce-sourced bound field, it
instead checks whether the field's own most recent history entry has
origin:'derived' -- set only when a refresh's live recompute produced a
real (non-null) value. This preserves tracker #66's "a null computation
unlocks the field for manual editing" behavior with no rule re-evaluation
needed at render time: a null result is never written (same "hands off"
rule applyLinkedRules always used), so a never-refreshed field, or one
whose last refresh computed null, simply has no derived entry to find.

Known limitation: a "copy field" bound row's own CONDITION
(computeBoundFieldRef, #66 Part 2) still evaluates against the trimmed
persisted ref if the condition itself reads source.<system>.foo -- narrow
enough (a row condition, not the common plain-value-rule case) to leave
documented rather than threading live data through that path too.

Historical data: trimming only applies going forward -- history is signed
and immutable, so anything already linked+fetched by a build before this
shipped keeps the old maximalist shape baked into that signed entry
permanently; there's no retroactive fix short of a dedicated fieldRef
redaction feature (out of scope here). Confirmed nothing in this tracker's
own real data had ever linked anything, so this was live for zero
existing issues.

Updated docs/FORMAT.md's "Field provenance" section with the full new
model. Rewrote 9 tests in tests/external-auth.spec.js that asserted the
old maximalist shape or expected live (non-refresh) bound-field
recomputation, added new unit test coverage in wigwag-core.test.js
(computeBoundValue's origin-based branch, applyLiveLinkedRules), fixed
wigwag-cli.js's isFieldLocked call site (new colId parameter). Full

history.value: Enhance the filter bar to filter by fields, with a field name autocomplete and a label value autocomplete UX just like the github projects one please!

history.text:
Plan (2026-09-18):

CURRENT STATE: the filter bar (filter-input) is plain keyword substring
match against title + linked-field ref text, plus a separate "#id" jump
mode (autocomplete dropdown of matching issue ids, already built --
jump-panel, jumpMode/jumpActiveIndex, onFilterKeyDown). Column-level
filtering already exists separately, per-column, via checkboxes in each
column header's "..." menu (columnFilters state, issueValueMatchesFilter/
computeColumnFilterExcludedIds in wigwag-core.js) -- select/multiselect
(checkbox list of configured options + "No value"), date (from/to range +
presets). That mechanism is well-tested and stays exactly as it is.

DESIGN: extend the SAME filter-input text box to also parse GitHub-
Projects-style `field:value` tokens, with two-stage autocomplete --
typing a token with no colon suggests matching FIELD LABELS; completing
`label:` (a recognized label) suggests that field's VALUES. This is a new,
independent, always-live (non-sticky, recomputed every render, like the
existing keyword match) filter layer -- ANDed with whatever the checkbox-
based column filters are separately doing, not merged into that state, so
neither mechanism's existing behavior/tests change.

- Parsing (pure, wigwag-core.js): split filterQuery on whitespace
  (a "..." quoted span counts as one token, for a value with spaces, e.g.
  status:"In Progress"). A token of the shape `label:value` where `label`
  case-insensitively matches a real field's label becomes a field token;
  everything else (no colon, or an unrecognized label) is kept as plain
  keyword text and re-joined for the existing substring match.
- Matching (pure, wigwag-core.js): select/multiselect resolve `value`
  against the field's configured options (case-insensitive id or label);
  no match found for the typed value -> that token is ignored (doesn't
  hide everything on a stray typo pre-autocomplete). date accepts an ISO
  date or a preset keyword (today/last7/last30/thismonth), reusing
  dateFilterPresetRanges. text/issue/commentStream: case-insensitive
  substring match against the stored value, freeform, no value
  autocomplete offered (nothing enumerable to suggest). Multiple tokens
  on the SAME field OR together (status:done status:"in progress"
  matches either) -- multiple DIFFERENT fields AND together -- same
  semantics the checkbox filters already use, for consistency.
- Autocomplete UI: a new dropdown panel (mirrors the existing jump-panel
  pattern/keyboard handling almost exactly -- ArrowUp/Down navigate,
  Enter/Tab commits the active suggestion into the text and keeps typing,
  Escape dismisses without clearing the box) showing under the filter
  input whenever the LAST token being typed is either colon-less (field
  suggestions: matching labels) or a completed `label:` with a recognized
  label (value suggestions: that field's options / date presets). Assumes
  the cursor stays at the end of the input while typing, same simplifying
  assumption the existing id-jump feature already makes.
- Scope: desktop table + kanban view only (both already share
  filterQuery/this same render-time filtering step) -- mobile's own
  filter input keeps its current simpler behavior, no autocomplete, per
  precedent of scoping UX passes to what's actually asked.

history.value: Investigate tracker.jsonl history-entry size overhead (redundant text, repeated pubKey)

history.text:
Tom noticed the file format stores a lot of redundant human-readable text in history entries (e.g. "Assignee set to Ben") that's technically derivable from field + value. Worth investigating whether/how to reduce it:

- The text IS intentionally redundant today, not accidental: it's part of the signed payload, so it locks in wording (option labels, field labels) as true at authoring time. Deriving it instead from CURRENT fieldDefs would retroactively rewrite history if a field/option is later renamed, and would break entirely for a since-deleted field (no label left to reconstruct from).
- Removing/changing it isn't free: it's baked into what gets cryptographically signed, so any change to the stored shape breaks verification of every existing signature -- this would need a real migration story, not just a code change.
- Measured the actual overhead split: a typical entry's "text" string is ~20-40 bytes, dwarfed by the ~400+ bytes of crypto overhead ALREADY on every single entry (two base64 ES256 signatures + a full JWK public key, all repeated verbatim per entry, even from the same identity). So text isn't actually the biggest lever for file size.
- The bigger opportunity, if this is worth pursuing, is probably deduplicating the repeated pubKey (e.g. a per-identity key registry referenced by id/fingerprint instead of inlining the full JWK on every entry) -- much larger potential savings, but a bigger structural change with its own tradeoffs (lookup indirection, more complex verification code, migration of existing files).

Related to #106 (ba01ddc6, project files getting large) and #116 (b564316d, data-minimization review) -- this is really a continuation of that size-reduction thread, focused specifically on per-entry crypto/text overhead rather than fieldRef payload bloat.

history.value: Merge provenance (A): signed export envelope + TOFU trust states

history.text:
Part A of merge_provenance.zip (design handoff, see #121/843ac132). Sequenced first per the handoff's own dependency order -- the export format and trust states are the foundation both prose-merge (B, d100c705) and the UI (C, 5c3051e9) build on.

Scope (README §1):
- New export envelope: line 1 of an export becomes {type:'wigwag.export', v:1, exported_by, exported_at, project, tracker, records, content_sha256, sig}. Every subsequent line is an existing record, unchanged. A file with no envelope on line 1 (v0) still ingests -- unsigned, unattributed.
- content_sha256 over the raw on-disk bytes of lines 2..n (not a re-serialization) -- verify before parsing; a hash mismatch marks the import 'damaged' but never blocks ingest.
- Signing: per Tom's call, reuse wigwag's EXISTING WebCrypto ECDSA P-256 identity-key signing (already used for every history entry) for the envelope's sig, rather than real SSH signatures -- infeasible in a filesystem-less browser PWA. Same opt-in-per-identity behavior the spec describes (an identity either has a signing key configured or doesn't; never generate one silently -- true today already).
- TOFU trust store: remember a sender identity's fingerprint on first successful signed ingest; compare on every subsequent one. Three states only: signed (quiet, one line), unsigned (stated plainly, never obstructed), changed (the only loud state -- name old+new fingerprint, offer Trust this key / Keep the old one). Two distinct failure modes (signature doesn't verify, content hash mismatch) both fold into changed's visual treatment but must be labelled distinctly. Nothing here gates the merge -- an unsigned file merges in one click, same as today.
- Store per sender identity, not per project.

Setting Status to Next -- this is the one to start on.

**wigwag-core.js** (new pure functions, 12 new unit tests, 109/109 passing):
- `buildExportEnvelope`/`parseExportEnvelope`/`verifyExportEnvelope` -- the envelope shape from the handoff's §1.1, with content_sha256 hashed over on-disk bytes (§1.2) and signing over the hash's hex (§1.3), using wigwag's EXISTING WebCrypto ECDSA identity keys (per the earlier decision) rather than SSH.

history.text:
Part B of merge_provenance.zip (design handoff, see #121/843ac132). Depends on A (a61676e0) -- needs the export envelope/provenance data to attribute conflict markers correctly. README §2, §4.

Scope:
- Scalar fields: last-write-wins by edit timestamp, ties broken by identity string ascending. NOTE: this is very likely ALREADY correct, as an emergent property of the existing signed-history-union merge (unionByKey + deriveIssueValues picking the latest sortKey) -- worth confirming with a test before writing any new logic, not assuming new code is needed here.
- Prose fields (description, long-text custom fields): genuinely new -- a three-way diff3 merge against the common ancestor. Non-overlapping edits merge silently; overlapping regions get conflict markers written directly into the field's text, staying there as real content (no pending/staging state).
- Marker grammar (fix now, will need to parse it back later): '<<<<<<< local copy · <identity>' / '=======' / '>>>>>>> <identity> · export <date> · <signed|unsigned|signed, new key>'.
- Open question flagged in the handoff, needs a real decision before implementing: does wigwag re-parse markers on every save (clears the 'needs a look' state only when cleanly removed, survives a partial edit) or just detect the literal <<<<<<< prefix as inert text? Recommend the cheaper 'detect literal prefix' approach unless Tom wants the more thorough one -- will flag for a decision when this is picked up.
- New local-only merge record per ingest ({type:'wigwag.merge', ingested_at, ingested_by, source:{...envelope fields...}, issues:[{id, fields:[{field, outcome, winner, edits:[...]}]}]}) -- records WHAT the merge did, not current issue state.
- Locality rule (README §4): merge records NEVER leave the copy that created them. Export writers filter out type:'wigwag.merge' unconditionally -- no flag, no exception. In a browser context this is a separate localStorage key (parallel to how COLUMN_ORDER_KEY etc. already stay local-only), not a gitignored sibling file as literally described (no filesystem here). Good test per the handoff: export from a copy with merge history must be byte-identical to export from a fresh copy with the same issue state; deleting the local merge log must not change a single issue value.

Implemented and verified live. Summary:

**wigwag-core.js** (new pure functions, 138/138 unit tests passing):
- `diff3Merge` -- a real three-way line merge using the 'common backbone' algorithm (base lines untouched by BOTH sides become sync anchors; segments between anchors resolve independently). Matches the handoff's own §2.1 example exactly. An earlier positional-hunk-alignment attempt was tried and found broken (silently dropped a non-overlapping edit adjacent to a real conflict) before landing on this approach -- documented as a regression test.
- `conflictMarkerLines`/`provenanceMarkerSuffix` -- the exact marker grammar from §2.2, naming the local edit's author, the inbound export's sender/date/signature state.
- `hasUnresolvedMergeMarkers` -- the handoff's own flagged open question, resolved: cheap literal `<<<<<<<` prefix detection over a full re-parse-on-save.
- `computeMergeProseEntries` -- for every type:'text' field where both sides authored unseen entries, runs diff3 against the shared ancestor and returns one new entry descriptor (idempotent -- re-merging the same file twice is a no-op).
- `buildMergeRecord`/`buildMergeIssueSummary`/`mergeLogStorageKey` -- the local-only merge log (§2.3/§4), scoped per-project, capped at 200 entries, structurally incapable of leaking into an export (buildSourceText never reads from it).

**wigwag.html wiring:**
- startMerge now commits one real signed entry per prose merge (authored by the CURRENT/merging identity) and records a merge-log entry when anything was touched.
- onMergeFileChange/onSubmitPasteMerge now properly sequence provenance classification before merging (was fire-and-forget in Part A, now needed for real marker attribution).
- wigwag-cli.js needs no changes -- it only reads mergedIssues from computeIssueMerge's return, so CLI-driven merges keep the older scalar-only behavior for prose fields (documented, not a gap).

**Two live bugs found and fixed during verification, both incorporated:**
1. Tom asked for the pre-existing 'merge notice' red dot badge on row title cells to be removed entirely (unwanted UI) -- done; the underlying detection now feeds the merge log instead of a bare dot.
2. Tom flagged the conflict entry's text as too casual -- reworded to '<field> updated by merge — merge conflicts require human review.'
3. Found live: the marker grammar's own '>>>>>>> ...' line is standard markdown blockquote syntax, and a lone '=======' line is a markdown setext-heading underline -- either would have mangled real conflict text the moment it displayed. Fixed: text with real markers now renders as plain escaped text instead of running through markdown at all.

**Tests:** 138 unit tests, 19 new Playwright tests in tests/merge-provenance.spec.js, 1 new regression test in tests/select-fields.spec.js (the markdown-collision fix), full regression across data-structures/github-sync/select-fields, and a clean 816/816 full suite run.

history.text:
Part C of merge_provenance.zip (design handoff, see #121/843ac132). Depends on A (a61676e0) and B (d100c705) -- this is purely the view over their data, per the handoff's own dependency ordering ('the format makes the view possible; the view is what ingest renders'). README §3, §5.

Scope -- three nested levels of ONE component, reused (with a receiving:true/false flag, never a user-facing 'Reading as' toggle -- that's explicitly a prototype-only affordance, not to ship) for both ingest-time review and merge history:
- Level 1 (always visible): sender, relative date, one-line summary, provenance line (state glyph + plain language per signed/unsigned/changed), envelope digest (record count + sha256, monospace, right-aligned). For 'changed' only: an amber key strip on expand with Trust this key / Keep the old one -- the only decision point in the whole flow, and it's about the key, never about the merge itself.
- Level 2 (default expand): per-issue table, one row per touched field -- settled value, edit count (load-bearing -- this is what signals whether the timeline is worth opening), origin note. Prose fields with markers render the actual merged body inline as a diff (tinted lines, amber marker lines) -- not a summary word.
- Level 3 (collapsed): two-lane timeline, local left/inbound right, dated gutter, 'both copies matched until N days ago' divergence marker. Each edit shows previous value (faded 45%, THAT LANE's prior value specifically, not the other side's) -> new value.
- New 'Merge history' entry in the project menu (badged only when something's genuinely unresolved: changed key awaiting a decision, a damaged file, or issues still carrying markers -- never just because a merge happened).
- An issue's own activity history should link back to the merge that touched it.
- Never use the word 'conflict' in UI chrome for the merge itself (conflicts are a property of the TEXT, not the merge action). Never add a confirmation step, staging area, or per-field checkboxes -- merging is never a question.
- Full test-id list is in the handoff's §6 (merge-card, merge-provenance[+data-sig-state], merge-key-strip, btn-trust-key, btn-keep-key, merge-envelope, merge-issue[+data-issue-id], merge-field-row[+data-field], merge-edit-count, merge-inline-diff, merge-marker-line, btn-merge-timeline, merge-timeline, merge-event[+data-side], btn-merge-primary, btn-merge-secondary, merge-history-list) -- reuse those exactly, don't invent new ones.

Starting. Before diving into markup, flagging one real ambiguity in the handoff worth resolving up front, and a small necessary extension to Part B's data shape -- proceeding with everything unambiguous in parallel rather than blocking on either.

**Ambiguity (asking Tom in chat, not blocking on it):** §5 describes the ingest-time card's primary/secondary actions as literally 'Merge update' / 'Not now' -- which reads like a pre-merge confirmation gate. But §2.1/the 'Do not' list say just as emphatically 'never ask the user to choose' and 'block, gate, or delay merge on any provenance state' -- and Part A/B already shipped (and Tom has used) an IMMEDIATE-apply merge flow with zero confirmation step. I'm not going to silently change already-shipped, approved merge behavior to add a new gate -- that's a real behavior change, not a UI-only addition. Treating the ingest-time card as a POST-merge summary (shown right after Apply Update completes, same component, receiving:true) unless told otherwise.

**Data shape extension:** Part B's buildMergeIssueSummary only stored outcome/winner/marker-count per field -- enough for a summary line, not enough for Level 3's two-lane timeline (which needs the actual per-edit list). Rather than duplicate edit content (actor/value/time) into the merge log -- which would go stale or leak past a later redaction -- extending it to store just localEntryIds/incomingEntryIds (real history entry ids) per field, so the UI joins live against the issue's own (redaction-respecting) current history at render time. No new value storage, no redaction bypass.

**Plan:**
1. Extend buildMergeIssueSummary (backward-compatible field addition) + tests.
2. Pure view-model builders in wigwag-core.js for Level 1 (provenance line/glyph, reusing Part A's classifyExportProvenance), Level 2 (settled value + edit count + origin note, prose fields get the real merged body), Level 3 (two-lane timeline with per-lane previous-value tracking + divergence marker).
3. New 'Merge history' entry in the Project panel (alongside Notes/Sync/Danger Zone) -- badged only when something's genuinely unresolved (changed key, damaged file, or an issue still carrying literal markers), never just because a merge happened.
4. Full test-id list reused exactly per §6 (merge-card, merge-provenance[+data-sig-state], merge-key-strip, btn-trust-key, btn-keep-key, merge-envelope, merge-issue[+data-issue-id], merge-field-row[+data-field], merge-edit-count, merge-inline-diff, merge-marker-line, btn-merge-timeline, merge-timeline, merge-event[+data-side], btn-merge-primary, btn-merge-secondary, merge-history-list).
5. Trust actions (btn-trust-key/btn-keep-key) wired to Part A's existing rememberSenderTrust primitive.
6. Never the word 'conflict' in UI chrome for the merge action itself; no 'Reading as' toggle shipped.

Full-suite verification at the end, as always.

Confirmed with Tom: building BOTH mechanisms, matching the handoff's own design exactly (same component, receiving:true/false flips which pair of actions shows):

- Ingest time (receiving:true): Apply Update now shows the provenance card FIRST as a real whole-file gate -- 'Merge update' (primary, applies) / 'Not now' (secondary, discards, nothing changes). This IS a behavior change from Parts A/B's already-shipped instant-apply -- their existing tests asserting 'no modal, applies immediately' will be updated to click through the new gate. Still never a per-field decision -- the whole file merges or nothing does.
- Merge History (receiving:false): 'Back out this update' (primary) / 'Download update' (secondary) -- a clean, real rollback for an already-applied merge, implemented as new signed entries restoring each touched field's pre-merge local value (never a silent mutation/deletion of the merge's own history -- consistent with the rest of wigwag's append-only model). Skips (with a note, doesn't clobber) any field that's been edited again since the merge, rather than silently discarding newer work.

Revised implementation order:
1. Extend the merge-log record (Part B) with per-field localEntryIds/incomingEntryIds/preMergeLocalEntryId/resultEntryId -- enough to reconstruct Level 3's timeline AND to know whether a field is still safely revertible, without duplicating any value content (redaction-safe, joins live against real history).
2. Pure rollback computation (computeMergeRollbackEntries) -- refuses to revert a field that's changed again since the merge.
3. Split startMerge into previewMerge (pure computation, no side effects) + confirmPendingMerge (applies) + cancelPendingMerge, so the SAME real merge computation backs both the gate's preview and the actual apply -- no duplicate logic.
4. Level 1/2/3 pure view-model builders.
5. wigwag.html wiring: the gate modal on Apply Update, the Merge History project-panel section (badged only when genuinely unresolved), all §6 test ids, trust actions.
6. Update existing Part A/B tests for the new gate step; add new tests for rollback + history UI; full suite.

Part C shipped: Apply Update now gates on a real "Merge update"/"Not now" confirm, and a new Merge History project-panel section lets a past merge be reviewed in real per-field detail (including a two-lane timeline) and, as one whole-transaction action, backed out.

Per Tom's own call in chat ("nobody picks or chooses about individual state changes -- the merge applies en masse or not at all"), this is a real behavior change from Parts A/B's shipped instant-apply for Apply Update's file/paste path specifically -- GitHub sync and Connect Remote's first pull are untouched (no envelope/signature to gate on in the first place, so they still apply immediately).

**Data layer** (wigwag-core.js): buildMergeIssueSummary extended (backward-compatible) with localEntryIds/incomingEntryIds/preMergeLocalEntryId/resultEntryId per field -- real history entry ids only, never duplicated value/actor/time content, so a renderer joins them live against the issue's own (redaction-respecting) current history. New pure functions: patchMergeSummaryResultEntryId, fieldStillSafeToRevert, computeMergeRollbackEntries (refuses -- with a reason, never silently -- to revert a field edited again since the merge, redacted since, or since deleted from the schema), buildMergePreviewViewModel/buildMergeFieldTimeline (Level 1/2/3 render-ready shapes), mergeRecordNeedsAttention (the History badge's own narrow condition).

**wigwag.html wiring**: startMerge split into startMerge (instant, unchanged, used by GitHub sync/Connect Remote) + applyComputedMerge (the shared apply logic) + previewMerge/confirmPendingMerge/cancelPendingMerge (Apply Update's own gated path) + rollbackMerge. The gate is a single top-level overlay (alongside connect-remote-overlay, viewport-independent -- reachable from both desktop and mobile, since mobile's own Apply Update entry point is the same paste flow). Merge History is a new Project Panel section (alongside Notes/Sync & Export/Danger Zone), badged only when mergeRecordNeedsAttention finds something genuinely unresolved.

**Test ids**: reused the handoff's §6 list exactly -- merge-card, merge-provenance[+data-sig-state], merge-envelope, merge-key-strip, btn-trust-key, btn-keep-key, merge-issue[+data-issue-id], merge-field-row[+data-field], merge-edit-count, merge-inline-diff, merge-marker-line, btn-merge-timeline, merge-timeline, merge-event[+data-side], btn-merge-primary, btn-merge-secondary, merge-history-list.

**Two deliberate scope cuts**, both to keep this shippable without inventing new UI conventions:
- Merge History's secondary action is "Close" (collapse), not "Download update" -- reconstructing an exportable file from a past merge log record (which deliberately stores only entry ids, not values) would need real new logic; not built.
- Level 3's two-lane timeline lives only in Merge History (per field, on demand via "View timeline"), not in the pre-merge gate itself -- the gate's Level 1+2 already gives enough to decide "does this feel safe" before a merge exists to have a timeline over.

A stale test-only bug in buildTestExport (never set projectId, so every Part A TOFU test silently went down the "brand new project" dialog branch instead of ever reaching a real same-project merge) fixed as part of this -- harmless before now, but blocking for tests that need the gate to actually appear.

Two failures during the full run were investigated and are NOT regressions -- tests/project-notes.spec.js's own nav-label list needed the new "Merge history" entry added (fixed, now asserts all 4 sections); tests/interaction.spec.js's History-tab-reset test re-ran clean in isolation and as a full file (193/193) -- a pre-existing order-dependent flake, unrelated to this work. - Timeline event rows: the relative time label (e.g. "4h ago") now carries the real absolute timestamp as a hover tooltip (title attribute), computed via the same formatDateLabel used elsewhere, guarded by the same hasRealSortKey check used for the label itself.

Verified: 156/156 wigwag-core unit tests, 27/27 merge-provenance.spec.js (updated the one test asserting the old exact copy text), full data-structures/github-sync/project-notes regression in progress.

Round 5 fix: live bug found via Tom's own real usage on #132 (68d960f2) -- the Level 3 timeline showed the SAME real history entry twice, once tagged "local" and once tagged "incoming".

Root cause: buildMergeIssueSummary's localEntryIds/incomingEntryIds (the raw material buildMergeFieldTimeline/buildMergeIssueTimeline render from) were built from every authored entry each side's OWN history contains for a field, with no check for whether that entry was actually shared (present identically on both sides -- e.g. a "Status defaulted to Todo" entry that already existed on GitHub before a background sync even ran). A shared/common ancestor entry isn't either side's own contribution to THIS merge, so it should never be double-counted as if each side authored it independently.

Fix: localEntryIds/incomingEntryIds now exclude (by entryKey) any entry present on the OTHER side too, in both the scalar and prose-field loops of buildMergeIssueSummary (wigwag-core.js + wigwag.html's WigwagCore IIFE). preMergeLocalEntryId/resultEntryId are untouched (rollback still needs local's real pre-merge entry, shared or not). This also fixes a related over-counting bug in the "Show the timeline -- N edits across both copies" toggle label, which was double-counting shared entries the same way.

Three pre-existing unit tests had explicitly encoded the buggy behavior as their expected output (literally asserting the shared entry appears in both lists) -- updated their assertions to the corrected behavior, and extended one with dedicated regression coverage.

Verified: 158/158 unit tests, 27/27 merge-provenance.spec.js, 97/97 broader regression (data-structures/github-sync/project-notes).

Separately: Tom also asked why the final "Status: Done" transition didn't appear anywhere in that timeline. Confirmed via the raw synced history that this is NOT a bug -- the merge-history record only covers ONE sync event (between the In Progress and Done pushes); Done landed on GitHub afterward and would need its own, later sync/merge-log entry, which the Merge History list should show as a separate item. No code change for that part.

Round 6 fix, per Tom's direct request: removed the gate's "The only decision is whether to merge." caption entirely, and made a genuinely content-free merge say so explicitly with "Merge update" disabled.

WHAT CHANGED:
- The old caption span is gone. When there's nothing to land, a new "No changes -- this file matches what's already here." message takes its place (same flex:1 slot); otherwise the slot is just an empty spacer, same as the "nothing safe to revert" copy fix earlier this session.

FOLLOW-UP FIX (found via the broader regression suite, not live): my first cut of "is there anything to land" was `mergeIssueSummaries.length === 0` -- wrong, because mergeIssueSummaries is only ever populated for an issue that ALREADY existed locally and had a touched field/prose entry. It silently misses two real cases: a genuinely brand-new issue arriving (computeIssueMerge pushes it straight into mergedIssues via a separate loop, no summary entry, since there's no local counterpart to diff against) and a comment-only change (comments union via the entirely separate mergeCommentStreams mechanism, never touching mergeIssueSummaries at all). That meant the new disabled-button guard was silently BLOCKING legitimate merges bringing in only a new issue or only a new comment -- caught by 3 real regression failures (a new-issue cross-project merge, and a comments-union test, plus a re-import-merges-into-existing-project test that hit the same gap). Fixed with a new pure function, mergeHasRealChanges(localIssues, computed), added to wigwag-core.js (and mirrored into wigwag.html's WigwagCore copy) that checks mergeIssueSummaries.length OR a real difference in any merged issue's comment-stream length OR the presence of an issue with no local counterpart -- and wired it into both buildMergeGateViewModel's hasNoChanges and confirmPendingMerge's guard, replacing the naive check. Added a dedicated unit test in wigwag-core.test.js covering all four cases (touched field / comment-only / brand-new issue / genuinely identical).

Also found (during that same regression pass) a second bug in my own fix's plumbing, not the logic itself: my first edit to wire mergeHasRealChanges into wigwag.html's WigwagCore export list silently failed (an ambiguous string match the Edit tool correctly refused), and I didn't notice -- so the function existed in source but was undefined at runtime in the actual app, throwing inside buildMergeGateViewModel and breaking the merge gate universally (not just for comment/new-issue cases). Caught live via an ad-hoc Playwright repro capturing the console error, not by guessing. Fixed by actually completing that edit and re-verifying window.WigwagCore.mergeHasRealChanges is a function before re-running anything.

Fixed the shared applyPasteMerge helper (dismiss via "Not now" when the gate says no-changes, instead of clicking a disabled primary) and two manual gate sequences that had the same assumption baked in inline. The TOFU trust-store assertions themselves are unaffected -- classifyIngestProvenance runs and records trust independently, before the merge gate is even shown.

Added a new dedicated test for the no-changes behavior itself (message text, real disabled cursor, hover-color unchanged, click-does-nothing, "Not now" still works), plus the mergeHasRealChanges unit test above.

history.value: Keep opaque option ids (not plain label strings) as the storage model for select/multiselect values

history.text:
Tom raised this while reviewing #124's merge-provenance timeline (which had a bug showing raw option ids like opt_1787164390598 instead of resolved labels): would plain string values (the option's label) be cleaner than opaque ids for select/multiselect fields?

Discussed and resolved: keep the id model. Rationale --

- An option is {id, label, color, emoji}; stored values reference the id, not the label. This buys RENAME-SAFETY: renaming or recoloring an option doesn't retroactively change what any issue's current value points to, and doesn't require rewriting every issue that uses it.
- Switching to plain strings would make renaming a real migration problem: either rewrite every issue currently holding the old string, or accept that old values silently stop matching the renamed option (losing color/pill rendering, since color lives on the option row, not the value).
- What ids cost: readability. Raw ids leaking into UI/debug output (like the opt_1787164390598 bug just fixed in #124) is a recurring failure mode -- this is the second time an unresolved id has leaked into a rendered view.
- Resolution: keep ids for correctness/rename-safety. The actual fix for the recurring leak is a shared resolution helper used everywhere a value is displayed, which now exists: resolveFieldValueView(def, val) in wigwag-core.js, added as part of #124's Round 3 fixes, reused by both the current-settled-value view and the historical timeline view.

Marking Done -- this is a design decision now captured for the record, not an open task. If a new instance of 'raw id leaked into UI' turns up somewhere that doesn't yet go through resolveFieldValueView, that's a bug against that specific view, not a reason to revisit this decision.

history.value: Paste/import latency on medium-large projects: componentDidUpdate's unconditional persist+measure fan-out, not file size

history.text:
Investigated Tom's live report of "a couple of seconds to paste [a medium-sized project] into a new instance." Spun off #118 (file-size overhead) after profiling showed file size / JSON parsing is NOT the bottleneck -- this is the real one.

MEASURED (wigwag's own tracker as baseline, 113 issues/807KB, plus a synthetic 6x clone at 678 issues/4.8MB):
- Pure JSON parse+hydrate (parseJsonl, Node, no DOM): ~5ms -> ~14ms. Scales linearly and is negligible at either size.
- Full paste-to-rendered-table, real browser (Playwright, headless): ~515ms -> ~1.4-2.4s across repeated runs. This is the number Tom is actually feeling, and it does NOT track file size/byte count -- it tracks row count, and worse than linearly at times.

Took a CPU profile (CDP Profiler) of the 678-row case. Top self-time contributors outside the templating runtime itself:
- persist() [wigwag.html ~5155]: on EVERY call, does up to THREE full JSON.stringify/JSON.parse passes over the ENTIRE issues array -- (1) stringify outgoing issues, (2) parse the existing on-disk doc AND re-stringify ITS issues just to build a stale/conflict-detection comparison baseline, (3) stringify the whole doc again for the actual localStorage write. That's O(project size) work, up to 3x per call.
- componentDidUpdate() [wigwag.html ~5198] runs persist() plus 12 more side-effecting methods (persistSecrets/persistProjectIndex/persistIdentities/persistCommentReads/persistColumnWidths/persistColumnWrap/persistColumnOrder/persistColumnFilters/persistSort/maybeScheduleGithubPush/hydrateMarkdownBodies/autoGrowTextareas/measureTableOverflow) UNCONDITIONALLY on every single render commit, regardless of what actually changed. Instrumented localStorage.setItem/getItem call counts during one 678-row paste-import: 27 setItem + 30 getItem calls -- i.e. this whole fan-out (including persist()'s up-to-3x stringify pass) fires roughly 2-3 times per import, not once.
- measureTableOverflow() [wigwag.html ~4098]: calls getBoundingClientRect() on the scroll wrap AND on every single row, every time it runs, to compute the "N more rows below" fade indicator. Forces synchronous layout (layout thrashing) each call. Instrumented at 1359 getBoundingClientRect calls for 678 rows (~2/row) during one import -- consistent with componentDidUpdate's fan-out running this ~2x across the operation.
- The dc-runtime templating engine itself (resolvePath/cssToObj/kebabToCamel/findTopLevelEquality, in the bundled runtime script, not app code) accounted for ~150ms/~10% of sampled time -- real but secondary, and it's generated tooling rather than something to hand-edit.

Net: at 6x the row count, wall-clock time went up ~3-4x while the JSON-parsing cost only went up ~3x from a much smaller base (5ms->14ms) -- the dominant, disproportionate cost is this repeated whole-project persist+measure fan-out, which scales with row count AND with how many times componentDidUpdate happens to fire during one operation.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION (not yet implemented, needs its own design pass):
1. Gate componentDidUpdate's side effects on what actually changed (a prevState/prevProps-style diff) instead of running all 13 unconditionally every render.
2. Make persist()'s on-disk-conflict-detection baseline incremental/cached rather than re-parsing+re-stringifying the whole on-disk doc on every call just to compare.
3. Debounce/batch persist() during a burst of rapid state changes (e.g. a bulk import) so it fires once after things settle, not once per intermediate render.
4. Gate measureTableOverflow() to only actually measure when the row count or scroll-container size changed, and/or throttle it, instead of forcing a full per-row layout pass on every render.

Profiling scripts were ad-hoc/throwaway (Playwright + CDP Profiler), not committed -- happy to redo if useful for whoever picks this up.

Live report from Tom: pasting a large blob of text (or seemingly any text) into the new Receive textarea (tracker #143, dfb378b2) takes multiple seconds -- materially longer in Safari than Firefox for the same paste.

This is very likely the SAME root cause already diagnosed here, not a new bug: pasteMergeDraft is top-level app state, so a single paste event still triggers exactly one componentDidUpdate cycle -- but that cycle still unconditionally runs the full persist() (up to 3x JSON.stringify over the whole project) + measureTableOverflow() (a forced layout reflow per visible row) fan-out this issue already describes, regardless of the fact that nothing about a textarea draft actually needs any of that work re-run.

The Safari-vs-Firefox gap is plausibly consistent with this theory too -- measureTableOverflow's getBoundingClientRect() calls force synchronous layout, and layout/reflow performance characteristics genuinely differ across browser engines (WebKit vs Gecko) for the same forced-reflow pattern, especially at scale (more rows = more forced layout per call).

Not independently investigated/profiled (this comment is capturing the live report for whoever picks this up) -- but worth noting as an argument for prioritizing the componentDidUpdate gating fix, since it's now surfaced in a second, unrelated-seeming user-facing spot (typing/pasting into ANY top-level-state-backed textarea, not just the original full-page paste-import flow) rather than being a one-off.

Partial fix landed: measureTableOverflow() (one of the two named dominant costs) is now gated on componentDidUpdate's own blanket call -- only re-measures when state that could actually affect row count/layout changes, instead of on every single setState anywhere in the app. Verified via direct instrumentation: typing 34 uncommitted keystrokes now triggers at most 1 re-measurement, down from one per keystroke.

The OTHER named dominant cost, persist(), is NOT fixed here -- I attempted the same kind of gate and it reliably reproduced (4/5 in isolation) a genuine infinite cross-tab broadcast loop, rooted in a separate, pre-existing hydrate/strip round-trip bug. Reverted that specific change and filed it as its own issue (#210) for dedicated investigation, since it needs the round-trip made properly idempotent before a persist()-frequency gate is safe here.

Committed 2779ec2, full suite clean (1081 passed, 3 pre-existing unrelated flakes, independently re-verified).

history.value: Deduplicate per-entry pubKey via a per-identity key registry (file size ~18% smaller)

history.text:
Continuation of #118's investigation. Tom confirmed he still wants the file-size reduction pursued for its own sake, even after profiling (#131) showed it's not what's causing the paste-latency he reported -- that's a separate render-path problem.

MEASURED (wigwag's own tracker.jsonl, 807KB, 114 lines, 986 history/comment entries, 934 signed):
- pubKey fields: 167,654 bytes (~20.8% of the file)
- sig fields (unique per entry, cannot be deduped): 84,060 bytes (~10.4%)
- text fields: 196,665 bytes (~24.4%)
- Only 6 DISTINCT pubKey values across all 934 signed entries, across 3 identities (tom@lant.uk: 4 keys -- device rotation across sessions/machines --, claude@lant.uk: 2, dan@lant.uk: 1).

If those 6 keys were stored once in a small registry, and each entry carried a short reference instead of the full inlined JWK, the pubKey-related bytes drop from ~168KB to ~19KB (6 full keys + 934 short refs) -- a projected ~18.4% reduction in TOTAL file size from this change alone. Actual savings scale with how many distinct signing keys/identities have touched a project -- more identities or more device/key rotations means more duplication removed; a single-identity project sees a smaller win.

DESIGN SKETCH (not yet built -- needs review before implementation):
- Add a  map to the  line (alongside //etc.), keyed by a short fingerprint (fingerprintPublicKey already exists in wigwag-core.js, used today for TOFU trust records -- reuse it rather than inventing a second id scheme).
- Each history/comment entry carries  instead of inlining  directly. Verification (verifyPayload) looks the key up in the registry by fingerprint instead of reading it off the entry.
- BACKWARD COMPAT: an incoming file (older export, hand-authored, from before this ships) may still carry inline  per-entry with no  registry at all -- that path must keep working unchanged, not require a hard migration. A new export always writes the registry form.
- MIGRATION: on load, an entry with inline  but no matching  entry gets backfilled into the in-memory registry (same spirit as the existing legacy-backfill/hydrateIssue pattern in wigwag-core.js), so old and new-shaped data interoperate in the same file without a one-time destructive rewrite.
- Every one of the 5 tracker.jsonl-format coupling points needs updating together (per CLAUDE.md's standing note): wigwag.html (write + verify + WigwagCore IIFE mirror), wigwag-core.js (same, canonical copy), wigwag-cli.js, wigwag-client.js, wigwag-agent.js, plus docs/FORMAT.md and schema/tracker.schema.json.
- Signature verification itself is UNCHANGED in scope: sig is still per-entry and still can't be deduped (each entry signs its own distinct payload); this only touches the pubKey the signature is verified against.

This is a real format change with its own migration story -- scoping it here rather than starting it blind. Flagging for review/prioritization before implementation; can pick this up as a normal Status=Next item whenever it's ready to be worked.

Correction to my last comment -- the "DESIGN SKETCH" bullets got mangled by a shell-quoting mistake on my end (backtick-quoted field names were silently eaten). Reposting that section cleanly:

DESIGN SKETCH (not yet built -- needs review before implementation):
- Add a `keys` map to the `fields` line (alongside `fields`/`projectHistory`/etc.), keyed by a short fingerprint (fingerprintPublicKey already exists in wigwag-core.js, used today for TOFU trust records -- reuse it rather than inventing a second id scheme).
- Each history/comment entry carries `keyRef: <fingerprint>` instead of inlining `pubKey` directly. Verification (verifyPayload) looks the key up in the registry by fingerprint instead of reading it off the entry.
- BACKWARD COMPAT: an incoming file (older export, hand-authored, from before this ships) may still carry inline `pubKey` per-entry with no `keys` registry at all -- that path must keep working unchanged, not require a hard migration. A new export always writes the registry form.
- MIGRATION: on load, an entry with inline `pubKey` but no matching `keys` entry gets backfilled into the in-memory registry (same spirit as the existing legacy-backfill/hydrateIssue pattern in wigwag-core.js), so old and new-shaped data interoperate in the same file without a one-time destructive rewrite.
- Every one of the 5 tracker.jsonl-format coupling points needs updating together (per CLAUDE.md's standing note): wigwag.html (write + verify + WigwagCore IIFE mirror), wigwag-core.js (same, canonical copy), wigwag-cli.js, wigwag-client.js, wigwag-agent.js, plus docs/FORMAT.md and schema/tracker.schema.json.
- Signature verification itself is UNCHANGED in scope: sig is still per-entry and still can't be deduped (each entry signs its own distinct payload); this only touches the pubKey the signature is verified against.

Starting implementation. Refined approach from the design sketch above, after reading the actual code:

SCOPE NARROWER THAN FIRST SCOPED: every ingestion path (paste, file import, GitHub pull, CLI merge) funnels through the single parseJsonl function, and the single export/save/copy/GitHub-push path funnels through buildSourceText -- both already centralized in wigwag-core.js (and hand-mirrored into wigwag.html's WigwagCore IIFE, unchanged elsewhere). wigwag-cli.js calls core.buildSourceText/core.parseJsonl directly with no format-specific logic of its own; wigwag-client.js/wigwag-agent.js never touch the file format at all (they drive a real browser instance). So this needs changes in exactly TWO places, not five: wigwag-core.js and wigwag.html's WigwagCore IIFE (plus docs/FORMAT.md). schema/tracker.schema.json predates signing entirely per FORMAT.md's own disclaimer and isn't touched by this either.

MECHANISM: transform at the serialization boundary only, not the in-memory shape.
- In-memory entry shape is UNCHANGED everywhere: {..., sig, sigRedacted, pubKey: <full JWK|null>}. Zero changes to verifyPayload, commitSignedEntry, squashHistory, deriveIssueValues, TOFU trust, or any of the ~50 call sites that read .pubKey today.
- buildSourceText (write): before serializing, dedupes every entry's pubKey (across projectHistory + every issue's history + every issue's commentStreams) into one per-project `keys` registry on the `fields` line, keyed by a short sequential id ("k0", "k1", ...) assigned in first-seen order. Dedup key is the JWK's own (x, y) curve coordinates (the actual key material), not JSON.stringify equality. Each entry that had a real pubKey gets `keyRef: "k0"` instead, with `pubKey` dropped from the serialized line. Entries with pubKey: null (unsigned, or legacy-backfill) are untouched.
- parseJsonl (read): reads the `fields` line's `keys` map (if present) and rehydrates any entry carrying `keyRef` back to a full inline `pubKey` immediately after parsing, before hydrateIssue/backfill or anything else touches it. An old file with no `keys` map and inline `pubKey` per entry parses exactly as it does today (rehydrate is a no-op) -- full backward compat, no formatVersion bump needed since no code needs to branch on a version number, only on whether keyRef is structurally present.
- Uses a synchronous (x,y)-based key identity rather than the existing async fingerprintPublicKey (crypto.subtle.digest) -- buildSourceText is called synchronously from many render-path call sites (size label, GitHub-push diff check, clipboard/share) and can't become async without much wider disruption. This keyRef is purely an internal storage/dedup detail, never shown to the user -- the user-facing TOFU fingerprint (fingerprintPublicKey, SHA-256-based) is untouched and stays exactly as-is.

Verification plan: node --check the isolated JS + round-trip splice for wigwag.html, wigwag-core.test.js unit tests (new coverage for buildSourceText/parseJsonl round-trip with real dedup + old-format backward-compat), full merge-provenance.spec.js (touches signing/export), then the broader regression suite before calling this done.

Done. Implemented the per-identity key registry exactly per the design sketch above.

WHAT SHIPPED:
- wigwag-core.js and wigwag.html's WigwagCore IIFE: buildSourceText now dedupes every signed entry's pubKey (across projectHistory + every issue's history + every commentStreams entry) into a `keys` map on the fields line, keyed by a short sequential id ("k0", "k1", ...) assigned in first-seen order. Dedup is on the JWK's own (x, y) curve coordinates, not JSON.stringify equality. Each entry that had a pubKey now carries `keyRef` instead; pubKey is dropped from the wire.
- parseJsonl rehydrates keyRef back to a full inline pubKey immediately on read, before anything else (verifyPayload, squashHistory, TOFU trust, display) touches it -- the in-memory shape is completely unchanged everywhere else in the app.
- Used a synchronous (x,y)-based identity, not the existing async fingerprintPublicKey -- buildSourceText is called synchronously from several render-path call sites (source-size label, GitHub-push diff check, clipboard/share) that can't become async. This keyRef is purely an internal storage detail, never shown to a user; the real TOFU fingerprint is untouched.
- Fully backward compatible: a file with no `keys` map and inline pubKey per entry (anything written before this) parses completely unchanged. No formatVersion bump -- nothing needs to branch on a version number, only on whether a given entry structurally carries keyRef.
- docs/FORMAT.md updated with a new "The keys registry" subsection under "Identity and signing."

SCOPE CORRECTION from my design-sketch comment above: this needed changes in exactly TWO files (wigwag-core.js + wigwag.html's IIFE), not five. Every ingestion path (paste, file import, GitHub pull, CLI merge) already funnels through the single parseJsonl, and every export/save/push path through the single buildSourceText, both already centralized in wigwag-core.js. wigwag-cli.js calls core.buildSourceText/core.parseJsonl directly with no format logic of its own. wigwag-client.js/wigwag-agent.js never touch the file format at all (they drive a real browser instance) -- zero changes needed there. schema/tracker.schema.json predates signing entirely per FORMAT.md's own disclaimer, so it wasn't touched either.

MEASURED: re-serialized wigwag's own live tracker.jsonl through the new buildSourceText -- 18.8% smaller (807,642 -> 656,105 bytes), with a clean round-trip (every issue's derived values identical before/after).

VERIFIED: 158/158 wigwag-core unit tests (2 new: dedup+round-trip, and old-format-with-no-registry backward compat), 27/27 merge-provenance.spec.js, and the full data-structures/github-sync/project-notes regression (97/97) -- one test broke and was fixed along the way: a test that downloads a real exported file and checks a tombstone's signature "cold" was reading `.pubKey` directly off the raw parsed JSON (bypassing parseJsonl's rehydration, by design -- the whole point of that test is verifying from nothing but the raw file). Updated its own verify helper to resolve keyRef via the file's own `keys` registry, the same way any real external consumer would.

BONUS CONFIRMATION: since wigwag-agent.js drives a real local wigwag.html instance and pushes for real, my own comments/status-updates on this and other issues during this work already pushed the live tracker.jsonl through the new format. Checked issue #1 (created months ago, untouched this session) after that push -- its entries already show keyRef with no inline pubKey at all, since a push re-serializes the whole file. No migration step needed; normal use already converted the live file.

history.value: GitHub sync should carry a real export envelope, not fall back to the generic "this browser" attribution

history.text:
Plan (Tom's own call: "the github sync should have an export envelope just the same").

Context: investigating #124's Merge History timeline for #132 surfaced that every GitHub-sync-sourced merge shows "this browser" as its attributed source in the Merge History list -- buildMergeHistoryViewModel falls back to that literal string whenever record.source (the export envelope) is absent, and GitHub sync currently never builds/attaches one -- it pushes/pulls the plain records body directly, unlike the "Save project file.../Copy to clipboard" -> "Apply update" flow, which already wraps an envelope via buildSignedExportText/classifyIngestProvenance.

All the underlying primitives already exist (buildExportEnvelope, parseExportEnvelope, verifyExportEnvelope, classifyIngestProvenance) -- this wires GitHub sync into the SAME existing machinery, not new crypto.

Push side (pushToGithub): build recordsBody via buildSourceText('full') exactly as today, then build a real envelope via buildExportEnvelope (same shape buildSignedExportText already uses: exportedBy = identityEmail, exportedAt = now, project/tracker from state), and push `JSON.stringify(envelope) + '\n' + recordsBody` as the actual file content instead of the bare recordsBody. Critically: _githubLastSyncedText (used by maybeScheduleGithubPush's debounce-skip check and pushToGithub's own conflict-retry guard) stays tracking the UNWRAPPED recordsBody, not the enveloped text -- otherwise every future edit-check would see a mismatch purely from the envelope's own exported_at timestamp changing, causing spurious pushes. parseJsonl already tolerates/ignores an envelope line on read (existing comment confirms this), so nothing downstream needs to change just to keep working.

Pull side (connectGithubRepo's initial pull, and pollGithubForRemoteChanges): call classifyIngestProvenance(result.text) (already does parse+verify+TOFU-trust-recording, already used by the paste/file import flows) right alongside the existing parseJsonl(result.text) call, build the same inboundInfo shape those flows already build ({exportedBy, exportedAt, provenance, fingerprint, envelope}), and pass it into startMerge(parsed, inboundInfo) instead of the current bare startMerge(parsed) call. This does NOT change GitHub sync's "applies immediately, no gate" behavior at all (that's startMerge vs previewMerge, unaffected) -- it only enriches what gets recorded in the merge log, so Merge History can show a real signer instead of "this browser".

Scope: wigwag.html + wigwag-core.js's WigwagCore IIFE only (the Component methods pushToGithub/connectGithubRepo/pollGithubForRemoteChanges live only in the app source, not wigwag-core.js proper, but the pure functions they call are the dual-copy ones). NOT touching wigwag-cli.js's own separate push/pull path in this pass -- that's the CLI's own direct git-checkout flow, a different mechanism; flagging as a possible follow-up rather than bundling it in, to keep this change reviewable.

Expected side effect once live: with multiple real signing keys already active on this tracker (tom@lant.uk has 4, per earlier size analysis -- device/session key rotation), a "changed key" TOFU classification will legitimately fire sometimes for ordinary GitHub-sync merges. That's expected, non-blocking (per the existing TOFU design: never gates the merge), not a bug.

Verification: extend tests/github-sync.spec.js with real coverage for envelope-presence-on-push and correct-attribution-on-pull, re-run existing merge-provenance.spec.js + github-sync.spec.js in full, plus the broader regression suite given this touches the live sync engine.

Done. GitHub sync now carries a real signed export envelope, same one "Save project file..."/"Copy to clipboard" already build -- reusing the existing buildExportEnvelope/classifyIngestProvenance machinery, no new crypto.

WHAT CHANGED (wigwag.html's Component methods only -- these live in app source, not wigwag-core.js/the WigwagCore IIFE, since they're GitHub-fetch/state orchestration, not pure functions):
- pushToGithub: builds the records body exactly as before, then wraps it with a real envelope (exported_by = the pushing identity's email, exported_at = now, content_sha256 over the records body, signed if the identity has a signing key) before pushing. _githubLastSyncedText deliberately keeps tracking the UNWRAPPED records body, not the enveloped text -- otherwise every future edit-check (maybeScheduleGithubPush's debounce-skip, and this method's own conflict-retry guard) would see a spurious mismatch purely from the envelope's own timestamp changing on every push, even with zero real content changes.
- connectGithubRepo's pull and pollGithubForRemoteChanges: both now call classifyIngestProvenance(result.text) alongside the existing parseJsonl(result.text) call -- exactly what the paste/file "Apply update" flow already does -- and pass the resulting {exportedBy, exportedAt, provenance, fingerprint, envelope} into startMerge as inboundInfo, instead of the bare startMerge(parsed) that discarded any provenance. Doesn't touch startMerge's own "applies immediately, no gate" behavior at all -- background sync stays fully automatic; this only enriches what gets recorded in the local-only merge log, so Merge History can attribute correctly instead of falling back to "this browser".

Fixes the bug found while investigating #124/#132's Merge History: every GitHub-sync-sourced merge previously had no exported_by at all (GitHub sync never built/attached an envelope, unlike the file/paste flow), so the UI's own fallback ('this browser') fired for every single one, even a merge that genuinely came from a named collaborator's own push.

Scope note: deliberately NOT touching wigwag-cli.js's own separate push/pull path in this pass -- that's a different mechanism (direct git checkout, not the browser's fetch-based sync), flagged as a possible follow-up rather than bundled in here.

Added 2 new tests to tests/github-sync.spec.js: one confirms a push's actual bytes start with a real `wigwag.export` envelope naming the right identity; the other mocks an incoming remote file that itself carries a real envelope from a different sender and confirms the resulting merge-log record attributes to that real sender, not "this browser".

Verified: 21/21 github-sync.spec.js (incl. the 2 new tests), 27/27 merge-provenance.spec.js, 105/105 combined merge-provenance + data-structures + project-notes regression. No wigwag-core.js changes were needed (only app-source Component methods), so no unit-test changes either.

Expected, non-bug side effect once live: this tracker already has multiple real signing keys under the same email (device/session key rotation) -- a "changed key" TOFU classification will legitimately fire sometimes for ordinary GitHub-sync merges going forward. That's the existing, non-blocking TOFU design working as intended, not a regression.

history.value: wigwag-client.js's waitForPush used timing guesses, silently losing edits when the debounced push took longer

history.text:
Found and fixed live, 2026-09-22, while confirming #133's own Status field had actually landed (it hadn't -- see below).

BUG: wigwag-client.js's waitForPush() used a blind fixed page.waitForTimeout(5500) (the real ~4s debounce plus a margin) after every write (addIssue/comment/setField), then just read whatever the footer happened to show and returned it as "syncStatus" -- never actually confirming THIS edit's own push had completed. wigwag-agent.js's CLI then printed that as if it were a real success confirmation.

Confirmed two real, silent losses from this on issue #133 (0b22b69e) itself: both a "Status -> In Progress" and (initially) a "Status -> Done" set-field call printed a normal-looking "Sync status: ... just now" line, but neither ever reached GitHub -- the debounced push simply hadn't finished executing by the time the fixed sleep elapsed and the CLI process's browser was torn down (client.close()) mid-push. Root cause is almost certainly #133's own fix (0b22b69e): GitHub sync's pull path now also verifies an incoming envelope (SHA-256 hash + ECDSA verify), adding real crypto latency to the sync pipeline that the old fixed window didn't budget for.

FIRST FIX ATTEMPT (also caught failing live): replaced the fixed sleep with "wait 4.5s, then poll the footer's own spinner until it clears." This ALSO lost an edit (a throwaway diagnostic add-issue call) -- root cause: this tracker's own background polling can independently touch state and reset the debounce timer while the CLI is waiting, so "spinner not visible" after a fixed wait is genuinely ambiguous between "already finished" and "hasn't started yet." The first fix could observe the latter and wrongly report success.

REAL FIX: wait for the spinner to actually APPEAR first (proving a real sync attempt has started), THEN wait for it to clear -- never inferring "done" from a spinner state we simply haven't observed yet. Stress-tested with 4 back-to-back addIssue calls in one session; all 4 independently confirmed present via a completely separate wigwag-cli.js pull afterward.

PROCESS NOTE / apology: while diagnosing this, created 5 throwaway test issues (#134-#138) directly in the live tracker instead of using the designated safe test issue 61822bcb per CLAUDE.md's own standing instruction. There's no delete-issue capability in any of wigwag-agent.js/wigwag-client.js/wigwag-cli.js, so marked all 5 Won't Do with an explanatory comment rather than leaving them ambiguous -- Tom, feel free to delete them manually if they're cluttering the list.

No wigwag.html/wigwag-core.js changes -- this is purely a wigwag-client.js reliability fix (the tool that drives a real browser instance for wigwag-agent.js). No new automated test coverage added (this is Playwright-driving-Playwright infrastructure, not app behavior) -- verified via live stress-testing instead, as described above.
