Scope, per new_bits.zip's README (parent: 57a27222) -- the newest/most complex of the three parts:

- Entry points: Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on Mac) from anywhere, including mid-typing in a field; a magnifying-glass icon button in the top app bar (28x28, matches the light/dark toggle exactly), tooltip "Search all projects (Ctrl+K)". Opening it closes the project switcher and the Send menu.
- Removed: the project switcher's own "Search projects" box, AND the table filter box's existing id-jump behavior (matchingIssuesByIdPrefix + its jump panel) -- the filter box becomes keyword-only, placeholder "Filter this project". The prototype disables rather than removes this code; remove it for real when building.
- Panel: 600px wide (max 92vw), 12vh from top, radius 12. Input row: search icon + 15px autofocused input (placeholder "Search all projects by #id or title") + an esc keycap. Results max-height 380, scrollable, each row: a 72px monospace #+8-char-id-prefix (matched chars highlighted), the title (matched chars highlighted, same treatment as the table filter; project-name rows shown bold), the project name on the right (or "Project" for a project-level row), and an visibility-toggled up-down keycap on the active row only. Active row gets a --c25 fill; hover makes a row active. Footer strip: "up-down move . enter open" left, "Searching N projects in this browser" right. Two empty states (no query / no hits) per the README's exact copy.
- Matching: index built ONCE per open (current project from live state, others from their own localStorage docs, titles via deriveIssueValues) -- NOT rebuilt per keystroke. Id match: >=2 hex/dash chars, optional leading #, PREFIX match on issue/project ids, score 0. Title match: >=2 chars, not starting with #, case-insensitive substring, issue titles score 1, project names score 2. Sort by score, current project first within a tie, capped at 30 results.
- Opening a result: blur the input first (so a subsequent Esc reaches the slide-over, not this panel); an issue in the CURRENT project calls openSlideOver(id) directly; anything in another project pushes #/project/<id>[/issue/<id>] and calls resolveDeepLinkFromHash(false), reusing the existing deep-link path so identity-switching comes for free. Esc closes the panel -- first in the global Escape chain, and the input itself stopPropagations it too.
- Explicitly NOT done in the prototype: no mobile entry point for this at all (out of scope for this pass, matching the prototype).

This is the piece most likely to have real design-fidelity gaps if built from the README alone -- will render the live mockup and drive it interactively (matching, results, keyboard nav, cross-project opening) before writing any implementation, per the standing lesson from the merge_provenance handoff.

Implemented per the handoff (new_bits.zip, Part C):

- Top bar: a magnifying-glass button (btn-global-search, 28x28, matches the light/dark toggle's own styling exactly, placed just to its left), title "Search all projects (Ctrl K / ⌘K)" depending on platform.
- Ctrl+K / Cmd+K opens/closes it from anywhere -- no typingTarget guard, so it works even mid-typing in the filter box or any other field. It's the first check in _onGlobalKeyDown, ahead of the Escape chain; globalSearchOpen is also the first check inside that chain, so Escape closes the panel before anything else gets a shot at the keypress. Opening it also closes the project switcher and Send menu.
- Index built once per open (buildGlobalSearchIndex), not per keystroke: current project from live state, every other project from its own localStorage doc (same docKey helper the rest of the app already uses for cross-project reads), titles via deriveIssueValues.
- Matching (globalSearchMatches): id match needs >=2 hex/dash chars (optional leading #), prefix-only, score 0; title match needs >=2 chars and no leading #, case-insensitive substring, issues score 1, project names score 2. Sorted by score, current project first on a tie, capped at 30.
- Panel: 600px (max 92vw), 12vh from top. Each result row: monospace 8-char id prefix + title (both highlighted via the existing splitHighlightSegments -- same mechanism the table filter already uses, no new highlighting code needed), project name on the right (or "Project" for a project-level row), an enter keycap on the active row only. Arrow keys move the active row, Enter opens it, hover also makes a row active. Two empty states (no query typed / query matches nothing) per the handoff's copy.
- Opening a result: blurs focus first (so a follow-up Escape reaches the slide-over, not a stale panel), an issue in the CURRENT project opens its slide-over directly; anything in another project pushes #/project/<id>[/issue/<id>] and calls the existing resolveDeepLinkFromHash -- identity-switching and everything else that path already handles comes for free, no new logic needed.

Removed, per the handoff's own "prototype disables rather than removes this code; remove it for real when building":
- The desktop filter box's #id jump-mode behavior entirely (the icon swap, the jump-panel dropdown, the jumping branch of onFilterKeyDown, the aria-expanded/jump-related view-model fields). Placeholder is now "Filter this project" -- keyword/field-token only. Mobile's own separate id-jump implementation (mobile-jump-row, its own state/handlers) is untouched; it shares some underlying computation (matchingIssuesByIdPrefix, the jumpMode-gated suppression of keyword-filtering the shared issues list) which I left alone rather than forking, since that's what the mockup's own real implementation did too and mobile's behavior needed to stay byte-identical.
- The project switcher's own "Search projects" box (switcher-search-input, switcherSearchQuery state, and the query-based filtering of the projects list) -- confirmed via a LIVE RENDER of the mockup (a static grep hit an older, superseded turn still sitting in the same canvas file) that the real spec shows no search box there at all; the switcher's project list is unfiltered now.

Design-fidelity note (recurring pattern this session): ported the mockup's Component methods essentially verbatim (buildGlobalSearchIndex/globalSearchMatches/openGlobalSearch/closeGlobalSearch/openGlobalSearchResult/onGlobalSearchKeyDown/globalSearchVals -- all already correct and dependency-free), but the mockup's own onFilterKeyDown and desktop id-jump markup predate this codebase's later field:value autocomplete work (tracker #113) -- had to surgically remove only the jump branch and keep the filterSuggest logic it sits alongside, not port the mockup's simpler version wholesale.

Verified live via Playwright (button + Ctrl+K entry points, empty states, title/id matching, arrow-key nav, hover, click-to-open, cross-project open via deep link, project-level results, desktop id-jump fully gone, switcher search box fully gone) before writing durable tests. Added tests/global-search.spec.js (19 tests, all passing) and trimmed tests/id-jump.spec.js down to its still-live "click-to-copy" coverage (its old desktop jump-mode describe blocks tested behavior that no longer exists). Updated two tests elsewhere that asserted the old "Filter by keyword or field" placeholder or the old jump/filter-suggest precedence (tests/filter-autocomplete.spec.js). wigwag-core.test.js unchanged (159/159) -- this feature touched no wigwag-core.js pure functions, only Component state/methods/markup.

Live report after shipping: typing in the search box felt sluggish, keypresses not registering immediately.

Reproduced with a synthetic 800-issue project and confirmed it's NOT search-specific: the pre-existing desktop filter box shows the identical ~500ms-5s per-keystroke main-thread block. Root cause is this app's one monolithic renderVals() rebuilding the entire table's view-model on every setState, regardless of what changed. Filed that as its own issue (#146, 70a52f00) rather than trying to fix it here.

For the search box itself, two real fixes landed:
1. Debounce the setState onChange triggers (150ms trailing), so a burst of typing pays for one expensive render at the end instead of one per keystroke. Enter reads a live-tracked pending value (_gsPendingQuery), not the possibly-stale committed state, so hitting Enter immediately after typing still opens the right result.
2. A second, worse bug debouncing alone exposed: this framework's controlled-input binding re-asserts the bound value right after invoking the on-change handler -- so even with setState deferred, an eventual render's value= write could race in-flight native keystrokes and silently drop/reorder characters (verified live: typing "synthetic" landed as "ic"). Fixed by making the input genuinely uncontrolled (dropped the value="{{ }}" binding) -- confirmed safe because the panel's whole DOM subtree unmounts/remounts fresh (via sc-if) every time it opens, so there's no stale-text-on-reopen risk needing a reset.

Verified with an 800-issue synthetic project: per-keystroke latency dropped from 500ms-5s+ to ~30-130ms, and the character-loss bug is gone (confirmed via a property-setter instrumentation trace, not just eyeballing).

Also added, per direct request: a small clickable Ctrl/Cmd+K hint (global-search-hint) in the desktop filter box, shown when it's empty (swapped for the clear button once there's a query) -- more discoverable than the icon button's hover-only tooltip.

Added tests/global-search.spec.js's own describe block for this (rapid typing isn't dropped, setState is genuinely deferred, Enter-during-debounce opens the right thing) plus a hint test. Full regression suite: 824/825 (the one failure is the pre-existing, already-documented deep-links.spec.js Escape/history.back flake -- reproduced clean twice in isolation, unrelated). wigwag-core.test.js: 159/159 unchanged.

Whoops -- I'd put the Ctrl/Cmd+K hint in the wrong box (the per-project keyword filter, unrelated to global search). Moved it to where it belongs: inside the global search panel itself, next to the existing 'esc' keycap (data-testid=global-search-shortcut-hint). Reverted the filter box back to exactly how it was. Updated tests/global-search.spec.js accordingly; full file re-run 22/22, plus filter-autocomplete.spec.js and id-jump.spec.js unaffected (27/27), wigwag-core.test.js 159/159.

Removed the redundant 'esc' keycap next to the Ctrl/Cmd+K hint in the search panel -- Escape still closes it (onGlobalSearchKeyDown, unchanged), just no longer visually labeled since it was confusing alongside the new hint. tests/global-search.spec.js updated and re-run, 22/22.

history.value: The 'merge history' view still shows (I think) the same event on both sides of the merge (the first event), and still I see lots of "this browser" merges, suggesting that the sync to github is not happening within a signed envelope?

history.text:
Both of these were fixed and verified earlier tonight (the duplicate-entry timeline bug on #124/5c3051e9, comment ~11:15pm; the GitHub-sync envelope on #133/0b22b69e, comment ~9:33pm) -- but I think what you're seeing is stale, not unfixed. Here's my reasoning, and how to tell the difference for real:

1. Merge History records are LOCAL-ONLY (never synced to GitHub, per the local-only merge log design) -- once a merge-log entry is created, it's an immutable historical record. Fixing the code doesn't retroactively rewrite entries that were already recorded before the fix landed. If the merges you're looking at happened before ~9:30-11pm tonight, they'll still show the old (buggy) shape forever, even though new merges won't.

2. Your browser tab only re-executes wigwag.html's JS on an actual page load -- pulling fresh DATA via GitHub sync doesn't re-fetch or re-run the CODE. If this tab has been open continuously through tonight's session, it's very likely still running the pre-fix JavaScript regardless of how many commits have landed since, and would reproduce both symptoms exactly as before no matter what I fix.

Both explanations point at the same fix: a hard reload of this tab, THEN a genuinely NEW merge happening after that (e.g. wait for the next background poll, or trigger one), should show: (a) no duplicated entry in a fresh Level 3 timeline, (b) a real signer name (not "this browser") on a fresh Merge History record.

Could you reload and check against a merge that happens AFTER the reload, rather than an existing Merge History entry in the list? If it's still wrong on a genuinely fresh one, that's real and I'll dig in properly -- but I want to rule out stale tab/stale data first given how confident the automated verification was (a live-reproduced regression test for the duplicate-entry bug, and a live round-trip test confirming pushed files carry a real envelope and pulls attribute correctly, both still passing).

history.value: Explore embedding wigwag as a Matrix Element widget, with a standalone instance also backed by the widget API

history.text:
Tom's idea, raised live in chat: embed wigwag as a Matrix Element widget, and have the standalone (non-widget) instance ALSO use the same widget API to back its data, rather than just localStorage+GitHub -- so there's one storage model, not two.

Not scoped or started -- Tom is going to look for a Claude widget skill he built previously first. Flagging the main tradeoff up front for whenever this gets picked up: wigwag's current storage model is one coherent thing (localStorage for the working copy, a single append-only JSONL export for GitHub sync). The Matrix widget API's own storage primitives (room state events, account data) have real size and rate-limit constraints that don't naturally fit an arbitrarily-large, single-file, full-history export -- making the standalone instance ALSO run on the widget API means a genuine storage-abstraction layer (probably chunking/summarizing history into multiple state events, or a hybrid model), not a thin adapter over the existing format. Worth exploring, but it's an architecture decision, not a bolt-on feature.

Tom, live: 'it's crucial that we retain the ability to support both modes of operation.' So this isn't a migration to the widget API -- standalone (localStorage+GitHub) and widget-embedded both need to keep working, presumably via a storage abstraction with two real backends behind it, not one replacing the other. Noting this before any design work starts, since it rules out treating the widget API as the new source of truth.

Plan finalized (revised after real discussion, superseding my two earlier comments above). Full detail in my own plan doc; summary here:

KEY DECISION: wigwag.html gets ZERO code changes. This copies Nordeck NeoBoard's actual pattern (Tom's own reference) rather than my first instinct of baking Matrix support into wigwag.html directly.

The insight that makes this work: wigwag.html already has a cross-tab sync mechanism (_onStorageEvent) that watches localStorage[docKey(projectId)] and adopts any new value it sees, live, via the same hydrateProject/hydrateIssue derivation the rest of the app uses. It doesn't care WHO wrote that key. Since the native `storage` event fires across same-origin frames (not just tabs), a same-origin iframe container can talk to an unmodified wigwag.html purely by reading/writing that one localStorage key -- no new protocol needed on wigwag.html's side at all.

So: a new file, wigwag-matrix-host.html (sibling to wigwag.html, NOT part of the bundled-artifact workflow, free to have real dependencies since it inherently needs network access anyway):
- Detects mode: widgetId in location.search + window.parent !== window -> real Widget-API postMessage bridge (embedded in Element, via @matrix-widget-toolkit/api from a CDN import). Otherwise -> standalone, direct homeserver connection with a personal access token. Both expose the same tiny internal interface (observe room events / send a room event) -- this is the actual NeoBoard shape, botless either way, since ordinary room events need no elevated permissions.
- Bootstraps wigwag's expected localStorage shape (project index, the doc itself, active-project pointer, a signing identity) before iframing wigwag.html, same shapes tests/helpers.js's gotoTracker already seeds for tests.
- Iframes wigwag.html unmodified, same-origin.
- Bridges Matrix <-> localStorage[docKey(projectId)] in both directions.

Event shape: one type, dev.wigwag.entry (room/timeline events, not state events -- wigwag's own append-only history maps directly onto Matrix's timeline, no chunking scheme needed), content = {v, scope: issue|project, issueId, stream, entry} where entry is exactly docs/FORMAT.md's existing signed history-entry shape, minus keyRef (that dedup is a JSONL-file-size optimization that doesn't apply once every entry is its own event -- inline pubKey per event instead).

New wigwag-core.js additions (Phase 1, consumed by wigwag-matrix-host.html, NOT mirrored into wigwag.html's window.WigwagCore since wigwag.html never touches this): matrixEventContentFromEntry/entryFromMatrixEvent, hydrateProjectFromMatrixTimeline (the Matrix analog of parseJsonl), and direct Client-Server API fetch helpers shaped like the existing pullGithubFile/pushGithubFile/probeGithubRepoAccess. Also: num assignment under concurrent Matrix writers will be DERIVED (sort by earliest creation-entry sortKey) rather than client-assigned, since Matrix's timeline has no serialization point equivalent to GitHub's sha-conditional PUT. And a small, backward-compatible addition to wigwag-core.js's own export tail (a `typeof window !== 'undefined'` branch alongside the existing module.exports) so wigwag-matrix-host.html can <script src="wigwag-core.js"> it directly instead of needing a third hand-copied mirror.

Phases: 1) wigwag-core.js Matrix adapter + tests (extends the existing wigwag-core.test.js, 159 tests today). 2) wigwag-matrix-host.html standalone mode (direct homeserver transport + bootstrap + bridge) -- testable with a mocked homeserver, no real Matrix needed. 3) widget-embedded transport swapped in behind the same interface -- real Element verification has to be manual, being honest that a real postMessage handshake can't be meaningfully automated. 4) polish/parity (redaction-as-new-event not m.room.redaction, event-size guard, FORMAT.md doc). 5) optional: CLI-side store, deferred snapshot optimization.

Starting Phase 1 now.

Phase 1 done: added the Matrix adapter to wigwag-core.js (WIGWAG_MATRIX_ENTRY_TYPE/matrixEventContentFromEntry/entryFromMatrixEvent/hydrateProjectFromMatrixTimeline, plus resolveMatrixRoomAlias/fetchMatrixRoomEntries/sendMatrixEntry/probeMatrixRoomAccess), and the small backward-compatible window.WigwagCore export tail so wigwag-matrix-host.html can <script src> this file directly instead of needing a third hand-copied mirror. 9 new tests in wigwag-core.test.js (168/168 total, up from 159), covering the encode/decode round-trip, malformed/foreign-event tolerance, num derivation under out-of-order concurrent creation, field-def derivation from project-scope entries, and the fetch helpers against a fake fetchImpl. wigwag.html untouched -- confirmed via grep (zero Matrix-related strings) and confirmed wigwag-cli.js/wigwag-client.js/wigwag-agent.js still load fine with the new export tail in place.

Next: Phase 2 (wigwag-matrix-host.html itself -- bootstrap, the localStorage bridge, the direct-homeserver transport). This is the bigger, more novel half of the work -- checking in with Tom before starting it rather than plowing ahead.

Phase 2 done: wigwag-matrix-host.html (standalone, direct-homeserver transport). Setup form -> connect -> probe access -> pull the room's timeline -> bootstrap the exact localStorage shapes wigwag.html itself would create for a new project -> iframe wigwag.html unmodified -> bidirectional bridge (a poll picks up new remote events and merges them via computeIssueMerge/computeFieldDefsMerge, same algorithm the app's own GitHub sync uses; a storage-event listener catches wigwag.html's own local edits and sends new entries out).

wigwag.html: still zero changes, confirmed by grep.

Three real bugs found and fixed via live Playwright debugging, not guessed:
1. My own 'browser-loadable wigwag-core.js' fix from Phase 1 was itself broken -- module.exports={...} still executed unconditionally, throwing ReferenceError: module is not defined in a plain <script> tag. Fixed with a real local-const + conditional-assignment pattern.
2. My test mock's call-counter incremented on the PROBE request too (limit=0), throwing off the 'first real fetch vs subsequent' detection so the actual seeded history was never returned to the real fetch.
3. Every seeded identity had an empty email, and wigwag.html correctly refused to commit any signed entry until requireIdentityEmail's gate is satisfied (right behavior on wigwag's part, not a bug there) -- fixed by deriving the identity's attribution from a real GET /account/whoami call rather than leaving it blank.

Also caught and fixed, via a live reproduction, a genuine race: creating one issue writes to localStorage more than once in quick succession, each firing its own storage event -- two overlapping pushNewLocalEntries() calls could each compute their own 'what's new' list from the same stale snapshot and both send the identical entry. Fixed with a single-flight-plus-rerun guard; added a regression test asserting sent entry ids are always unique.

9 new Playwright tests in tests/matrix-host.spec.js (all against a mocked homeserver, tests/helpers.js's new mockMatrixClientApi, same page.route() pattern as the existing GitHub mocks) -- covering connect success/failure/alias-resolution/room-naming, existing-history-on-first-connect, local-edit-sends-to-room, remote-poll-merges-live, reconnect-resolves-same-project, and reconnect-does-not-clobber-a-not-yet-round-tripped local edit. wigwag-core.test.js unaffected, 168/168.

Next: Phase 3 (the real Widget-API postMessage transport, gated on widgetId, for actual Element embedding) -- real Element verification for that phase has to be manual per the plan, flagging that up front rather than promising automated coverage that can't exist.

Phase 3 done: the real Widget-API postMessage transport for actual Element embedding.

- wigwag-matrix-host.html now detects widgetId in location.search (+ window.parent !== window) and switches to a hand-rolled Widget API (MSC2762) client instead of the standalone form. Room/user/display-name context comes from the standard $matrix_room_id/$matrix_user_id/$matrix_display_name URL template variables Element (or any spec-following client) substitutes into the widget's URL before loading it -- no round-trip needed for that.
- Refactored connectMatrixRoom into a shared, transport-agnostic bridge (createMatrixBridge) plus two transports behind one interface: createDirectTransport (Phase 2's existing logic, unchanged behavior) and createWidgetTransport (new). All 9 existing Phase 2 tests pass unchanged against the refactor.
- Widget mode polls via read_events on the same 5s cadence the direct transport already polls on, rather than wiring up live pushed events -- keeps both transports' sync model identical for v1; live push is a plausible later refinement, not required.
- Deliberate implementation choice, flagged for visibility: hand-rolled the postMessage protocol directly rather than pulling in @matrix-widget-toolkit/api from a CDN as the original plan draft tentatively suggested. This sandbox can't verify a CDN library's correctness without a real Element session anyway, and hand-rolling both sides let me build a disposable fake-widget-host test page (tests/fixtures/fake-widget-host.html) that drives the real protocol handling end-to-end. Added 5 new tests in tests/matrix-host.spec.js against it (auto-connect with no setup form, missing $matrix_room_id surfaced as a clear error, existing history reflected on load, issue-creation round-tripped through send_event with the same dedup guard as the direct transport, and a live remote update picked up on poll). 14/14 total passing.
- This validates wigwag-matrix-host.html's OWN protocol handling, not real Element compatibility -- that still needs an actual manual smoke test (real Element dev build, a scratch room, the widget added by URL). Not attempted here, and I want to be upfront that it hasn't been.
- Plan doc updated to reflect the hand-rolled choice.

Next up per the plan: Phase 4 (redaction-as-new-event semantics, a size-ceiling guard for oversized entries, docs/FORMAT.md documentation of the dev.wigwag.entry event shape). Let me know if you'd like me to keep going or pause for you to try the standalone+widget modes for real first.

Phase 3 confirmed working live in real Element (not just the fake-widget-host test harness) as of today. Three real bugs surfaced only through live testing against Element, each fixed and now covered by a regression test in tests/matrix-host.spec.js:

1. Widget mode was hiding the #status container the instant it detected widget mode, before ever attempting to connect -- any error/status message was invisible, i.e. a white screen no matter what happened underneath.
2. read_events requests omitting room_ids hit a 'deprecated behaviour' fallback in Element's own ClientWidgetApi that throws internally before ever replying -- fixed by always passing room_ids explicitly.
3. The big one: answering Element's supported_api_versions handshake with an empty {} (treating it as an ignorable notification) makes Element's OWN code throw, since it unconditionally does response.supported_versions.includes(...) with no guard. That throw landed in the same dispatch path that delivers replies to the widget's own pending requests -- so every read_events call after the very first quietly got no reply at all, looking exactly like a hang. Fixed by replying with the real supported_versions list the matrix-widget-api library itself declares.

Also found and fixed along the way: a missing org.matrix.msc2762.timeline:<roomId> capability (a third, separate gate from the per-event-type receive/send capabilities), and a capability-approval race where the very first read can legitimately arrive before a human has clicked through Element's own approval dialog (now retried with backoff).

18 tests passing in tests/matrix-host.spec.js (up from 9 after Phase 2), covering both the standalone and widget-embedded transports. Tom has confirmed it working live in real Element. There are some UX questions still to work through (parked for now, not blocking). Phase 4 (redaction-as-new-event semantics, an entry-size guard, docs/FORMAT.md documentation) is still on deck whenever wanted.

history.value: We need to expose "Created" and "Updated" timestamp fields. I think they should be hidden by default, and should of course be derived from the existing state rather than any newly tracked data.

history.text:
Plan for exposing Created/Updated as real, hideable columns:

**Model**: a new field type, `timestamp`, and two reserved field ids, `created`/`updated` -- always present (auto-added to fieldDefs the same way the Comments field is: `ensureTimestampFieldDefs`, mirroring `ensureCommentsFieldDef`, called from `hydrateProject`). Values are NEVER written via history -- `deriveIssueValues` special-cases `type === 'timestamp'` and computes them directly: Created = earliest sortKey across the issue's own history, Updated = latest sortKey across history AND all comment streams (a new comment counts as an update). Stored as a raw ms-epoch number for precision (so "Updated 5m ago" is meaningful, not just "today").

**Hidden by default**: the first time these fields get introduced to a project (fieldDefs lacked them before hydrating), they're added to hiddenFieldIds automatically. Once a project has them (new or migrated), un-hiding is a normal, sticky choice like any other column -- this only fires once, on first introduction.

**Rendering**: read-only always (no click-to-edit, unlike other field types which are only conditionally read-only) -- relative-age text ("3d ago"), full date/time on hover. Reuses the existing date-range filter UI (presets + from/to) since these behave like a `date` field for filtering purposes, just with a ms-epoch value under the hood instead of a YYYY-MM-DD string.

**Deliberately not touching**: the "Add field" type picker (a hardcoded <option> list in the markup -- timestamp just isn't one of the choices, so it's already impossible to create one by hand) and the field editor (falls through to label-only editing, same as any other non-select/multiselect/text/issue type already does -- no special-casing needed). Bulk "Set field" gets an explicit exclusion (same as Comments already has) since setting these would be a silent no-op otherwise. Field deletion gets no special protection -- like Comments, it'll just reappear on next hydrate, which is consistent with how the one other 'always-present, code-managed' field already behaves.

**Not in scope for this pass** (flagging so it's a deliberate cut, not an oversight): CSV/XLSX export and copy-as-markdown will get *some* sensible formatting, but I'm not building anything bespoke beyond what falls out naturally from the existing per-type export code paths.

Implementing now via the usual extract/patch/reencode/verify workflow, wigwag-core.js + the embedded WigwagCore mirror kept in sync, new Playwright coverage, docs/FORMAT.md updated.

Done. Summary:

**Implemented**: two new reserved fields, `created`/`updated` (type: `timestamp`), always present (auto-added on hydrate, same mechanism as the Comments field), hidden by default on first introduction to a project. Values are never written via history -- always derived fresh from the issue's own activity (earliest/latest sortKey across history AND all comment streams, so a new comment counts as an update). Read-only everywhere, unconditionally -- no click-to-edit affordance exists for this type at all. Reuses the existing date-range filter UI. Excluded from bulk 'Set field' and the 'Add field' type picker. CSV/XLSX export get sensible formatting (ISO string / a real Excel date-time cell).

**Verification**: 7 new wigwag-core.js unit tests (175 total passing), 5 new Playwright tests in tests/timestamp-fields.spec.js, plus a full 853-test regression pass that surfaced 4 fallout failures -- all now fixed:
- 3 were stale test expectations (hardcoded field-count/field-list assertions that needed updating for the new, correct behavior).
- 1 was a real, pre-existing UI bug the feature exposed: the 'Add field' popover's flip-upward positioning logic never actually checked whether the popover fit in the direction it flipped to -- it could previously get lucky, but enough hidden-field rows (mine pushed it over) made it clip above the viewport. Fixed at the root with an actual max-height clamp based on real available space, plus a scroll cap on the hidden-fields list itself, so this can't recur regardless of how many fields a project ends up hiding.

Final collateral check: interaction.spec.js + data-structures.spec.js + filter-autocomplete.spec.js together, 275/275 passing.

docs/FORMAT.md updated with a full section on the new field type.

Two permanent storage models: Room Scoped Widget Mode vs User Scoped Local Mode

Named 2026-09-25, in reaction to a live cross-room data leak in the Matrix widget (tracker #149, 29e719c1): wigwag will permanently support two distinct storage/operation models, not one model with edge cases.

**Room Scoped Widget Mode** (the Matrix widget, wigwag-matrix-host.html):
- Data persisted to the room's own Matrix timeline -- the room is the durable state.
- Supports multiple projects, but only ONE project context (the room itself) -- everyone who can see the widget in that room sees the same state.
- Any project newly shared into this mode falls into the room context immediately -- no "Shared with you" limbo, that concept doesn't exist here.
- Two open concerns: (1) Matrix rate limits -- mitigated via batched sends + retry-with-backoff (sendMatrixEntry/sendMatrixEntries); (2) underlying data visibility/decryptability -- wigwag's own data should carry the SAME protection as the room itself (e.g. E2EE rooms). Nordeck's NeoBoard (github.com/nordeck/matrix-neoboard) is a useful reference here: durable board state lives in room events/state, only ephemeral live signals (cursor, presence) go over WebRTC/MatrixRTC -- nothing durable in browser storage.

**User Scoped Local Mode** (Tauri client, or any locally-served/opened wigwag.html):
- Data persisted to browser local storage (today's existing model, unchanged).
- Supports multiple project contexts (= wigwag's existing multi-identity system), multiple projects per context.
- A project newly shared into this mode lands in "Shared with you" until explicitly attributed to a real identity -- existing requireAttribution behavior, untouched.

**Interop**: data exported from either mode looks the same (today's JSONL/export-envelope format, unchanged), and is importable into the other mode.

**Immediate application**: the live cross-room leak that prompted naming this is being fixed as "implement Room Scoped Widget Mode's isolation boundary" -- a widget instance's local storage cache becomes a disposable, per-room-namespaced projection of the room's own state (a wigwag.html-level storageNamespace param, prefixing its own STORAGE_KEY/PROJECTS_KEY/etc.), never the thing an edit's durability actually depends on.

**Explicitly NOT in scope for that fix**: making local storage a *pure* rebuildable cache where a write isn't "done" until the room confirms it (today, a local write is the first durable record; the room push happens after, eventually). That's a real, larger change to wigwag.html's own persistence layer -- deserves its own design pass as a follow-up initiative, not bolted onto the namespace fix.

Implemented the storage-namespace mechanism this establishes for Room Scoped Widget Mode's isolation boundary, in reaction to a live-reported cross-room leak (a project adopted while connected to one room was showing up in a completely different room's switcher, sharing the same browser).

wigwag-core.js/wigwag.html: an optional ?storageNamespace=<id> URL param prefixes every exported storage-key constant (STORAGE_KEY, PROJECTS_KEY, IDENTITIES_KEY, etc.) with <id>:, computed once at script load. Fully generic, not Matrix-specific -- wigwag.html has zero awareness anything is different. Defaults to no prefix (byte-identical keys) for every deployment that never passes it: Node tooling, tests, Tauri, plain browser.

wigwag-matrix-host.html: sets this per-room via deriveProjectId(roomId) (the same stable hash already used for the room's legacy default project id) as early as createMatrixBridge is constructed, applies it to its own reads/writes via a small nsKey() wrapper (since the host's own page URL never carries the param -- the room isn't known until connect() runs), and passes the identical value to the iframe via ?storageNamespace=. Host and iframe now structurally cannot see each other's -- or another room's -- data; verified directly with a test connecting to two different rooms in the same browser and confirming zero leakage either into the room's own Matrix timeline or the local switcher.

The earlier projectId->roomId registry (adoptLocalProjects's own bookkeeping) is now redundant for the leak it was built for -- different rooms use genuinely different PROJECTS_KEY/docKey values, so there's nothing to leak into in the first place -- kept as defense in depth rather than load-bearing.

Documented in docs/FORMAT.md's "Matrix room backing" section. All matrix-host.spec.js tests (34) and the full wigwag-core.js unit suite (201) pass; full Playwright regression suite running now to confirm zero impact on normal (non-widget) usage.

Still not attempted (explicitly out of scope for this fix, per the two-mode framework above): making local storage a *pure* rebuildable cache where a write isn't "done" until the room confirms it. That's a real, larger change to wigwag.html's own persistence layer -- a genuine future initiative, not bolted onto this.

Correction/sharpening from Tom, direct quote: "The objective of room scoped widget mode is that all the data lives securely managed under the same conditions as in the room. Decrypting and storing in local browser storage managed by the wigwag client is a fail."

This means the storage-namespace fix (per-room-prefixed localStorage keys, landed this session) does NOT implement Room Scoped Widget Mode's actual guarantee -- it only stops two different rooms' plaintext from colliding in the same bucket. Decrypted room content is still being persisted indefinitely in a store wigwag itself controls, outside Matrix's own protection lifecycle (room leave, key rotation, redaction don't touch it). Namespacing is a real, correct fix for a DIFFERENT bug (cross-room contamination) -- it should not be described as progress toward this mode's core security guarantee.

A genuine implementation needs one of: (a) no persistent local cache at all -- rehydrate into memory from the room each session, discard on close; (b) a local cache encrypted with room-derived key material so it decays with the room's own lifecycle; (c) persist only non-content metadata locally (which projects/rooms exist) and always read actual issue content live from the room. This is a real wigwag-matrix-host.html/wigwag.html persistence-layer redesign, out of scope for anything shipped so far -- needs its own design pass before implementation.

Plan approved for the real fix (not just namespacing): a StorageBackend interface inside wigwag.html's app-source, with two implementations behind one UX layer.

- LocalStorageBackend: today's persist()/persistProjectIndex()/persistIdentities()/adoptExternalIssues()/the three-key storage-event listener, moved verbatim behind the interface. No behavior change, no format change -- this is what boots by default (Tauri, plain browser), so daily use stays untouched.
- RpcStorageBackend: wigwag.html forwards readDoc/writeDoc/readProjectIndex/etc. over postMessage to whatever parent frame answers a wigwag:hello handshake. wigwag.html itself stays Matrix-agnostic -- it only knows 'a parent will service these calls'.
- wigwag-matrix-host.html becomes the RPC host instead of a DOM/localStorage poker: same Matrix logic already built this session (discovery, batching, retry, adoptLocalProjects), but now answering RPC calls and holding all doc/project-index state in memory only -- never localStorage.setItem for content. Deletes the now-superseded storageNamespacePrefix/nsKey/hideIdentityChrome-CSS-injection/MATRIX_BRIDGED_ROOMS_KEY mechanisms entirely, since content never touches the iframe's localStorage in the first place.
- render()'s identity-switcher/project-picker logic keys off real capability flags (multiIdentity, sharedProjectContext) from the active backend, replacing the external CSS-injection hack with one real code path.
- New security-regression test: after a full edit session as a widget, assert the iframe's own localStorage has zero project/doc/identity content.

Starting implementation now.

Correction to the NeoBoard comparison, checked against the actual repo (docs/ADRs), not recollection:

NeoBoard does NOT keep 'nothing durable locally' -- ADR007 explicitly caches whiteboard CRDT documents in IndexedDB (offline editing, surviving an unannounced iframe close, performance), with zero discussion of the security implications of that local cache. So 'all your data is in the room, nothing local' is a stricter bar than NeoBoard's own real architecture -- still holding wigwag to that bar per Tom's stated objective, just noting NeoBoard can't be cited as proof it's already solved elsewhere.

Also surfaced a real, separate problem while checking this: NeoBoard's docs don't address what happens when a new member joins an E2EE room and lacks keys for older events (confirmed absent from ADR005/SECURITY.md). General Matrix mechanics: session keys aren't retroactively shared with later joiners, regardless of history_visibility. NeoBoard's structural mitigation is a full-snapshot model (not deltas) -- a new member only needs the latest snapshot's session key. wigwag's append-only, never-compacted signed history is the opposite shape -- hydrateIssue/deriveFieldDefs need the entire entry history, so per-entry E2EE would leave a new joiner looking at a badly broken partial project. Filing this as its own issue rather than folding it into the current storage-shim work, since it's a separate, real design question (including snapshot size/chunking/rate-limiting, since a full-doc snapshot for an actively-used project could be large and Matrix caps a single event at 65536 bytes).

For the widget transport, raised the per-request limit substantially as a mitigation, but could NOT safely add a real exhaustion loop -- this codebase already confirmed live that MSC2762/2876's continuation token isn't guaranteed to terminate, so looping on it risks a worse bug than the one being fixed. Only a full reconnect (which re-discovers from scratch) would show it -- directly violating 'everyone who can see the widget in the room sees the same state'. Plan for the rate-limit incident's real fix, worked through live with Tom (thanks for the sharp questions on edge cases):

1. Encrypted media-blob snapshots, replacing event-chunking. A snapshot becomes one client-side-encrypted blob (POST /_matrix/media/v3/upload) referenced by a single small manifest event, instead of dozens of dev.wigwag.snapshot.chunk events -- cuts a 1500-entry import from ~61 room-event sends to ~2, avoiding the per-room event-send rate limiter almost entirely, and eliminates the 'partially-delivered chunk set' failure mode outright (nothing left that can be half-sent). Widget transport uses MSC4039 (upload_file/download_file/get_media_config); direct transport hits the media API directly.

2. Project creation becomes a moderator-gated Matrix state event (dev.wigwag.project, state_key: projectId) rather than an unconditional local-then-bridged action -- Tom's explicit call, leaning on Matrix's own power-level model (state_default, typically 50) as a real safety control, not just a discoverability optimization. Room Scoped Widget Mode gains a genuine 'no projects yet' empty state instead of always synthesizing a default project. Existing rooms/projects are grandfathered in (evidenced by real timeline entries, no retroactive gate) -- only new projects go through it. A rejected creation must surface a clear error, never silently orphan local state.

3. Snapshot cadence gets a time-based floor alongside the existing 200-entry threshold, so a quiet, rarely-edited project still gets re-snapshotted periodically.

Three independently-verified slices (state-event project index -> media-blob snapshots -> cadence). Full plan with file/line references written to my own planning notes; starting Slice 1 now.

history.value: Room Scoped Widget Mode + E2EE: new-member decryption gap and snapshot size/rate-limiting

history.text:
Follow-on from f6b39bf0 (Room Scoped Widget Mode / User Scoped Local Mode). Surfaced while checking NeoBoard (github.com/nordeck/matrix-neoboard) as a reference architecture for the storage-shim work in progress there.

**The gap**: NeoBoard's own docs (ADR005, SECURITY.md) don't address what happens when a member joins an E2EE room and lacks decryption keys for older events -- confirmed absent, not inferred. General Matrix/Megolm mechanics: a Megolm session key is shared (via to-device messages) with whoever is a room member when that session starts. It is NOT retroactively shared with later joiners. m.room.history_visibility only controls whether the homeserver hands over the old ciphertext at all (joined/invited/shared/world_readable) -- even at its most permissive, that's just access to encrypted bytes, not the ability to decrypt them. So a new member generally cannot decrypt history from before they joined.

NeoBoard's structural mitigation: it stores a FULL SNAPSHOT model, not deltas -- net.nordeck.whiteboard.document.snapshot/.chunk room events (chunked, reassembled by sequenceNumber, see docs/model/matrix-events.md). A new member only ever needs the latest snapshot's session key, not the whole history -- any snapshot sent after they joined is automatically readable by them.

**Why this bites wigwag specifically**: wigwag's data model is the opposite shape -- append-only signed history, nothing ever pruned or compacted (deletions are tombstones, not removals). hydrateIssue/deriveFieldDefs need the ENTIRE entry history to derive current state. If per-entry timeline events were E2EE-encrypted the way NeoBoard's chunk events are, a new member joining an established room could be structurally unable to decrypt most of a project's history -- a badly broken partial project, not a graceful degradation.

**Snapshot size, Tom's specific worry**: Matrix caps a single event's content at 65536 bytes -- any full-doc snapshot bigger than that needs chunking, same as NeoBoard (whose own docs note 'the amount of messages is larger than many servers allow', serious enough to warrant a dedicated rate-limiting config doc). wigwag's append-only, never-compacted history for an actively-used project can plausibly grow to hundreds of KB or more over time -- one entry per field edit/comment/rename, forever kept. A naive 'resend the whole doc as a snapshot on every save' policy would mean chunking into many events, repeatedly, at the same volume that already triggered real rate-limiting once this session (the bulk-import batching work).

**One promising angle, not yet evaluated**: wigwag already has squashHistory/buildSourceText('squashed', ...) in wigwag-core.js (used today for plain-text export) -- collapses history to current derived values instead of every entry, plausibly much smaller for a mature project. Trade-off not yet checked: squashing likely drops per-entry signed provenance, which the room's own audit/merge model may depend on.

Not solved here -- needs its own design pass, separate from the storage-shim work on f6b39bf0 (that work is orthogonal: it stops decrypted content sitting in local storage regardless of whether entries are ever E2EE-encrypted at all).

Tom's own live-testing insight, worth recording here directly: you don't need a stranger joining an E2EE room to make full-history-replay hurt -- ordinary room growth does it too, no encryption involved at all.

Hit live today: after a bulk import, connecting/reconnecting only pulled ONE page of the room's most-recent history before considering itself done (relying on a slow 5s poll to eventually catch up on the rest). Since a bulk import's entries ARE the most recent events, that first page was dominated by them -- meaning a second, older project (further back in the room's timeline) was invisible entirely, and even the new project's own name was missing (its __project_name__ entry hadn't been paginated in yet either). Fixed the immediate correctness bug (full post below), but the underlying shape of the problem is exactly this issue's own point: full-history replay on every connect doesn't scale, with or without E2EE in the picture. A real snapshot mechanism (NeoBoard-style) would mean a fresh connect just needs the latest snapshot, not the whole timeline -- solving the E2EE new-member gap AND this ordinary-growth performance/correctness problem at the same time, for the same reason.

Also worth noting for scoping that work later: the widget transport (MSC2876 read_events) can't reliably loop-to-exhaustion the way the direct/personal-token transport's standard Matrix /messages pagination can -- this codebase already confirmed live that its continuation token isn't guaranteed to terminate. That's an argument FOR a snapshot approach over 'just paginate harder' for the widget transport specifically, since reliable full-history pagination may not even be achievable there at all.

Built and tested end-to-end: the room snapshot mechanism this issue proposed (full writeup above), motivated by both the E2EE new-member gap this issue is about AND the ordinary-room-growth pagination/correctness bug found live today (posted on f6b39bf0/#153).

Two new event types (dev.wigwag.snapshot manifest + dev.wigwag.snapshot.chunk payload, chunked by entry count like the existing bulk-adopt batching, not raw bytes -- no NeoBoard-style byte-slicing needed since wigwag's entries are already well-formed JSON). NOT a squash to current values -- full signed provenance is kept always, matching 'history is the sole source of truth'. A snapshot is a genuine E2EE fix (not just a pagination one) because it's a NEW event, encrypted under whatever session is current when sent -- a member who joined after the original entries but before the snapshot still gets it.

Write side: always snapshots right after a bulk-adopt (closes the exact scenario that caused today's live bug), plus a 200-entries-since-last-snapshot threshold from the live poll. Read side: connect() reassembles the latest COMPLETE snapshot per project (an incomplete/torn one is discarded, falls back to full replay automatically), combines it with only the newer 'tail' entries, and feeds the result into the existing discoverProjects/hydrateProjectFromMatrixTimeline completely unchanged -- they can't tell a snapshot-sourced entry from a directly-pulled one.

Verified with 5 new tests: snapshot-only hydration (no individual entries needed at all), snapshot+tail combining correctly (no double-counting), incomplete-snapshot fallback, auto-write-on-bulk-adopt, and a full round trip (write, genuinely reconnect, read back correctly) -- plus 7 new wigwag-core.js unit tests for the encode/decode/reassembly functions themselves. Full project suite green.

Known, explicitly out-of-scope-for-now gaps: old/superseded snapshots are never cleaned up (room grows unboundedly over a long enough time -- not a correctness problem, worth its own follow-up); and the WIDGET transport (unlike the direct/personal-token one) can't safely skip fetching old pages once a snapshot is found, since MSC2876's read_events continuation token isn't reliably guaranteed to terminate -- confirmed live earlier today. Snapshot-aware hydration alone still delivers real value there (correct results, far less to process) even without that fetch-side optimization.

history.value: Pasting into the keyword filter box doesn't apply the filter

Not yet root-caused with a live repro, but a plausible lead from reading the markup/handlers: filter-input binds sc-camel-on-change (onFilterChange, reads e.target.value correctly) and sc-camel-on-key-down (onFilterKeyDown) separately. wigwag also has a separate hex-id-prefix 'jump' path (matchingIssuesByIdPrefix) that a pasted hex-looking string could trigger instead of/alongside the plain keyword filter -- if paste routes into that path without also engaging the keyword filter, the underlying table would stay unfiltered while some other UI (a jump panel) responds instead. Worth verifying with a live paste (not simulated typing) against a project with no matching id, watching which handler actually fires and whether filterQuery ever updates in state.

Root-caused and fixed, found while investigating the related #156: when a typed/pasted query happens to look like a real issue id prefix, jumpMode goes true and row-filtering was unconditionally skipped -- originally so a jump-to-issue popover could take over, but that popover was never actually wired up on desktop at all (confirmed independently via #156), so the result was exactly this: box shows the text, table keeps showing every row, totally silent.

Dropped the jumpMode guard on the actual row-filtering (kept jumpMode/jumpResults/mobile jump-row completely untouched -- see #156 for why that is its own, more involved decision, not folded into this fix). The id-jump popover (matchingIssuesByIdPrefix, triggered when the filter query looks like a hex id/prefix) predates global search and should be removed outright, not fixed.

Diagnosis while investigating a live 'jump popover doesn't appear' report: the id-jump feature is only half-implemented on desktop today. Its backing logic is fully built -- jumpMode/jumpResults computed every render from matchingIssuesByIdPrefix, jumpDismissed/jumpActiveIndex state, an outside-click handler referencing [data-testid="jump-panel"] -- but no markup with that testid exists anywhere, and jumpMode/jumpResults are never even passed into the desktop render bindings (only the mobile equivalent, mobile.jumpMode/mobile.jumpResults, is wired up and rendered as mobile-jump-row). So on desktop it's silently dead: a real match list gets computed every keystroke and goes nowhere. Mobile's version does work.

Scope for removal: matchingIssuesByIdPrefix and its wigwag-core.js/wigwag.html-IIFE dual copy, the jumpMode/jumpResults/jumpQueryStripped computation and jumpDismissed/jumpActiveIndex state (both scopes -- switchProject's reset block, componentDidMount's outside-click list, mobile filter open/close resets), the mobile-jump-row markup and mobile.jumpMode sc-if block, openJumpResult(), and the '#' prefix stripping/placeholder copy ('Filter or jump to #id') that assumes this feature exists. Check tests referencing any of jump-panel/mobile-jump-row/jumpMode/openJumpResult before removing -- some existing coverage will need deleting alongside the feature, not just left to rot as dead assertions.

Picked this up overnight while fixing #155 (which turned out to share root cause with this one), but stopping short of the full removal here -- found something worth your own call before I execute it.

Confirmed the half-implemented-on-desktop diagnosis: jumpMode/jumpResults are computed every render but never reach the desktop template at all, and there's genuinely no [data-testid=jump-panel] markup anywhere on desktop. Also confirmed mobile's version does work, exactly as noted.

The complication: on a touch-only mobile viewport, mobile-jump-row currently appears to be the ONLY way to jump directly to an issue by id. The global search panel (Ctrl+K/Cmd+K, tracker #144) has no visible tap-target anywhere in the mobile sheet UI -- btn-global-search only exists in the desktop header and the widget toolbar, neither of which mobile's layout renders. So 'superseded by global search' is true for desktop, but doesn't actually hold for mobile unless I'm missing an entry point somewhere. Removing mobile-jump-row as scoped would leave mobile with no way to jump to an issue by id at all, not a clean no-op.

Side finding: both platforms' row lists are driven by the same filtered  array, and jumpMode was unconditionally skipping keyword-filtering on it -- so mobile was ALSO showing an unfiltered full row list stacked underneath its (correctly-populated) jump-row suggestions whenever jump mode triggered, not just desktop's silent nothing-happens. Fixed that shared bit for #155 (committed separately) without touching jumpMode/jumpResults/mobile-jump-row itself.

Holding off on the rest of this issue's scope (removing matchingIssuesByIdPrefix, mobile-jump-row, openJumpResult, the jumpDismissed/jumpActiveIndex state, and the '#id' placeholder copy) until you've confirmed either: (a) mobile should lose this with no replacement, or (b) there's a mobile search entry point I'm not seeing, or (c) scope this to desktop-only (delete the dead desktop computation, leave mobile's working feature alone).

history.value: Disable all github sync in widget mode

From a /btw chat with claude:

 What do we think about the widget mode having github sync capability?

My honest take: it shouldn't run concurrently with Room Mode's own Matrix-based sync, and if it isn't already blocked, that's worth closing off explicitly.

The core problem: Room Scoped Widget Mode's whole premise is "the room is the durable state" — Matrix room events are the source of truth, merged via wigwag's own signed-history-union logic fed from the timeline. GitHub sync is a second, fully independent sync backend with its own merge semantics (computeIssueMerge reconciling against a pulled JSONL file). Running both for the same project means two uncoordinated sources of truth converging differently — a real correctness risk, not just redundancy.

There's also the same identity problem we just hit with Jira/Salesforce: a GitHub token lives on the identity (githubToken, or a per-project override), and Room Mode suppresses identity to a single auto-bootstrapped one with no reachable settings UI to hold a token. So even setting aside the dual-source-of-truth issue, there's no clean place for the credential to come from.

Where it gets murkier: githubRepo/githubRepoPath/githubRepoBranch live on the project doc itself, not the identity. So if a project that already had GitHub sync configured got imported/received into a room, those fields could in principle ride along on the doc — and I don't know off the top of my head whether the sync-trigger code (maybeScheduleGithubPush, the background poll) currently checks for widget/room mode before acting on those fields, the way we just added that check for the bulk-refresh action. Given the pattern from earlier today — things that look disabled in widget mode but weren't actually gated — I'd bet this is another instance worth checking explicitly rather than assuming it's already handled.

My recommendation: treat GitHub sync as mutually exclusive with Room Mode per project, and gate it the same way (isWidgetMode/ROOM_MODE_CAPABILITIES) if that check isn't already there.

history.value: Changing github tracker seems to break :grimace:

history.text:
Root-caused and fixed, live in chat -- this was a real, confirmed data-loss incident, not just a rough edge.

What happened: switching the connected repo (and/or token) via Settings had NO side effect beyond updating the raw config value -- no sync-status reset, no reconnect. The auto-push mechanism only fires when the PROJECT'S OWN CONTENT changes, so it had no idea the sync TARGET itself had changed -- the UI kept showing stale 'Synced' (green) from the old connection, and nothing was actually attempted against the new repo until some unrelated content edit eventually triggered an auto-push. When that push finally fired, it carried either no sha at all or a stale one left over from the old repo -- and pushGithubFile's own conflict check only ran 'if (sha)', so a missing sha skipped the check ENTIRELY and fell straight through to an unconditional overwrite. Concretely, this clobbered real content (issues #157/#158, plus follow-up comments on #155/#156) that had already been pushed to lampholder/project-state by the CLI -- recovered via a pull+merge+push just now, verified directly against the real remote (not just this tool's own read-back).

Two fixes shipped:
1. pushGithubFile's file-existence check now runs unconditionally, not just when a sha was supplied -- 'I've never seen this file' now correctly means 'go check first', not 'assume it doesn't exist'. A missing sha is treated exactly like a mismatched one: if the file exists, that's a conflict, caller must pull first. Unit-tested directly (wigwag-core.test.js), including the exact incident shape (no sha, file already exists -> conflict, never a blind overwrite).
2. Changing githubRepo/githubRepoPath/githubRepoBranch/githubTokenOverride now immediately invalidates the cached sha/etag/last-synced-text and triggers a real reconnect (respecting document.hidden, same as every other sync trigger) -- no more silently stale 'Synced' status, and no more waiting on an unrelated edit to discover the new target even exists.

Also tried and reverted: caching _githubLastSyncedText on every successful pull-merge (to avoid a harmless redundant push right after a plain reconnect) -- this broke the legitimate conflict-retry path, which depends on that comparison to detect a genuine post-merge change still needing a push. Reverted; the underlying inefficiency (an occasional harmless duplicate commit right after a reconnect finds nothing new) is a known, pre-existing, non-destructive gap, not fixed here.

New/updated tests: tests/github-sync.spec.js ('switching to a different repo mid-session reconnects...' -- the direct regression check for this incident) + 2 existing tests updated for the new conflict-check semantics. Full suite: 22/22. wigwag-core.test.js: 233/233.

Related but out of scope for this fix: #159 (github sync shouldn't run concurrently with Room Mode's Matrix sync at all) is a separate, deeper design question about whether project-level GitHub config should exist in Room Mode in the first place -- worth its own follow-through, not addressed here.

history.value: Split field-binding rules out of the portable project object

history.text:
Filed after the fact (implementation happened first, live in chat with Tom, then filed here per project convention).

Problem: fieldDefs[colId] mixed portable parts (label/type/options) with binding parts (linkedSourceId/rule/ruleRows/ruleFallback), all traveling together through every portable form a project takes -- JSONL export, paste-merge, Matrix-room-scoped sync. Tom's call: bindings are meaningless away from their local Jira/Salesforce/GitHub-proxy bridge, and two people (or a customer) binding the same shared field to their own different systems must not clobber each other -- so bindings must never be part of the portable object.

Implementation:
- New localStorage key LOCAL_FIELD_BINDINGS_KEY (git_native_tracker_local_bindings_v1), per-device/per-project/per-field, outside every export/sync path.
- effectiveFieldDefs(fieldDefs, localFieldBindings) overlays the local map onto portable fieldDefs at evaluation/render time only -- local wins by presence, never by recency (an inbound file's legacy-embedded rule can never resurface over a field already migrated locally).
- The 4 write sites (commitRuleRows, switchRuleToAdvanced, setFieldRule, setFieldLinkedSource) now write only to the local store -- no projectHistory entry, since none of them touch label/type/options. Computed value logging (origin: derived) is untouched.
- ~13 read sites + 3 setState-closure evaluation sites swapped to effectiveDef/effectiveFieldDefs; the one render() swap covers the whole render tree.
- One-time cleanup: editing a field that still carries a *legacy* embedded rule (from before this split) also writes one portable cleanup entry stripping just the binding keys, so deriveFieldDefs's latest-wins reconstruction stops leaking the old rule into future exports. Verified live: a legacy-bound demo-fixture field (type) leaked its rule before this fix, and does not after.

Verification: new tests/local-field-bindings.spec.js (5/5), wigwag-core.test.js unit tests for effectiveFieldDefs (3 new), tests/bound-value-panel.spec.js + tests/data-structures.spec.js re-run together (89/89, zero regressions). docs/FORMAT.md updated with a new subsection. wigwag-cli.js/wigwag-client.js need no changes (confirmed: they only touch fieldDefs opaquely via core.applyLinkedRules/computeFieldDefsMerge).

Not done yet: a full single-worker Playwright suite run (planned next, ~35-40 min).

Found and fixed a real regression during the first full-suite run: bind-issue-field.spec.js's 'copy field' test failed -- buildTextCell() (the text/issue-type cell renderer) still read the raw portable this.state.fieldDefs[colId] directly instead of this.effectiveDef(colId), so an issue-type field bound via the row editor (whose rule now lives only in local storage) stopped rendering its locked/linked pill. select/multiselect/date cells were already correct (they go through buildCell(issue, colId, def) with def sourced from render()'s effectiveFieldDefs()-derived local var) -- buildTextCell was the one path that recomputed its own def independently and was missed.

Fixed (one-line swap), re-verified: tests/bind-issue-field.spec.js 8/8, tests/local-field-bindings.spec.js + tests/bound-value-panel.spec.js + tests/data-structures.spec.js 94/94 together. A second full single-worker suite run is in progress now.

Full single-worker Playwright suite run completed: 922 passed, 1 failure (tests/github-sync.spec.js:284, 'a burst of local edits results in exactly one debounced push' -- expected 2, received 3). Re-ran that one test in isolation and it passed cleanly, confirming it's the same pre-existing pushCount off-by-one flake already known in this file (unrelated to fieldDefs/bindings -- nothing in this change touches GitHub sync debouncing). Two interaction.spec.js 'Staleness highlighting (KNOWN GAP)' tests also showed as failed-then-passed-on-retry, matching their own documented baseline-flake status.

No regressions from the field-binding split. tests/local-field-bindings.spec.js, tests/bind-issue-field.spec.js, tests/bound-value-panel.spec.js, and tests/data-structures.spec.js are all green in this same full run.

Closing this out.

history.value: Widget reconnect can resend an already-committed backfill entry to the room

history.text:
Live-reported by Tom (2026-09-28): scrolling and/or selecting in a real Element widget generated extra dev.wigwag.entry room events -- a decrypted example he shared was a project-scope 'legacy-backfill' entry (id: backfill-field-updated, field: updated, sortKey: -4) appearing as a SEPARATE real Matrix event, i.e. sent twice.

Root cause (traced, not guessed -- confirmed against the actual code in wigwag-matrix-host.html and wigwag-core.js, neither of which I'd touched this session before investigating):

- wigwag-matrix-host.html tracks what's already been sent/received in a purely in-memory Set (knownEntryIds), scoped to that page's own JS lifetime -- never persisted.
- If the widget HOST iframe itself (the wigwag-matrix-host.html page Element manages as the widget, not the wigwag.html app nested inside it) gets unmounted and remounted -- plausible on scroll/visibility changes, a common thing for embedding hosts to do -- knownEntryIds resets to empty.
- On the fresh reconnect, there's a race: the just-sent backfill entry may not have round-tripped through the homeserver yet (Matrix's own eventual consistency / megolm decrypt lag), so the fresh room read doesn't yet see it. Meanwhile the LOCAL copy of the project (in the iframe's shimmed storage) already has it from before. The merge treats it as 'local content the remote side doesn't know about yet' and resends it.
- backfillProjectHistory's entries are fully deterministic (same id, content, and sortKey every time), so the resend is a genuine byte-identical duplicate, not corrupted data -- but it's still a real duplicate landing permanently in the room's timeline, and nothing on the read side previously collapsed it.

Fix shipped (wigwag-core.js's hydrateProjectFromMatrixTimeline, the one shared function every read path -- host bootstrap, reconcile, and wigwag-matrix-host.spec.js's own coverage -- funnels through): dedupe incoming entries by the (id, sortKey) PAIR, not id alone. Deliberately not id alone -- a genuine edit/redaction legitimately reuses the same id for its tombstone and its new live revision, distinguished only by a fresh sortKey (see commitEditComment's own convention, and patchSignature's identical (id, sortKey) matching elsewhere in the codebase). Two entries sharing both id AND sortKey can only be a duplicate delivery of the exact same revision.

This closes the user-visible symptom (no more duplicate lines accumulating in a project's real history) regardless of the exact resend trigger, but does NOT eliminate the underlying resend race itself (a wasted-but-harmless extra encrypted room event can still occur on this same remount+lag scenario) -- a full fix for that would mean making knownEntryIds more robust across a host remount (e.g. seeding it more conservatively, or a short grace period after reconnect before treating anything as newly-local), which is a separate, more involved design question flagged here for later rather than rushed tonight.

Verification: 2 new wigwag-core.test.js unit tests (exact-duplicate dedupe; genuine same-id-different-sortKey edit NOT collapsed), full wigwag-core.test.js 231/231, full tests/matrix-host.spec.js 56/57 (the 1 failure is a pre-existing, already-flaky-before-this-fix test confirmed via git stash -- unrelated).

Follow-up: this issue recurred live (Tom, 2026-09-28) for a different field (backfill-field-created this time), proving the earlier read-side (id, sortKey) dedupe only stopped the double-COUNTING, not the wasteful resend itself, exactly as flagged as a known limitation in my last comment here.

Root-cause fix now shipped, in two parts:
1. wigwag-core.js's hydrateProjectFromMatrixTimeline now also calls ensureTimestampFieldDefs (matching hydrateProject's own unconditional guarantee) -- closing the one real gap that made it unsafe to stop sending these entries: a fresh viewer with zero local state previously had no way to derive created/updated at all unless a real backfill entry already existed in the room's raw timeline.
2. With that gap closed, wigwag-matrix-host.html's pushNewLocalEntries and pushSnapshotForProject now both exclude project-scope created/updated backfill entries specifically from ever being sent as real Matrix events -- every reader now independently and deterministically derives the same two entries, so there's nothing to gain by sending them and nothing lost by never trying. Nothing to duplicate if nothing is ever sent.

Caught one real bug while implementing this, worth recording: my first pass excluded ANY origin:'legacy-backfill' entry from ever being pushed, not just created/updated specifically. That's wrong -- backfillIssueHistoryFromValues and backfillProjectHistory's general case both use that same origin tag for entries synthesized FROM a real, already-known value (an import/paste that only supplied plain field values, not full history) -- that's genuine content only the importing device has, and excluding it silently dropped real user data from ever reaching the room. A full matrix-host.spec.js run caught this immediately (4 failures: bulk-adopt snapshot, large paste-merge import, round-trip read-back, imported-project push all showed 0 entries/snapshots sent where 1+ was expected). Narrowed the exclusion to specifically scope:'project' entries with field 'created' or 'updated' -- the only two fields actually covered by ensureTimestampFieldDefs's universal guarantee.
