history.value: Room Scoped Widget Mode: rehydrate should be a pure replace from room state, with unsent local edits shown as pending instead of merged in

history.text:
Tom's own proposal, live in chat (2026-09-28), while diagnosing #156's root cause: instead of reconcileIntoLocal() merging fresh room-derived state with whatever's sitting in local storage, don't merge at all -- rehydrate should be a pure, total replace from room history (latest snapshot + tail), and any local edit that hasn't round-tripped back yet should be shown as a distinct, visible 'pending' state layered on top, rather than being folded into the same blob that room state lives in.

Why this is stronger than #156's shipped fix: #156's fix excludes exactly two fields (created/updated) from ever being push candidates, because a rehydrate-triggered write to the merged local doc looks identical to a genuine new edit to the push pipeline, and those two are the only ones proven safe to blanket-exclude. This proposal removes the ambiguity structurally instead of special-casing it: if 'what the room says' is a pure, always-replaceable projection that never gets merged with local content, a rehydrate can never manufacture something that looks like 'new local content to push', for ANY field, not just two. The whole bug class (not just this one instance of it) goes away.

Important nuance: there are two different moments today that both call reconcileIntoLocal, with very different risk profiles for dropping the merge:
1. The post-reload/reconnect bootstrap -- right after a host reload, the in-memory shim (both localStorage and knownEntryIds) is already wiped clean before this first runs, so the merge here is already close to a no-op against fresh-from-remote content. Dropping it here is low-risk -- there's nothing real to lose, the reload already lost it.
2. The live 5-second poll tick, while the widget's been open continuously and a local edit from moments ago hasn't round-tripped yet. HERE the merge is doing real, necessary work today -- without it, a poll bringing in someone else's remote change would silently blow away an unsent local edit. This is the case the 'pending' UI is actually for, and it's the one that needs real design, not just deletion.

What 'pending' would need to be, concretely: a genuine outbox, decoupled from the room-state view -- not derived by diffing a merged blob against knownEntryIds the way pushNewLocalEntries does today. Every genuine wigwag:local-write from the iframe appends to a pending list; the room-state view stays a pure, replaceable projection of history; rendering overlays pending-on-top-of-confirmed. Nice property: because entries are content-addressed by (id, sortKey), 'has this pending entry been confirmed' reduces to a stateless membership check against the latest rehydrated view -- no new ack protocol needed between host and iframe.

Side effect worth calling out: this would make #156's shipped fix redundant in the GOOD way -- under this model the created/updated backfill entries are derived, not user-initiated, so they'd never enter the pending outbox at all. The narrow fix becomes unnecessary by construction rather than by exclusion list.

Open design questions, not yet resolved:
- Is 'pending' purely local (only the author sees their own unsent edit) or broadcast to other room viewers? Sounds like the former from how this was described, but it's a real design fork -- broadcast pending is closer to a presence feature, a bigger scope.
- What does a pending edit that outright FAILS (rate-limited, rejected) look like, vs one that's just slow? Today a failed send is silently retried on the next local-write; a visible 'pending' state probably wants a distinct 'failed' state too, not just 'in flight'.
- Real UI work needed in wigwag.html (some per-row/per-field 'not yet synced' affordance) -- this isn't just host-side plumbing.
- knownEntryIds' current dual role (dedupe-on-send-failure AND implicit 'what's new' detector) would likely get simplified/replaced by the pending-outbox model, but that code is shared with the snapshot/bulk-adopt paths -- needs care, not a quick edit.

Not started -- filed for a proper design pass, per Tom's explicit 'discuss, don't build yet' at the time.

- pending is purely local
- pending_and_fails.zip shows the UX around pending and failed changes
- simplifying or removing knownEntryIds sounds _very_ good to me

Engaging -- design handoff (pending_and_failed.zip) reviewed, plus Tom's 3 answers: pending is purely local, knownEntryIds simplification welcomed, and the visual direction is settled (5c for the table cell, 5b's dot+caption pattern reused for the slide-over; 5a and 5b's own cell treatment both explicitly rejected in the handoff).

Plan, in dependency order:

1. Host-side pending outbox (wigwag-matrix-host.html), independent of the existing merge machinery for now:
   - A per-project Map keyed by (id, sortKey) -- matches the read-side dedupe key hydrateProjectFromMatrixTimeline already uses.
   - Populated the moment an entry is queued to send (pushNewLocalEntries) -- marked 'pending'.
   - Cleared to 'confirmed' (removed from the outbox) once reconcileIntoLocal's freshly-rehydrated room state actually contains that (id, sortKey) -- a stateless membership check, no new ack protocol.
   - Marked 'failed' (kept, not silently dropped) when transport.send actually errors/rejects, distinct from merely slow.
   - Pushed to the iframe via a new host->iframe message (wigwag:pending-update), same shape/spirit as the existing wigwag:storage-changed.

2. Iframe-side rendering (wigwag.html):
   - New per-issue/per-field pending/failed lookup, fed by wigwag:pending-update.
   - Table cell (5c): full per-cell grid lines, affected cell gets a faint state wash + 2px left border-accent replacing the normal grid line, plus a 10px inline dot after the value -- pending pulses blue (#3b5bdb), failed is a still red (#c2410c/--danger-ink), confirmed is just today's look.
   - Slide-over field (5b pattern): same dot after the field's caps label, one 11px caption line under the value -- 'Pending, syncing to the room' or 'Failed to sync, Retry' (Retry underlined, clickable; pending has no action).
   - Retry wires to a new host message asking it to re-attempt that one specific entry now, rather than waiting for the next natural local-write trigger.

3. Once (1)+(2) land and are independently verified, the actual architecture change this issue is named for: reconcileIntoLocal stops merging remote into local on the LIVE POLL path (the post-reload/reconnect bootstrap already amounts to a no-op merge today, per my earlier trace, so that half is low-risk) -- safe now specifically BECAUSE the outbox independently preserves any unconfirmed local edit as its own overlay, so a pure replace-from-room-state can no longer silently blow one away. knownEntryIds' 'what's new to push' role gets replaced by the outbox directly; its dedupe-on-resend role may still be needed for the snapshot/bulk-adopt paths -- checking that carefully before touching it.

Starting on (1) and (2) now -- (3) follows once those are verified working end-to-end.

Phase 1+2 shipped and verified (host outbox + pending/failed UI). Phase 3 (making reconcileIntoLocal a pure replace, simplifying/removing knownEntryIds) is still outstanding -- leaving this In Progress, not Done.

What's shipped:
- Host-side pending outbox (wigwag-matrix-host.html): a per-project Map keyed by (id, sortKey), populated the moment an entry is queued to send, cleared once reconcileIntoLocal's freshly-rehydrated room state actually contains that (id, sortKey) -- a stateless membership check, no ack protocol. Marked 'failed' (not silently dropped) when a send genuinely errors.
- wigwag:pending-update host->iframe message, replayed on wigwag:hello-ack too (so a plain iframe reload doesn't briefly show 'confirmed' for something the host still has outstanding).
- Grid cell (5c): full per-cell grid lines already existed; added the faint state wash + 2px left border accent (color-mix off the existing --accent-fill/--danger-ink tokens, per the handoff's 'reuse, don't invent' instruction) and a small absolutely-positioned dot -- matches the existing isLocked padlock's own precedent for overlaying arbitrary cell content, since several cell types (select/multiselect) render an inner width:100% flex row that a plain flex-sibling dot would have overflowed past.
- Slide-over field (5b pattern): dot after the caps label, one caption line under the value ('Pending, syncing to the room' / 'Failed to sync — Retry', Retry underlined and clickable).
- Retry re-runs the normal send pass for the whole project (the failed entry is already sitting in the local doc, never rolled back) rather than a bespoke targeted-resend mechanism.

Real bug caught during live verification, not just assumed working: persist() (wigwag.html) unconditionally writes on every componentDidUpdate, and the room-mode storage shim unconditionally posts wigwag:local-write on every write, regardless of whether content actually changed. Marking an entry 'failed' is itself a state change in the iframe -- which persists -- which re-triggers a send attempt -- which fails again -- forever. Fixed by excluding already-failed entries from automatic retry (only an explicit Retry, or a genuinely new edit to that same field with a fresh id/sortKey, sends again). Caught this by actually running the feature end-to-end with a forced send failure before writing the permanent test, not by reasoning about it in the abstract.

Verification: new tests/matrix-host.spec.js test covering the full pending -> confirmed and pending -> failed -> Retry -> confirmed cycle, including an explicit check that a failed send does NOT self-perpetuate. Full matrix-host.spec.js: 59/59. Desktop-side regression check (buildCell now runs unconditionally for every cell, in or out of Room Mode): select-fields.spec.js + bind-issue-field.spec.js + bound-value-panel.spec.js, 86/86 -- confirms zero impact outside widget mode.

Phase 3 shipped -- all three phases complete.

reconcileIntoLocal no longer merges against readCurrentLocalDoc ("whatever was previously written", the actual root of the original resend-looks-like-new-content bug class). It now merges exactly two independently-tracked, well-defined sources: the room's own freshly-rehydrated history (remoteDoc), and this device's own pending outbox reconstructed into a mergeable partial doc (outboxAsPartialDoc -- the literal inverse of flattenEntries). remoteDoc is deliberately fed as computeIssueMerge's 'local' argument (not the outbox) -- an issue only on the 'incoming' side gets a fresh arbitrary num, correct for a genuinely brand-new unconfirmed issue but wrong for the overwhelming common case (an existing issue with no pending edit, i.e. absent from the outbox) if reversed.

knownEntryIds is gone entirely, per your own call that removing it 'sounds very good'. Its two jobs are now both stateless:
- 'is this already confirmed' -- a fresh membership check against remoteDoc's own flattened (id, sortKey) set, computed on demand, never a mutable cache that can go stale.
- 'have I already attempted this' -- the pending outbox itself (which already existed for phase 1's UI) now does double duty as the real dedupe/retry gate, replacing the old separate bookkeeping entirely. Two structures doing overlapping jobs became one.

pushSnapshotForProject's bulk path got the same treatment -- marks/rolls-back via the outbox instead of knownEntryIds, though a snapshot failure clears the mark entirely rather than surfacing a per-field 'failed' indicator for potentially hundreds of entries at once (a deliberate scope cut, not an oversight).

This closes the resend bug class structurally, not by exclusion list: nothing about this mechanism can ever again mistake 'I just re-derived something the room already has' for 'here's new content to push', for ANY field -- not just the two (created/updated) #156's narrower fix special-cased.

Verification: full tests/matrix-host.spec.js re-run after the rewrite -- 59/59, covering paste-merge imports, bulk-adopts, snapshot round-trips, multi-project rooms, and cross-room isolation, none of which needed a single test change despite the underlying mechanism being completely rebuilt. Live-reverified the phase 1+2 pending/failed UI end-to-end against the new mechanism (pending -> confirmed, and pending -> failed -> Retry -> confirmed) -- unaffected. wigwag-core.test.js 233/233 (untouched by this phase, confirmed anyway).

history.text:
Design handoff from table_layout.zip (design_handoff_layout_proposals/README.md + section 6a of Widget Header.dc.html):

A moderator captures the current column set, order, widths, and freeze point as a snapshot and sends it to the room as a layout proposal, via a new toolbar icon that is visible only to moderators (no disabled state shown to non-moderators -- it simply doesn't appear for them). Sending shows a confirm popover stating the room's member count before it goes out.

Every recipient -- including the sender -- then sees one banner above the table with a mini preview strip of the proposed layout, plus Accept and Dismiss actions. Accepting applies the layout locally only: it never touches issue data, is never exported or merged, and the layout stays freely editable afterward exactly as any other local layout change would be.

Only one proposal is shown at a time. A newer proposal replaces an unaccepted older one outright, rather than queuing or stacking.

Test ids from the handoff: btn-propose-layout, layout-proposal-banner, layout-proposal-preview, btn-accept-layout, btn-dismiss-layout.

DESIGN DECISION (already agreed with Tom, not open for re-litigation as an implementation detail):

The proposal is sent as a real Matrix STATE event, not a timeline entry. Two reasons this is deliberate, not incidental:

1. Moderator-gating comes for free from the room's own power levels -- same precedent already used for work.wigwag.project -- rather than needing a separate app-level permission check.
2. 'Only one proposal shown at a time, newer replaces older' also comes for free from state-event semantics: a state event holds exactly one value per state_key, so there's no accumulation to prune or reconcile -- sending a new proposal simply overwrites the old one.

Please implement against this rather than a timeline-entry approach.

Starting implementation. Plan, in short:

- New Matrix STATE event type work.wigwag.layout-proposal, fixed state_key so 'newer replaces older' is a protocol property, not app logic. Content: columnOrder, columnWidths, hiddenFieldIds, freezeColId, proposedBy, proposedAt.
- Moderator gating is a real power-level check (new plumbing -- reads m.room.power_levels on both the direct-token and widget Matrix transports) so btn-propose-layout is genuinely absent from the toolbar for non-moderators, not just disabled. Confirmed with Tom directly: full check, not the lighter 'show to everyone, reject server-side' fallback used for project creation.
- The send-confirm popover will NOT show a real room member count in this pass (also confirmed with Tom) -- generic confirm text only; a real count is an explicit deferred follow-up if wanted later.
- Column layout snapshot reads/applies through the existing columnWidthsFor/persistColumnWidths/columnOrderFor/persistColumnOrder functions -- no new intermediate shape, and Accept never appends any project/issue history entry or touches portable fieldDefs (matches 'never touches issue data, nothing exported/merged').
- Banner/preview/accept/dismiss state is ephemeral (plain component state, same precedent as the existing room-write-rejected notice) -- not persisted across reload.

Will post a summary here once implemented and verified.

- Moderator visibility is a real, live power-level check (isModeratorForStateEvent in wigwag-core.js, reading m.room.power_levels), not 'show to everyone, reject server-side' -- btn-propose-layout is genuinely absent for a non-moderator.

history.value: Full-screen boot splash on load (design_handoff_issue_tracker, splash_screen.zip)

history.text:
Design handoff from splash_screen.zip (design_handoff_issue_tracker/README.md + Issue Tracker.dc.html). This zip bundles the SAME base mockup as narrower_columns.zip (#166, now shipped) plus one genuinely new feature on top. Confirmed via grep that the other 3 README-described features (header compression, cell affordance fade, cell padding pinch) are already fully implemented and tested under #166 -- nothing further needed for those. Only the boot splash is new work.

FEATURE -- full-screen boot splash (README section "Full-screen boot splash"; DC file: search bootOverlayPhase/bootOverlayVisible/bootMarkBreathe/bootSweep):
- Fixed, full-viewport overlay (position:fixed; inset:0; z-index:400) shown on load, masking the brief unstyled-paint/layout flash while the header/table assemble.
- Content: centered Wigwag mark (logo glyph, 3-path SVG viewBox 0 0 48 62, already used verbatim elsewhere in wigwag.html) + wordmark "Wigwag" in Space Grotesk 700 (font already loaded in wigwag.html via @font-face), breathing via bootMarkBreathe (scale 1<->0.94, opacity 1<->0.8, 1.8s ease-in-out loop). Below it, a 120x3px bar (bg var(--n8)) containing a 40%-width var(--accent-fill) bar sweeping left->right via bootSweep, 1.1s ease-in-out loop.
- Background: var(--surface-page) -- confirmed this token already exists in wigwag.html's light AND dark :root blocks, matching the app's own background so the splash and app never visibly swap tone. Same for --n8, --accent-fill, --n10, --logo-ink -- all already defined, nothing to invent.
- State: bootOverlayPhase starts 'visible'. Derived render values: bootOverlayVisible = phase !== 'hidden'; bootOverlayOpacity = phase === 'fading' ? 0 : 1 (CSS transition 0.4s ease on opacity); bootOverlayPointerEvents = phase === 'fading' ? 'none' : 'auto' (so the fade-out never blocks clicks on the real UI underneath).
- Mockup's lifecycle hook: componentDidMount does a double requestAnimationFrame (let one real paint happen first), then a 260ms minimum-display timer -> 'fading', then 420ms more -> 'hidden' (unmounted via sc-if).

DEVIATION FROM THE MOCKUP (deliberate, flagging before implementing): the mockup assumes a single, synchronous boot path, so componentDidMount is a fine anchor for it. wigwag.html has two: Local Mode calls runBootSequence() synchronously from the constructor; Room Scoped Widget Mode calls it asynchronously, up to ~8s later, from beginRoomModeHandshake()'s timeout fallback or activateRoomMode() after a real handshake -- componentDidMount fires at a fixed point regardless of which path is live, so anchoring the dismiss-timer there would let the splash fade out and disappear mid-handshake, well before real content is ready. Two adaptations:
1. Anchor the double-RAF+260ms dismiss-timer kickoff to the END of runBootSequence() instead of componentDidMount -- it's synchronous and is called from exactly one of those three mutually-exclusive sites per page load, so "boot sequence actually finished" is accurate in both modes.
2. Place the splash's own <sc-if value="{{ bootOverlayVisible }}"> block OUTSIDE/BEFORE the <sc-if value="{{ notRoomModeBootstrapping }}"> wrapper that gates nearly all other top-level UI (confirmed: that wrapper hides its contents for the entire Room Mode handshake window). The splash needs to render during that window too, via its own fixed positioning, rather than being hidden by that same wrapper.

Everything else (markup structure, keyframes, derived values, state shape) ports directly from the DC file.

Picking this up next, after wrapping up #166's full-suite verification.

Done -- shipped exactly as scoped (logo/wordmark/sweep, 260ms min display + 420ms fade, dismiss-timer anchored to the end of runBootSequence() rather than componentDidMount, markup outside notRoomModeBootstrapping -- all per the deviation flagged before starting, to survive Room Scoped Widget Mode's async boot handshake).

The full regression suite found three real, genuine issues this exposed, all root-caused and fixed (not just papered over):

1. Testid collision: named it boot-splash-overlay initially, which tripped interaction.spec.js's existing "no flash of full-screen modal overlays on page load" guard -- that test sweeps every [data-testid$="-overlay"] and asserts none are ever visible at boot, since that whole pattern was built for gated modal scrims (email-gate, paste-import, etc.) that are NEVER legitimately open at boot. The splash breaks that premise on purpose. Renamed to boot-splash to stop colliding with that guard rather than weakening it.

2. Click-blocking vs. test timing: the splash deliberately blocks clicks (pointer-events) for up to ~680ms on every page load/reload -- correct for a real user (nobody clicks meaningfully within 700ms of a reload anyway), but several existing tests only waited a fixed 300-400ms before interacting, so their clicks landed on the (invisible-while-fading-but-still-blocking) overlay instead of the real content underneath. Added a shared waitForBootSplashGone() helper, wired into every shared navigation helper plus the handful of ad-hoc bypasses that needed it directly.

3. The more interesting one: this is the FIRST thing to guarantee a real setState() on an otherwise genuinely idle reload (nothing else changing). That triggers componentDidUpdate's full persist battery for the first time ever on an idle reload -- including persistProjectIndex(), which unconditionally re-asserts whatever project THIS tab currently has active as the shared cross-tab "last active anywhere" pointer. That's apparently always been true architecturally, but previously only got exercised when something else ALSO happened to trigger a state change -- an idle reload with nothing else going on essentially never used to touch it. tests/cross-tab-sync.spec.js caught this directly: tab A reloads (idle), the splash's own phase transitions fire persistProjectIndex() for the first time, and it stomps a DIFFERENT tab's more recent project switch. Fixed by seeding the de-dup cache from this tab's own resolved project at the end of runBootSequence(), before the splash can trigger that first write -- a genuine later switch still persists correctly, an incidental render caused by the splash no longer does.

Full suite: 990 passed, only the 2 confirmed pre-existing baseline flakes (mentions.spec.js's tight timing assertion, milestones.spec.js's pushCount flake -- both reproduce on a clean pre-session checkout too, unrelated to this).

Committed as 27619b3. Moving on to #168 next.

Follow-up, same session: live testing (Tom) surfaced many more instances of the same pre-mount flash bug class on top of the shipped splash -- 'Connecting to room...' flashing in Local Mode, the widget transport's own connect-form/'unpacking' text, several placeholder logos/skeletons, a full teardown+rebuild from the bundler's own script-revival mechanism, and three untagged modal backdrops (field editor/rule builder/slideover) with no testid for the existing prehide mechanism to reach.

Root cause (confirmed via live frame-by-frame measurement): two separate bundler mechanisms -- (1) sc-if hint-placeholder blocks paint against something other than the real hint value during an initial static pass, before any real component state exists; (2) the unpacker's script-revival does a full document.body teardown+rebuild (scripts don't execute via replaceWith/innerHTML, so it manually recreates and reswaps every <script> tag), which measurably zeroes out the DOM for a moment right before the real mount.

Fix: extended the existing __wigwag_prehide_style convention to cover room-mode-bootstrapping, boot-splash (now unconditional, not just when embedded), a newly-tagged mobile-shell-root, room-no-projects, and the three newly-tagged backdrops -- systematically swept all 27 top-level hint-placeholder-guarded fixed/inset:0 blocks to confirm the set is complete. Room Mode specifically: wigwag.html now signals wigwag:ready to its parent only once roomModeBootstrapping actually flips false (not componentDidMount, which fires too early on first mount -- this exact bug was live-caught and fixed this round). wigwag-matrix-host.html splits showFrame() into startLoadingFrame()/revealFrame(), and its own placeholder is now a static, zero-animation splash matching wigwag.html's -- animation was explicitly rejected after Tom found it caused its own perceived flicker on re-render ('simple, clean, zero flicker').

Verified across 9 iterative live-tested rounds plus a final full single-worker suite run: 990/992 passing, both failures confirmed pre-existing/unrelated (mentions.spec.js's documented first-connect flake; interaction.spec.js's History-tab-reset test, which passes 3/3 in isolation and against the pre-change baseline -- only flakes under full-suite CPU contention). Committed as d4d1367.

Two real bugs found live during this work were investigated but NOT fixed -- filed as their own issues rather than guessed at: #170/ebec3dc5 (widget mode occasionally shows a stale/incomplete project on slow 10s opens) and #171/bd789504 (Room Mode table rows sometimes render too tall then shrink). Both need fresh, better-instrumented investigation, not more guessing on top of this round.

Regression + revert, same conversation thread as the earlier follow-up above. Making boot-splash's prehide unconditional (to fix a disappear/reappear flicker) traded it for a worse bug, live-reported: a full flash of raw, unresolved template text ('{{ note.ProjectName }}' style content, every modal/menu visible simultaneously) in plain Local Mode, for roughly the window between the unpacker's document swap and componentDidMount's real mount.

Root cause: the Layer-1 #__bundler_thumbnail is destroyed outright by document.documentElement.replaceWith() (it's part of the OLD document being wholesale replaced, not revealed later), and with boot-splash ALSO unconditionally prehidden, nothing covered that gap. Desktop's own hint-placeholder-val for boot-splash is {{ true }} specifically so it covers exactly this gap -- unconditional hiding defeated that for the one context (desktop) where it was never the problem to begin with; it was only ever needed for the embedded/widget case (where the real value should be false but the broken placeholder pass might show it anyway).

Reverted to conditional (window.parent !== window) -- commit 36aab28. Confirmed via direct screenshot at the previously-flagged flash moment (clean splash, no garbage visible) and confirmed widget mode still never shows it. The ORIGINAL flicker this unconditional version was fixing does return (live-reported immediately after, expected) -- a real fix for that needs moving boot-splash's initial paint out of the component's own render tree entirely (so it survives the real component's first-render churn), which is a bigger, separate, not-yet-attempted undertaking. New regression test added asserting any transient raw template text is always covered by an opaque, visible splash (not that it never exists in the DOM at all -- innerText doesn't know about z-index occlusion, ruled out as a false-positive with a real screenshot first).

history.value: macOS CI build: "Wigwag is damaged and should be moved to the Trash" (unsigned binary, Apple Silicon Gatekeeper)

history.text:
Live-reported (Tom): downloaded the macOS artifact from the new CI workflow (#168/233a071d), got "Wigwag is damaged and should be moved to the Trash" on open -- not the usual "unidentified developer, right-click to open" prompt.

Root cause: Apple Silicon's kernel-level code-signing enforcement requires EVERY executable to carry at least an ad-hoc signature to run at all -- this is stricter than classic Gatekeeper's "unidentified developer" warning (which right-click->Open bypasses) and isn't bypassable the same way. Our CI build has no signing step configured at all, so the binary has zero signature, which macOS on Apple Silicon reports as "damaged" rather than "unsigned" -- a well-documented, confusing failure mode for exactly this situation (not a real corruption, not a bad download).

Fix: tauri.conf.json's bundle.macOS.signingIdentity set to "-" tells Tauri's bundler to ad-hoc self-sign the .app during build -- zero cost, no real Apple Developer certificate needed. This downgrades the failure from "damaged, binned" to the normal, expected "unverified developer" prompt that right-click->Open does bypass. Real notarization (removing that prompt entirely) is a separate, deliberately deferred follow-up (needs a paid Apple Developer account) -- already flagged as a known limitation on #168.

Applying the signingIdentity fix now alongside the load-screen work.

history.value: Widget mode (10s slow open): shows a phantom placeholder project (wrong name, 0 issues) instead of the real one; writes still land correctly; refresh fixes it

history.text:
Live-reported (Tom): widget took ~10s to open (slow), and when it did, the displayed project was wrong:
- Name showed as a generic placeholder ("Project 1131c798" -- the 8-char suffix fallback, see discoverProjects below), not the real project name.
- That 8-char suffix doesn't match any real project id Tom could find (worth double-checking it's not just the trailing 8 chars of the REAL id, easy to miss in a full UUID -- but flagging as reported, unconfirmed either way).
- Zero issues shown, despite the real project having them.
- BUT: adding an issue in this broken state actually lands in the REAL project (confirmed by Tom checking afterward) -- so the underlying write-target reference is correct, only the DISPLAYED read-side data (name, issue list) is wrong/stale/incomplete.
- A refresh fixes everything.

Pattern strongly suggests a genuine data-completeness or ordering race in the connect/discover/bootstrap flow, not a reference-identity bug. Initial investigation (not a fix, just orientation for whoever picks this up):

- bridges/wigwag-matrix-host.html's discoverProjects() (~line 1122) falls back to `'Project ' + id.slice(-8)` specifically when core.deriveProjectName() finds NO project-scope rename entries for that id yet in the event set it was given -- i.e. this fallback firing at all means the real name-bearing entries (and, separately, zero issues shown means the real issue entries) simply weren't present in the data discoverProjects() was run against at the time.
- connect() (~line 2139) builds that event set from a SINGLE `transport.pullInitial()` call. A comment already on this function (re: room-creator/power-levels fetches) explicitly flags that "its own full-timeline pull has no guarantee of reaching a project created long before this reconnect" -- i.e. pullInitial()'s completeness is ALREADY a known, documented open question for other data, not necessarily exhaustive.
- "A refresh fixes it" is consistent with either: (a) a second pullInitial() attempt genuinely getting further back / more complete pagination (non-deterministic completeness), or (b) by the time of the refresh, background polling (bridgeTimer) had already backfilled the missing data into the room's local storage shim, so the refresh's boot reads already-complete local state rather than depending on a fresh network pull reaching far enough.
- The ~10s slow-open is itself a useful clue -- whatever's happening (possibly multiple paginated reads, possibly a retry cascade somewhere in connect()'s own sequence of dedicated reads) is clearly doing substantial work before landing on an incomplete result, not failing fast.

NOT yet determined: whether this is purely a pullInitial()-completeness issue, or whether there's ALSO a race between when connect()'s results get written into the room-mode storage shim and when wigwag.html actually reads from it (e.g. via the wigwag:hello-ack snapshot handoff) -- i.e. whether the shim write genuinely finished before wigwag.html's own read, or whether wigwag.html can boot against a partially-populated shim. Needs real investigation (live repro + instrumentation of the actual event counts/timing on a real slow connection) before attempting a fix -- this is in an area of the bridge that's already been the subject of many prior live-bug-fix iterations (see the extensive comments throughout connect() about stale/incomplete reads for other data), so a confident fix needs to actually understand which of the above it is, not guess.

Filed rather than fixed tonight -- this needs a clear-headed investigation (real repro, instrumentation, understanding which of the above mechanisms is actually responsible) rather than a guess at 5am on top of an already-large night of changes.

Additional data point, same session: Tom also saw the table visibly grow/resize itself shortly after initial render, in Room Mode specifically. Very likely the SAME root cause as the wrong-project-name/0-issues symptom above, not a separate bug: if the initial snapshot handed to wigwag.html (via wigwag:hello-ack's ackData.snapshot) is incomplete, and the REST of the real entries arrive moments later via the bridge's own background poll (bridgeTimer, pushed into the iframe's storage shim via wigwag:storage-changed -- confirmed this mechanism exists and would cause a real state update/re-render), new rows would genuinely appear and grow the table -- which looks exactly like "the table resizes itself."

Investigated and ruled out a separate theory first (worth recording so it isn't re-investigated): wondered if this was instead a measurement bug from wigwag-matrix-host.html's own startLoadingFrame/revealFrame split (tracker #167/2275c4a6) -- #frame sits display:none for part of boot, and a hidden iframe's content genuinely has zero layout (confirmed empirically: clientHeight/scrollHeight/offsetParent all collapse to 0/null, not just "unpainted"). measureTableOverflow() runs on every componentDidUpdate and could have baked in a wrong measurement during that window. Fixed that regardless (guarded measureTableOverflow against offsetParent===null, added an explicit wigwag:revealed-triggered remeasure after the real reveal) since it's a genuine, independently-valid defect -- but traced its only consumer, tableCardMargin, and found it's forced to '0' whenever ROOM_MODE_CAPABILITIES is set, i.e. that whole mechanism's visible effect is SUPPRESSED in Room Mode specifically. Confirmed with Tom this fix did NOT resolve what he's still seeing -- so that was a real bug worth fixing, but not THIS bug.

Given this, the actual fix here is almost certainly on the SYNC-COMPLETENESS side (same open question flagged in the comment above: whether pullInitial()'s own completeness is the gap, or a race between connect()'s results landing in the storage shim and wigwag.html's own read of it) -- not a rendering/measurement issue. Still needs the same real, focused investigation flagged above: live repro, instrumentation of actual event counts/timing, before attempting a fix. Not something to guess at on top of everything else changed tonight.

history.value: Room Mode: table rows sometimes render too tall, then visibly shrink to normal height shortly after

history.text:
Live-reported (Tom), Room Mode: "sometimes there's a flicker as the table appears to resize itself after rendering." Clarified on follow-up: NOT more rows appearing (ruled that theory out) -- the SAME rows render, they're just too tall initially, then visibly shrink to their normal height shortly after.

Three theories investigated and ruled out via direct code tracing, recorded here so they aren't re-investigated:

1. Row-COUNT growth via background poll (bridgeTimer pushing new entries in after initial render via wigwag:storage-changed) -- ruled out by Tom's own clarification that it's the same rows, not new ones.
2. measureTableOverflow() baking in a wrong "no overflow" result while #frame sits display:none during part of boot (tracker #167/2275c4a6's startLoadingFrame/revealFrame split) -- confirmed empirically that a hidden iframe's content has genuinely zero layout (clientHeight/scrollHeight/offsetParent all collapse), and FIXED this regardless as a real, independently-valid defect (guarded measureTableOverflow against offsetParent===null, added an explicit wigwag:revealed-triggered remeasure after reveal) -- but traced measureTableOverflow's only consumer (tableCardMargin) and found it's forced to '0' whenever ROOM_MODE_CAPABILITIES is set, i.e. suppressed in Room Mode specifically. Confirmed with Tom this fix did NOT resolve what he's still seeing.
3. Column widths not yet reflecting the real persisted values because the Room Mode snapshot handoff (ackData.snapshot) hasn't fully landed yet when columnWidthsFor() first reads them, causing text to wrap more than it should (tall rows) until the real widths arrive and text un-wraps (shrink) -- ruled out by checking isRoomModeContentKey(): it ONLY matches PROJECTS_KEY/docKey(...); COLUMN_WIDTHS_KEY is NOT a room-mode content key, so it's always read from REAL, unshimmed localStorage with zero Room Mode timing dependency at all.

Attempted a live repro using the fake-widget-host.html test harness, seeded with realistic content matching the demo fixture's own GitHub-linked-title scenario (tests/fixtures/demo-milestone.jsonl's i1, which has a real fieldRef and would show "Loading…" before resolving) -- rows went straight from an empty placeholder state to their final, correct heights with no observed tall-then-shrink transition. Did not reproduce.

Not fixed tonight -- genuinely elusive/intermittent ("sometimes"), three plausible mechanisms ruled out by direct code inspection, and a synthetic repro attempt didn't trigger it either. Needs either a more specific repro recipe from Tom (what's the row/field content like when this happens? does it correlate with anything -- project switch, window resize, specific field types, comment counts?) or accepting this needs a fresh, better-instrumented look rather than more guessing at the end of an already very long session.

history.value: Widget view: detect (not decrypt) an E2EE room so empty-state copy doesn't lie

history.text:
Raised live by Tom while reviewing the widget empty-state feature (#175/01bd4c2f, now being removed -- see that issue): if a Matrix room has native E2EE turned on, wigwag has ZERO awareness of it anywhere in the codebase -- confirmed by direct search, the only 'encrypt' hits in the whole repo are encryptSnapshotPayload in bridges/wigwag-matrix-host.html, which is wigwag's own app-level encryption of its snapshot blob before upload, unrelated to Matrix's native room encryption.

In a genuinely E2EE room, every timeline event (including wigwag's own custom entry events) arrives as opaque m.room.encrypted ciphertext -- wigwag's event-matching code doesn't recognize any of it, so a room with real (encrypted) issues and a genuinely empty room look IDENTICAL from its perspective: both just 'no matching events found'. This is exactly why 'No issues yet!' was actively misleading, not just imprecise, in that case -- it would confidently lie.

What IS cheaply buildable without a full E2EE/decryption implementation: Matrix state events (unlike timeline messages) are never encrypted, so m.room.encryption's presence is always readable via a plain state fetch -- same pattern already used for power_levels. That would let wigwag detect 'this room has encryption on' (even though it still can't read anything) and show an honest message ('This room is end-to-end encrypted -- wigwag can't read it') instead of either a misleading empty-state or a silent, ambiguous blank area.

Full E2EE support (olm/megolm session handling, device verification, key exchange) is a much bigger lift and explicitly NOT what this issue is about -- just the cheap detection-only piece. Not started.

Correction to my own comment above -- Tom caught a real error in my reasoning, live. I'd concluded 'full E2EE support' was needed and framed it as out of scope; that's wrong.

The actual mechanics: megolm sessions get re-evaluated against room membership on a join (clients rotate/re-share the active outbound session at that point per normal Matrix behavior), so a new member legitimately receives the current session key going forward through completely standard key-sharing -- no retroactive decryption of any pre-join ciphertext required. A snapshot pushed by any already-E2EE-participating client AFTER that point -- using the EXISTING pushSnapshotForProject/uploadSnapshotBlob mechanism already built for scalability (tracker f6b39bf0's rate-limiting) -- gets encrypted with a session the new member can read. Full project state, one shot, zero historical decryption needed.

This splits what looked like one hard problem into two very different ones:
1. Reading room HISTORY (hard -- needs key backup/sharing, genuinely thorny, legitimately out of scope).
2. Participating in the room's LIVE E2EE state going forward (device registration, olm account, receiving/decrypting the CURRENT megolm session) -- real client-side crypto work, not nothing, but meaningfully smaller and more standard than #1, and the existing snapshot mechanism becomes the delivery vehicle for free once #2 exists.

Doesn't change that this is still real, non-trivial crypto implementation work (olm/megolm, device trust decisions) -- but the shape of the problem is meaningfully different from what I described above, and the cheap detection-only piece (reading the always-unencrypted m.room.encryption state event) remains a good, much smaller first step regardless of whether #2 ever gets built.

Second correction, live, same conversation -- Tom again: Matrix has room history key sharing (MSC3061) -- when history_visibility allows it and the other participants' clients implement key-forwarding, a NEW joiner can receive pre-join megolm session keys directly and decrypt old messages with zero gap, no snapshot needed at all.

This kills my proposed detection signal above (lastSnapshotAt < myOwnJoinTime) -- it would false-positive constantly in exactly the rooms where MSC3061 already works, which is worse than nothing (a banner that's wrong often enough gets ignored). The real signal has to be ACTUAL decrypt failures, not a timing proxy: did I receive an event whose metadata I can see (sender, timestamp, event id) but genuinely cannot decrypt, after giving key-forwarding a realistic moment to land -- and that count needs to be able to heal itself quietly (retry previously-failed events as new keys arrive via to-device messages, no banner at all if they resolve) rather than being a one-shot verdict taken at join time.

Revised shape of the three original questions:
1. Joining user detects incompleteness via persistent real decrypt failures (a genuine MEGOLM_UNKNOWN_INBOUND_SESSION_ID-class failure that doesn't resolve after a grace period/retry), not a snapshot-vs-join timestamp comparison.
2. Signal to others: an unencrypted per-user state event (same shape as #169's layout-proposal pattern) carrying something like undecryptableCount, updated as retries succeed -- not a static boolean set once at join.
3. Resolution stays manual (a 'send snapshot now' action offered once failures are real and persistent), relying on the existing 24h snapshot cycle as the honest fallback -- this part didn't change.

Net: still real, non-trivial crypto work (olm/megolm, now also key-forwarding/retry handling specifically), and still contingent on wigwag having ANY live E2EE participation at all, which doesn't exist today. Flagging for whoever picks this up next: don't reach for a timing heuristic here, it has a real, demonstrated false-positive case.

Follow-up design work split into its own issue since it grew beyond pure E2EE detection into general snapshot-management health (two of the three weaknesses there apply to any project, encrypted or not): #178/3f849ce5, 'Holistic snapshot coordination redesign'. Covers the shared-state-event redesign, generous (non-moderator-gated) manual AND automatic triggering, redaction-tied-to-supersession, and -- directly continuing this issue's own thread -- the 'everyone who could help is offline' case: a persistent (not transient) per-user gap signal, gated risky actions (new issue / delete / export) while a gap is open, and an honest 'waiting for someone to help' UX that doesn't over-promise resolution time.

history.value: Holistic snapshot coordination redesign (shared state, generous triggering, gap-aware action gating)

history.text:
Design conversation with Tom, live. Three named weaknesses in today's snapshot mechanism (bridges/wigwag-matrix-host.html), plus a fourth (E2EE new-member catch-up, tracker #176/303d7dc9) that turns out to share the same root cause and the same fix:

ROOT CAUSE, confirmed by reading the real code: there is no shared, canonical state about 'what's the current snapshot situation for this project' -- only private, per-process memory. lastSnapshotAt/lastSnapshotEntryCount are plain in-memory Maps scoped to one browser tab, reset on every reload. pushSnapshotIfDue's threshold check (200 entries or 24h) runs independently in every connected client against its own private guess. An existing code comment already says the quiet part out loud: 'multiple viewers independently crossing the threshold around the same time is wasteful but harmless.' Cleanup is explicitly out of scope today ('cleaning up superseded/orphaned blobs is explicitly out of scope for now'). No manual trigger exists anywhere except a test-only hook (window.__wigwagTestForcePushSnapshot).

PROPOSED DESIGN: make 'current snapshot status' a real piece of shared room state -- one more state event, same shape as the existing layout-proposal/moderator-status pattern (tracker #169/4f07e72b) -- {snapshotId, createdAt, entryCount, cutoffSortKey}, plus a short-lived 'claim' sub-field for an in-progress upload, readable by every client instead of private per-tab memory.

1. Redundant timers -- fixed by clients checking the SHARED value instead of private per-process memory, so they actually agree on whether one is overdue; the claim field lets a second client back off instead of racing, same spirit as the existing in-process snapshotInFlight lock just extended across clients.
2. Old snapshots linger forever -- superseding the shared state event is a natural, specific trigger to fire a real Matrix-level m.room.redaction against the PREVIOUS manifest event (not just silently superseding it, which is all that happens today). Doesn't guarantee the homeserver actually garbage-collects the underlying media blob (server-dependent), but stops the old manifest being trivially discoverable by reading room history, which is most of what currently makes app-level redaction (redactHistoryEntry) feel like theater against a still-fetchable pre-redaction snapshot.
3. Nobody can choose to push one -- promote the existing, already-safe, already-locked pushSnapshotForProject from test-only hook to a real UI action.

SCOPE DECISION, confirmed live with Tom: triggering is NOT moderator-gated, in either direction -- ANY member can manually push one, and ANY client can AUTOMATICALLY push one in reaction to another member's gap signal (see below), no human click required. Rationale, direct from Tom: the widget's own MSC2762 capability grant (confirmed by reading WIDGET_CAPABILITIES) is scoped per-event-type to ONLY wigwag's own project data (entries/snapshots/project-state/layout-proposals, plus read-only power-levels/room-create) -- it can never read arbitrary room content. Given that bound, 'share wigwag project data generously among members who already assume they're looking at the same tracker' is a smaller surprise than a member silently holding an incomplete view of what everyone assumes is shared. This also simplifies the earlier #176 design: the per-user gap signal isn't a request a moderator has to notice and act on, it's a plain health signal any connected client reactively resolves.

Follow-up, same conversation: Tom raised the case where EVERYONE who could share a fresh snapshot is offline when a new member joins -- wigwag should detect the gap, say so honestly, and stop the user doing something harmful in the meantime (his example: creating a new issue on a project they can't fully see). Worked through this properly rather than just transcribing it -- several real implications surfaced:

1. PRECISION LIMIT, worth stating plainly so nobody designs toward something impossible: an encrypted event's TYPE is itself inside the ciphertext. A client cannot tell, before decrypting, whether a given undecryptable event was a work.wigwag.entry or unrelated room chat. 'Count of undecryptable wigwag entries specifically' is not a computable signal. The honest version is coarser and room-wide: 'this room has SOME undecryptable history' -- deliberately over-cautious (a false positive costs an unnecessary banner; a false negative costs a confident duplicate issue created against data the user couldn't see).

2. THE SIGNAL MUST BE PERSISTENT STATE, not a transient/ephemeral notification -- this is specifically what makes the 'everyone was offline' case resolve itself eventually rather than silently failing forever. As durable state (not a one-shot message only live clients see at the moment it fires), whoever NEXT connects -- an hour, a day, a week later -- still sees the still-standing signal and can react to it, automatically, per the generous-triggering design above. If it were ephemeral, the exact scenario Tom described (nobody was online at the right moment) would mean the signal is just gone and nobody ever finds out.

3. GATING ISN'T UNIFORM across actions. Clearest case: creating a NEW issue (highest duplication risk against invisible content) -- hard block. Same bucket: destructive actions (delete) and anything that PROPAGATES the incomplete view elsewhere (Send/export/merge into a separate copy) -- these all add-to or spread a knowingly incomplete picture. Pure viewing/sorting/filtering: untouched, no reason to gate. Editing a field on an issue you CAN already see is the genuinely gray middle case -- real context exists for it, just maybe not ALL of it; leaning warn-not-block there rather than lumping it in with 'create new'.

4. SCOPE BOUNDARY worth stating explicitly in any implementation: this is a courtesy rail for an honest client protecting an honest user from an honest mistake, NOT a security/anti-abuse boundary. Nothing stops a different or modified client from posting anyway -- Matrix has no server-side mechanism to prevent that, and this feature isn't trying to.

5. UX HONESTY: the 'waiting for help' state should not promise fast resolution it can't guarantee -- MSC3061 history-key-sharing might resolve a gap within seconds of a relevant device coming online, or might never arrive at all (wrong history_visibility, no participant's client implements key-forwarding, the relevant device is gone for good) depending entirely on circumstances the local client can't predict. Message like 'waiting for someone to help you catch up', not 'this will clear up shortly'.

6. Composes cleanly with the generous-triggering design in the main comment above: Bob's own client detects its own gaps -> writes the persistent signal -> gates its own risky actions locally -> shows the honest banner. ANY other already-connected, already-keyed-in client (not just a moderator, not just whoever Bob happens to ping) observes the signal whenever it next connects and can auto-push a fresh snapshot in response, closing the loop without requiring a human to notice and act at the right moment.

7. Everything in this issue and #176 is explicitly FUTURE work, contingent on wigwag first gaining any real live E2EE participation capability at all (device registration, current-session megolm) -- which does not exist today. Worth restating clearly so this isn't mistaken for a gap in TODAY's shipped behavior.

Two corrections to the design above, live with Tom.

CORRECTION 1 -- the coordination state event must NOT carry the real manifest content. Confirmed by reading the actual send path (wigwag-core.js): sendMatrixSnapshotManifest -> putMatrixEvent with no stateKey, which only ever takes putMatrixEvent's /send/{eventType}/{txnId} path (never /state/), i.e. TODAY's manifest -- encryption key material included -- is a genuine timeline event, correctly megolm-gated whenever the room has E2EE on. Nothing is baked into anything unencrypted today. The risk is specific to the PROPOSED redesign: state events are NEVER Matrix-encrypted, full stop, regardless of room E2EE settings -- so if the new lightweight coordination state event were implemented by just copying today's manifest content wholesale (encryption field included) into a state event for convenience, that would silently hand the real decryption key to anyone who can read room state, with zero dependency on actual megolm access. The fix is a clean split, not a single event doing both jobs: the REAL manifest (key material included) stays exactly as it is today -- a timeline event, megolm-gated. A SEPARATE, new, deliberately-minimal state event carries ONLY coordination metadata that's genuinely fine to be plaintext -- which timeline event id is currently 'the latest snapshot', its cutoffSortKey, createdAt. No encryption field, ever, in the state event. 'Can I decrypt the latest snapshot' then means 'can I decrypt the specific timeline event the state-event pointer names' -- clean and checkable, without weakening real access control.

CORRECTION 2 -- 'can I decrypt the latest snapshot + everything after it in the DAG' (Tom's proposed simplification, a real improvement on the original room-wide 'any undecryptable event' heuristic) runs into a harder wall: checked directly, MSC2762's widget API gives wigwag NO visibility into decrypt failures at all. Per the spec and documented Element bug history, the widget always receives already-decrypted events from the host; there is no signal for 'something here failed to decrypt' surfaced to an embedded widget, only silence (historically, events sometimes didn't arrive at all in encrypted rooms, with the only indication being an unread badge in the HOST's own UI -- invisible to the widget). So wigwag-the-widget cannot directly ask 'did anything fail here.'

Resolution: make the signal INDIRECT instead of direct, riding the same coordination state event from Correction 1. Extend it to also carry, per client, 'the highest entry sortKey I've successfully processed.' 'Am I caught up' becomes a comparison: is my own high-water-mark meaningfully behind the most recent one someone else published, despite my supposedly receiving live updates? That's inferable from data wigwag CAN see (what it successfully received), without needing any introspection into decrypt failures the widget API doesn't expose. Weaker than true failure-detection (if everyone who could tell me is offline, per Tom's original scenario, there's nothing yet to compare against -- which is honestly the same 'waiting for help' state as before, just reached by a different path) but it's the version actually buildable against the real widget API, and it doesn't require wigwag to become a full independent E2EE-capable Matrix client just for this one check.

history.value: Apple Developer account: steps to wire up real macOS code signing + notarization

history.text:
Tom has a real Apple Developer Program membership now (9/year, already purchased). Steps HE needs to do himself (all need a real Mac + his own Apple ID -- none of this is doable by Claude, no account access, no payment, no Mac in the sandbox):

1. CONFIRM ENROLLMENT: developer.apple.com -> Account -> make sure membership shows Active (can take a few hours after payment).

2. GENERATE A CSR (Certificate Signing Request), on the Mac:
   - Open Keychain Access -> menu bar Keychain Access > Certificate Assistant > Request a Certificate From a Certificate Authority.
   - Enter his email, common name (e.g. his own name or 'Wigwag'), select 'Saved to disk'. Produces a .certSigningRequest file.

3. CREATE THE CERTIFICATE in the Apple Developer portal:
   - developer.apple.com -> Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles -> Certificates -> '+'.
   - Choose 'Developer ID Application' specifically (NOT 'Apple Distribution', which is App-Store-only and wrong for direct-download distribution like wigwag's).
   - Upload the CSR from step 2. Download the resulting .cer file.

4. INSTALL + EXPORT AS .p12:
   - Double-click the downloaded .cer to add it to Keychain Access (it'll pair automatically with the private key the CSR step generated).
   - In Keychain Access, find the new 'Developer ID Application: ...' certificate, right-click -> Export, choose .p12 format, set a password (needed in step 7).

5. BASE64-ENCODE THE .p12 FOR CI:
   - Terminal: 
   - This produces the value for the APPLE_CERTIFICATE secret below.

6. GET A NOTARIZATION CREDENTIAL -- either path works, pick one:
   - EASIER: an app-specific password. appleid.apple.com -> Sign-In and Security -> App-Specific Passwords -> generate one. Use this + his real Apple ID email.
   - MORE ROBUST (recommended for CI, no 2FA/personal-password dependency): an App Store Connect API key. appstoreconnect.apple.com -> Users and Access -> Integrations -> Individual API Keys (or team keys) -> generate one with at least 'Developer' role. Download the resulting .p8 key file ONCE (Apple only lets you download it once) -- note the Key ID and Issuer ID shown alongside it too.

7. FIND HIS TEAM ID:
   - developer.apple.com -> Account -> Membership Details -> Team ID (10-character alphanumeric).

8. ADD GITHUB REPO SECRETS (Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions -> New repository secret) -- Claude cannot create these, they need to go in via the GitHub UI:
   - APPLE_CERTIFICATE -- the base64 text from step 5.
   - APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD -- the .p12 password from step 4.
   - APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY -- the certificate's full common name, exactly as it appears in Keychain Access, e.g. 'Developer ID Application: Thomas Lant (TEAMID1234)'.
   - APPLE_TEAM_ID -- from step 7.
   - Either: APPLE_ID + APPLE_PASSWORD (the app-specific password from step 6), OR APPLE_API_KEY (the .p8 contents) + APPLE_API_KEY_ID + APPLE_API_ISSUER -- whichever path was chosen in step 6.

9. TELL CLAUDE once the secrets are in place -- the workflow/config changes on wigwag's side (tauri.conf.json's signingIdentity, wiring these env vars into the macOS leg of tauri-build.yml) are a separate, already-scoped follow-up that doesn't need anything further from Tom beyond confirming the secrets exist.

Verified against Tauri's own current docs and tauri-action's real env var names (not guessed) -- see chat for sources. None of this has been tested against a real Apple account/Mac from this session (can't be -- no Mac, no account), so step order/field names should be treated as 'correct as of checking the docs just now', not personally walked-through.

Correction to step 5 above -- the actual terminal command got accidentally stripped by a shell-quoting mistake when I posted the original comment. The real command is:

openssl base64 -in /path/to/certificate.p12 -out certificate-base64.txt

(replace /path/to/certificate.p12 with wherever the exported file actually landed, e.g. ~/Desktop/certificate.p12)

Done -- real macOS code signing + notarization confirmed working end to end, real CI run, real Apple Developer ID Application certificate.

What actually happened, for the record (a couple of real snags, both resolved):
- Keychain Access initially refused to import the issued certificate (error -25294/errSecNoSuchKeychain) -- it had defaulted the import destination to something other than the login keychain. Fixed via File > Import Items, explicitly targeting "login".
- The .p12 export option was greyed out until using the "My Certificates" category specifically and expanding to the paired private key -- plain "Certificates" category didn't show the pairing needed for a .p12 export.
- App Store Connect API key access required an extra permissions/access request Tom didn't have yet -- switched to the simpler Apple ID + app-specific-password notarization credential instead (APPLE_ID/APPLE_PASSWORD/APPLE_TEAM_ID), which needs nothing beyond an app-specific password from appleid.apple.com. Tradeoff noted at the time: tied to Tom's own Apple ID account state rather than a standing API credential, acceptable for a single-maintainer project.
- First real CI attempt failed on a casing mismatch: the APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY secret had the name mixed-case ("Thomas Holden Lant") but the real certificate's Common Name is all-caps ("THOMAS HOLDEN LANT") -- cert identity strings need to match exactly, byte for byte.
- Second attempt got through signing cleanly and submitted to Apple's notary service, then failed on a transient single-request HTTP timeout while polling submission status (NSURLErrorDomain -1001) -- a known, generally benign notarytool polling flake, not a real problem. A straight re-run succeeded.

Final wiring: tauri.conf.json's ad-hoc signingIdentity ("-") removed; tauri-build.yml's macOS leg now passes APPLE_CERTIFICATE, APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD, APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY, APPLE_TEAM_ID, APPLE_ID, APPLE_PASSWORD into the tauri-action build step, all as repo secrets. Verified on a feature branch first (tauri-macos-signing) before fast-forwarding into main once genuinely green, per Tom's own call to not touch main until proven. wigwag.work's "Desktop app" card text updated to drop the unsigned-build warning for macOS (Windows's stays, since Windows still has no signing cert of its own -- a separate, not-yet-started follow-up).

Problem: the column header menu and title-column menu (both driven by the same openColMenuId/toggleColMenu state) always anchored downward with no height cap, clipping when opened near the bottom of a short window (the motivating case: widget embeds).

Fixed by applying the EXACT same pattern toggleAddField already used successfully elsewhere in wigwag.html (computeAnchor's spaceBelow/spaceAbove, already a shared helper 'used by every popup this app renders' per its own comment) -- flip upward when space below < 280px and space above is more plentiful, cap height to whichever direction it opens in (8px margin, 120px floor), scroll internally rather than clip. Real bug caught in my own first attempt: both menu markup sites had a hardcoded overflow:hidden positioned AFTER the new computed style in their combined style attribute, silently overriding the new overflow-y:auto -- confirmed via getComputedStyle before/after fixing.
