history.value: Legacy per-field backfillProjectHistory entries use a bare fixed id -- two devices with differing un-migrated field defs would collide on merge

history.text:
Found as a side-discovery while fixing the project Notes merge bug (exported/imported projects weren't pulling in Notes changes -- root cause: Notes had no signed history at all, so merge just guessed 'keep local unless its empty'). Fix: Notes got the same treatment as the project name (field:__project_name__) -- a real, derivable, signed history entry on projectHistory (field:__project_notes__), merged via the same real three-way (diff3) path prose issue fields already get.

Backfilling a pre-existing project's Notes into this new history shape needed a synthesized 'legacy-backfill' entry, same as backfillProjectHistory already does for ordinary field definitions. For Notes I deliberately made that entry's id content-derived (hash of the actual Notes text), NOT the bare fixed string ('backfill-field-' + fieldId) the existing per-FIELD-DEF backfill already uses -- because two independent devices' Notes are very likely to have genuinely diverged before ever seeing this feature, and a fixed id would make unionByKey silently treat two DIFFERENT legacy Notes strings as 'the same entry', dropping one side's content outright on the very first merge.

That same latent risk already exists for the EXISTING per-field-def backfill (backfillProjectHistory's 'backfill-field-' + colId) -- it's just much less likely to bite in practice, since two legacy devices' own default/stock field definitions for the same built-in column are usually identical, whereas free-typed Notes text is not. Flagging it here rather than fixing it as a drive-by: it's pre-existing behaviour, out of scope for the Notes fix itself, and touching it risks a wider blast radius (existing tests may assert specific backfill-id values) that deserves its own look rather than a rushed side-effect.

history.value: Project Notes merges now diff3-reconcile properly, but aren't shown in the merge preview card or covered by 'Back out this update'

history.text:
Follow-up to the Notes-merge fix (tracker: 'exported a project and imported it on top of an older version -- it didn't pull in changes to the project Notes field'). Notes is now a real, derivable, signed-history value (field:__project_notes__ on projectHistory, same reserved-sentinel pattern as the project's own name) and a genuine divergence gets the real three-way (diff3) merge prose issue fields already get -- see docs/FORMAT.md's new 'A project's Notes field is also derived from a log' section.

Deliberately NOT done as part of that fix, to keep it scoped:
- The merge preview card (merge-card) doesn't show a row for Notes the way it shows one per touched issue field -- a Notes-only merge applies silently with no visual confirmation of what changed beyond the Notes panel itself.
- buildMergeIssueSummary/the local merge log (mergeIssueSummaries) is issue-scoped only -- a Notes merge-reconciliation entry is appended straight via appendProjectHistory, never recorded there, so 'Back out this update' has nothing to revert for Notes even when the rest of that same merge IS revertible.

Both are real UX gaps, not correctness bugs -- the underlying data is merged correctly either way. Scoping a real preview-card row + merge-log integration for a project-level (not per-issue) field properly is more design work than a drive-by fix, so flagging rather than rushing it.

history.value: Project Notes didn't merge on import -- promoted to a real, signed, diff3-mergeable history field (like the project name)

history.text:
Live-reported (Tom): "I just exported a project and imported it on top of an older version - it didn't pull in changes to the project Notes field."

Root cause: the project-level Notes field had zero signed history -- saveNoteEdit() just did a bare setState, and applyMergedIssues' own merge logic only ever adopted an incoming Notes value when the LOCAL copy's own Notes was currently empty. Any local content at all, however stale, permanently blocked a genuinely newer incoming value -- not a merge, a guess.

Fix: Notes is now promoted to a real, derivable, signed-history value, following the exact same reserved-sentinel pattern as the project's own name (tracker #149) -- field:__project_notes__ on projectHistory, deriveProjectNotes() picks the highest-sortKey entry, deriveFieldDefs excludes the sentinel. Because it's real history now, a genuine divergence between two copies gets the identical three-way (diff3) merge real prose (type:'text') issue fields already get, via the SAME computeMergeProseEntries (projectHistory is just treated as a pseudo-issue's own history -- no new merge algorithm needed). mergeHasRealChanges also checks for a genuine Notes divergence, so a file that changed only Notes still enables "Merge update" instead of looking like a no-op.

Deliberately scoped to the INTERACTIVE gate only (previewMerge/confirmPendingMerge -- file import, paste, "Apply update..."). startMerge's own silent/automatic path (every GitHub pull: initial connect, background poll) keeps applyMergedIssues' older "adopt into an empty slot only" guard completely untouched -- that guard is itself a deliberate fix for a real live incident (2026-09-07, "Project-level notes keep disappearing!") with its own explicit intent that a silent background poll must never inject unresolved conflict markers into Notes nobody's watching, nor clobber in-progress local editing. Verified both paths explicitly (tests/github-sync.spec.js's existing 'Project notes surviving a GitHub pull/push cycle' suite still passes unchanged).

Also fixed along the way: legacy backfill (a pre-existing project with non-empty projectNotes but no history entry yet) now uses a content-derived id, not a bare fixed string -- two independent legacy devices with DIFFERENT un-migrated Notes text would otherwise collide on id and silently drop one side's content on the very first merge between them. Filed the same latent risk for the pre-existing per-field-def backfill as a separate issue (#182, not touched here -- different blast radius, deserves its own look).

Docs: new 'A project's Notes field is also derived from a log' section in docs/FORMAT.md, mirroring the project-name section. Tests: 3 new cases in tests/project-notes.spec.js (genuine divergence -> diff3 merge; clean one-sided adoption; two independently-backfilled legacy devices don't collide). Full suite green.

Follow-up filed separately (#183): Notes merges aren't yet shown in the merge preview card or covered by 'Back out this update' -- correctness is fine, just no UI visibility yet.

history.value: Crash: a field definition with no label broke the whole table's render (live-reported on wigwag.work/app after an import)

history.text:
Live-reported (Tom): "I just killed an import on wigwag.work/app with an import which resulted in Root.renderVals(): can't access property 'trim', label is undefined".

Root cause, confirmed via a real repro (not guessed): computeHeaderCompression(label, width) in wigwag-core.js/wigwag.html calls label.trim() on its very first line with zero guard, and it's called unconditionally as computeHeaderCompression(def.label, width) for EVERY column header on every render. A field definition that lacks a .label key entirely crashes that one call -- but since it's inside the single column-building loop every OTHER column also runs through, the exception takes the WHOLE table's render down, not just that column. Confirmed: the page goes fully blank except the error line, and it recurs on every subsequent reload until the bad field is gone or the code tolerates it.

Fixed: label = label || ''; guard, same defensive pattern truncate() already uses elsewhere in the same file. A label-less column now renders with a blank (but fully interactive -- renameable from its own column menu) header instead of taking the app down. Commit 061f0f2.

Not yet fully closed: I haven't pinned down exactly HOW a field definition without a label got created in Tom's real case -- the normal UI paths (+ Add field, field rename) both guard against an empty name, so this likely came from an externally-authored, hand-edited, or otherwise non-standard imported .jsonl file. There's no schema validation on import at all today (fittingly, one of the built-in demo issues literally describes wanting exactly that: "Add JSONL schema validation on Import & merge"). Asked Tom whether he still has the file that triggered this, to nail the exact origin -- the crash itself is fixed regardless.
Won't do for now - if it comes back it comes back

history.value: Project comments didn't merge either -- same bug as Notes, fixed via union (not diff3)

history.text:
Follow-up Tom asked directly: 'Are there any remaining fields which are not full signed history?' -- the one remaining gap was projectComments (the project-level comment thread, separate from any issue's own comments).

Same crude pattern Notes had: applyMergedIssues only adopted an incoming file's projectComments when the local copy currently had ZERO project comments. Two copies that had each posted even one comment never merged on import -- whichever side imported kept only its own comments, permanently.

Each comment is already individually signed, so unlike Notes this didn't need a real diff3 pass -- just a proper unionByKey merge by commentKey, the same primitive issue-level commentStreams already use. Applied unconditionally for BOTH the interactive gate and startMerge's own silent path (GitHub sync, background polls) -- unlike Notes, a union of discrete comments is strictly additive with no 'surprise conflict marker in free text' risk, so there was no reason to withhold it from the silent path the way Notes' real-merge treatment is.

With this, every portable field is now backed by real signed history with correct merge behaviour: issues (values/fieldRefs/commentStreams -- all pre-existing), project name, project field definitions, project Notes (#184), and now project comments.

Tests: 3 new cases in tests/project-notes.spec.js. Full suite green (1009 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated flake). Commit 245737c.

history.value: Migrate the project doc + merge log from localStorage to IndexedDB (removes the 5MB Firefox quota ceiling)

history.text:
# Browser persistence migration: localStorage → IndexedDB for the project doc + merge log

## Context

A real user hit Firefox's localStorage-specific quota (a separate, older mechanism from the Storage API's disk-scaled quota — Firefox caps localStorage itself at 5MB by default via `dom.storage.default_quota`, confirmed via Mozilla Bugzilla). wigwag's history is append-only (every edit kept forever, each signed entry embedding its own ~180-byte inlined public key), so an actively-used project's own localStorage doc genuinely grows without bound. `persist()` (the save-on-every-edit function) hit `QuotaExceededError`, caught by a bare `console.warn` with **no user-visible indication** — edits looked like they worked but were never actually saved, silently lost on reload. The user's own real projects measured 2040KB and 1423KB; the app's own merge log hit 119KB.

Export-time code already dedupes repeated public keys into a shared registry (tracker #128), but that only applies to the exported `.jsonl` file — the live copy sitting in localStorage never gets that treatment. Tom, after understanding the real tradeoff (localStorage is synchronous by spec, which is *why* its quota is small and separate from IndexedDB's much larger async-backed one — not a policy knob, an architectural one), chose to do the real migration now rather than stack band-aids. This plan moves the two keys that actually grow unbounded — the per-project doc and the per-project merge log — onto IndexedDB, leaving everything else untouched.

**Decided with the user:**
- The silent-failure banner (loud warning on a genuinely failed save) ships as a **separate, later follow-up** — it's useful for the other 17 untouched localStorage keys too, and is better designed after real-device testing shows what IndexedDB-specific failures need surfacing.
- The render-path summary cache's brief "0/blank until the warm sweep reaches it" window for non-active projects right after a cold multi-project boot is **accepted as-is**, no loading affordance added for it.

## Scope decision

**Only `STORAGE_KEY`/`docKey()` (the per-project doc) and `MERGE_LOG_KEY_PREFIX` (the merge log) move to IndexedDB.** Every other key — `SECRETS_KEY`, `PROJECTS_KEY`, `IDENTITIES_KEY`, `COLUMN_WIDTHS_KEY`, `WRAP_KEY`, `COLUMN_ORDER_KEY`, `COLUMN_FILTERS_KEY`, `HIDDEN_FIELDS_KEY`, `LOCAL_FIELD_BINDINGS_KEY`, `COMMENT_READS_KEY`, `ISSUE_SUBSCRIPTIONS_KEY`, `MENTION_NOTIFICATIONS_KEY`, `NOTIFIED_MENTIONS_KEY`, `SNAPSHOT_INGESTED_KEY`, `EXPORT_TRUST_KEY`, `SESSION_PROJECT_KEY` (sessionStorage), device-id, appearance — stays on localStorage/sessionStorage, byte-identical to today. Measured real sizes put nearly all the bytes in exactly the two migrating keys; everything else is confirmed under 2.3KB with no unbounded-growth shape, so migrating it adds call-site/cross-tab-listener churn for zero quota benefit.

**The exported/pushed/pulled `.jsonl` file format is completely unaffected** — `buildSourceText`/`parseJsonl` (`wigwag-core.js`, also hand-inlined into wigwag.html's `window.WigwagCore` IIFE in the outer shell) already read/write from `this.state`, never localStorage directly. This migration touches zero functions that live in `wigwag-core.js` — no hand-sync of that inlined copy needed.

**Room Scoped Widget Mode is untouched.** It already shadows the bare `localStorage` identifier with an in-memory shim for exactly `PROJECTS_KEY` and `docKey(...)`-shaped keys (`isRoomModeContentKey()`) — that branch must keep doing exactly what it does today, never touching real localStorage *or* IndexedDB.

## Design

### IndexedDB schema
One database, `wigwag-docstore`, opened once per tab and memoized. Created in `onupgradeneeded` for version 1 (IndexedDB's own version number *is* the schema version — no second ad hoc version field):
- **`projectDocs`** — out-of-line keys (`store.put(doc, projectId)`), value is the exact same object shape `persist()`/`loadPersisted()` already produce/consume (`{fieldDefs, issues, projectHistory, githubRepo, githubRepoPath, githubRepoBranch, githubTokenOverride, projectNotes, projectComments}`).
- **`mergeLogs`** — out-of-line keys, key = `mergeLogStorageKey(this.storagePrefKey(projectId))` (keeps the existing Room-Mode-aware composite-key convention), value = the same capped-200-entry array.
- **`meta`** — bookkeeping only, used for migration-in state (below).

Write a small promise-based wrapper directly inside wigwag.html's Layer-2 `text/x-dc` script (`openWigwagDb()`, `idbGetDoc`/`idbPutDoc`/`idbDeleteDoc`, `idbGetMergeLog`/`idbPutMergeLog`, `idbGetMeta`/`idbPutMeta`) — **not** in `wigwag-core.js`, which is also `require()`'d directly by `wigwag-cli.js`/`wigwag-core.test.js` in plain Node with no DOM and must never gain an `indexedDB` dependency. Wire `db.onversionchange` → `db.close()` now as cheap insurance for a future schema bump.

### The `docStore` abstraction (keeps Room Mode untouched)
Every one of the 21 `docKey` + 2 `mergeLogStorageKey` call sites goes through one indirection, uniformly `async` regardless of branch:

```js
const docStore = {
  async getDoc(projectId) {
    if (ROOM_MODE_CAPABILITIES) { const raw = localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY + ':' + projectId); return raw ? JSON.parse(raw) : null; }
    return idbGetDoc(projectId);
  },
  async putDoc(projectId, doc) { /* same branch shape */ },
  async deleteDoc(projectId) { /* same branch shape */ },
  async getMergeLog(prefKey) { /* same branch shape */ },
  async putMergeLog(prefKey, log) { /* same branch shape */ }
};
```
Room Mode's branch is today's existing code, just wrapped in a resolved Promise. If `tests/matrix-host.spec.js` ever fails during this work, that's an immediate signal the branching is wrong — not that Room Mode's actual behavior changed.

### One-time migration-in (existing users)
On boot, for **every** project id in `PROJECTS_KEY`'s milestone list (not just the active one — real users have several):
1. Skip if `meta.migrationState[id]` already marks it done.
2. If `projectDocs` has no record for `id` and `localStorage.getItem(docKey(id))` is present, parse it and `idbPutDoc(id, doc)`.
3. **Read it back and compare** before marking anything done — never assume a write succeeded.
4. Same copy+verify for that project's merge log.
5. **Don't delete the localStorage copies yet.** Given this whole migration exists *because* a silent-failure bug already shipped once, delete only after (a) the IndexedDB write is read-back-verified **and** (b) a *subsequent* boot has independently re-loaded that project successfully from IndexedDB too (`meta.migrationState[id] = 'verified-twice'`). One redundant localStorage copy lingering an extra session is a fine price for not repeating the same class of mistake.

Runs as part of the new async boot path below, gated behind `localDocLoading` so it never races first render.

### Boot sequence
Reuse the exact pattern Room Mode's `roomModeBootstrapping` already establishes (confirmed directly in the decoded source: `if (s.roomModeBootstrapping) return { bootOverlayVisible: ..., ... }` in `renderVals()`, backed by the existing `data-testid=boot-splash` component). Add a parallel `localDocLoading` boolean (Local Mode only — Room Mode keeps its own gate, never sets this one):
- Constructor: set `localDocLoading: true` in Local Mode, then kick off (not await) an async `finishBootSequenceAsync()` that runs migration-in, `await docStore.getDoc(projectId)` in place of today's synchronous `loadPersisted()` body, the merge-log load, then `setState({ ...patch, localDocLoading: false })`.
- `renderVals()`: `if (s.localDocLoading) return { ...identical boot-overlay shape as the roomModeBootstrapping branch... }`, immediately alongside the existing check.
- Everything else in `runBootSequence()` (identities, project index, secrets, etc.) stays exactly as synchronous as today — only the doc/merge-log load moves.

`switchProject(id, after)` keeps its external signature unchanged; internally, `await docStore.getDoc(id)` replaces the synchronous read, then today's same big `setState({...}, after)`. No new loading UI for this in the first cut — a single doc read is sub-tens-of-milliseconds even at ~2MB; add a skeleton only if Phase 5's real-device pass shows it's actually needed.

### `persist()` — conflict dance, async-ified
Port the existing read-compare-write dance onto a single IndexedDB `readwrite` transaction (get → compare `issues` against `_docIssuesBaseline[projectId]` exactly as today → either `put()` or bail into `adoptExternalIssues`). IndexedDB's atomicity tightens the race (today's `getItem`+`setItem` are two separate non-transactional calls) but does **not** obsolete the baseline-compare policy itself — "issues specifically defer to disk, other fields don't" is an application decision the storage engine can't make for us.

**New requirement**: `componentDidUpdate()` calls `persist()` unconditionally on every render, and `persist()` is now async — rapid renders could call it again before a prior transaction resolves. Serialize with a chained promise: `this._persistChain = (this._persistChain || Promise.resolve()).then(() => this._persistOnce()).catch(e => console.warn('[tracker] failed to save state:', e))`. This has no synchronous equivalent today and needs its own new test.

### Cross-tab sync: BroadcastChannel for the two migrated keys only
The single `storage` event listener keeps handling everything else (`PROJECTS_KEY`, `IDENTITIES_KEY`, column widths/order/wrap/filters, sort, local field bindings) completely untouched. Add one `BroadcastChannel('wigwag:docsync')` per tab (same setup/teardown points as the existing listener):
- `persist()` success → `postMessage({ type: 'doc-saved', projectId, doc })`.
- `recordMergeLog` → `postMessage({ type: 'merge-log-appended', projectId, log })`.
- `deleteProject` → `postMessage({ type: 'doc-deleted', projectId })`.

Extract the current `_onStorageEvent` doc-key branch's body (hydrate + `setState` + `checkForNewMentions`/`checkForSubscribedIssueUpdates`) into a shared `_applyRemoteDocUpdate(doc)`, called from the channel's `onmessage` when `data.projectId === this.state.projectId`. That old docKey branch becomes dead code once nothing writes that key to real localStorage. For a **non-active** project's message, update the summary cache only (below) — no render needed unless a surface showing other-project info is currently visible.

BroadcastChannel doesn't deliver to its own sending context (matching `storage`'s existing non-self-delivery) and has no replay for a tab opened after the fact — covered by the boot-time warm sweep below, not relied on for history.

### Render-path summary cache (for the methods that read *other* projects synchronously during render)
`resolveWigwagRef`, `buildGlobalSearchIndex`, `projectGithubRepo`/`projectGithubRepoInfo`, and the mobile-sheet helpers `mobileIssueCountFor`/`mobileRepoFor` read non-active projects' full docs synchronously, inline, during render — render can't `await`, and converting these to per-cell async sub-components would be a much larger blast radius. Keep an in-memory `this._projectSummaries = { [projectId]: { issueCount, githubRepo, githubRepoPath, githubRepoBranch, issues: [{id, title}] } }`:
- **Active project**: updated synchronously the instant `persist()`'s write succeeds — zero staleness, ever, for the common case.
- **Other projects, at boot**: a background warm sweep (after `localDocLoading` clears, not gating render) reads each project once via `docStore.getDoc`.
- **Thereafter**: kept warm by the same `doc-saved`/`doc-deleted` broadcasts, reusing that channel for a second purpose at near-zero extra cost.
- **Re-sweep on visibility**: piggyback on the existing `document.visibilitychange` → `onBecameVisible()` hook as insurance against a missed broadcast.

Accepted (per discussion with Tom): immediately after a cold, large, multi-project boot, a surface reading a project the sweep hasn't reached yet sees `{issueCount: 0, githubRepo: '', issues: []}`, self-correcting within moments — degrades to `resolveWigwagRef`'s existing "not found yet" fallback shape, not a new failure mode, but still worth a dedicated test (below) rather than assuming it's fine.

### Silent-failure banner
Explicitly **out of scope for this work** — filed as its own tracker follow-up once this ships, scoped to cover both the new IndexedDB path and the 17 untouched localStorage keys with one shared mechanism.

## Phased sequencing

1. **Groundwork** — `docStore`/IndexedDB wrapper + migration-in routine written and verified in isolation (disposable Playwright script per `docs/EDITING.md`), not yet wired into any real call site.
2. **Schema + migration-in as a shadow copy** — wired into boot; every existing read/write keeps using localStorage unchanged (IndexedDB populated but unused). New `tests/indexeddb-migration.spec.js`: fresh profile with populated legacy localStorage → byte-identical record per project after boot; a second boot doesn't redo/duplicate the copy; an existing IndexedDB record isn't clobbered by a stale localStorage copy.
3. **Flip the active project's path to IndexedDB** — `docStore` wiring for `persist`/`loadPersisted`/`switchProject`/`deleteProject`/`createBlankProject`/`importParsedAsNewProject`/`connectRemoteFinish`/`attachRemoteToProject`/`ingestEmbeddedSnapshotIfPresent`/`bootstrapFirstProjectIfNeeded`, the `localDocLoading` gate, the persist() serialization queue, the transaction-based conflict dance, merge log via `docStore`. **This is the phase that fixes the actual production bug.** Must land together with the test-harness updates below (same phase, not split later). Verify: `tests/local-persistence.spec.js` (staleness-guard contract) unchanged; `tests/boot-splash.spec.js` (reappears on reload; never shown in Room Mode); `tests/matrix-host.spec.js` unchanged (confirms Room Mode's branch untouched); new serialization-queue test (rapid same-tab edits land in call order).
4. **BroadcastChannel cross-tab sync** — `tests/cross-tab-sync.spec.js` passes unchanged (the explicit named contract), plus a new echo-loop test instrumenting `BroadcastChannel.postMessage` the way the existing column-width test instruments `localStorage.setItem`.
5. **Render-path summary cache** — `tests/global-search.spec.js` (incl. the existing large-project responsiveness test, which validates reading from memory not storage), `tests/wigwag-links.spec.js`, `tests/mobile.spec.js`'s `M2: switcher sheet` block. New tests: cold-boot transient-empty-then-corrects behavior; a doc saved in tab A updating tab B's mobile switcher count live without switching into that project.
6. **Real-device/Tauri/Safari verification** — no code changes expected. Confirm on real Firefox the original bug (2MB+ project, `QuotaExceededError`) is actually fixed. Check Safari (historically has IndexedDB private-browsing quirks — genuinely unverified here) and the Tauri build on each real target webview (zero existing storage overrides, zero prior verification).
7. **Cleanup** — lazy localStorage deletion per the "verified twice" rule; file the silent-failure-banner follow-up; update `docs/FORMAT.md`/`docs/EDITING.md` if the new code's location needs a mention.

## Test-harness migration (its own workstream, lands with phase 3)

Most seeding uses `page.addInitScript(...)`, which runs before the page's own scripts and relies on synchronous localStorage. **Leave all `addInitScript` seeding on localStorage exactly as today** — the app's own migration-in logic absorbs it into IndexedDB during boot, which also makes every test run a live regression test of migration-in itself. Only **post-boot** direct reads/writes (tests simulating "another tab changed this directly," or asserting on persisted state after an interaction) need new async IndexedDB helpers in `tests/helpers.js` (`idbGetProjectDoc`/`idbSetProjectDoc`/`idbGetMergeLog`, via `page.evaluate(async (...) => {...})`), then a sweep of the specs with their own inline post-boot `localStorage.getItem/setItem('git_native_tracker_v1:...')`/merge-log calls: `comment-stream-fields`, `data-structures`, `deep-links`, `external-auth`, `github-sync`, `identities`, `identity-attribution`, `interaction`, `issue-deletion`, `issue-field`, `local-persistence`, `matrix-host`, `mentions`, `merge-provenance`, `milestones`, `row-selection`, `wigwag-links`.

## Risks and unknowns (real, not papered over)

- **Safari IndexedDB quirks** — unverified here; historically had private-browsing restrictions and cross-tab bugs. Phase 6, not assumed fine.
- **Tauri desktop parity** — zero existing storage overrides anywhere in `src-tauri/`, zero prior verification against any real OS-native webview. Phase 6, not assumed fine.
- **Summary-cache eventual consistency** is a genuine (accepted) UX regression from today's always-synchronously-correct reads.
- **The 17-spec-file test migration is a large, mechanical surface that must land in the same phase as the active-project path flip** — splitting it later leaves a broken suite with no real signal.
- **IndexedDB transactions tighten but don't eliminate the baseline-compare logic** — ports over, doesn't disappear.
- **BroadcastChannel has no replay** — covered by the boot-time warm sweep + visibility re-sweep, not the channel alone.

## Critical files
- `/workspace/wigwag.html` — the only place the actual change happens (decode/patch/re-encode per `docs/EDITING.md`; `Component` class's `persist`/`loadPersisted`/`switchProject`/`docKey`/`_onStorageEvent`/`renderVals`/`buildGlobalSearchIndex`/`resolveWigwagRef`/merge-log methods, plus the new `docStore`/IndexedDB wrapper code)
- `/workspace/docs/EDITING.md` — mandatory decode/patch/re-encode/verify procedure for every wigwag.html change
- `/workspace/tests/cross-tab-sync.spec.js`, `/workspace/tests/local-persistence.spec.js` — the two explicit must-keep-passing behavioral contracts
- `/workspace/tests/helpers.js` — central seeding/reading helpers used by 17+ spec files; needs new async IndexedDB helpers
- `/workspace/tests/boot-splash.spec.js`, `/workspace/tests/mobile.spec.js`, `/workspace/tests/global-search.spec.js`, `/workspace/tests/wigwag-links.spec.js`, `/workspace/tests/matrix-host.spec.js` — regression targets for the boot gate, summary cache, and Room Mode isolation
- `/workspace/wigwag-core.js` — confirmed unaffected; must stay that way (no `indexedDB` dependency ever belongs here, it's `require()`'d in plain Node by `wigwag-cli.js`/`wigwag-core.test.js`)

## Verification

history.value: Markdown rendering throws InternalError and loses content on an unusually large single-field value (multi-MB, no whitespace)

history.text:
Found while verifying tracker #187 (localStorage -> IndexedDB migration) Phase 6 against real Firefox. Not a regression from that migration -- unrelated to storage, purely a rendering issue.

Repro: in a real Firefox instance, edit a multiline markdown field (tried with "Mitigation" on the demo fixture) to contain a single ~6MB value with no whitespace breaks (e.g. 'x'.repeat(6*1024*1024)), commit it, then reload the page. Observed:
- A console error during/after the edit: `{"name":"InternalError"}` (Firefox's InternalError class typically means "too much recursion" -- likely a regex backtracking or recursive-descent issue in the markdown renderer when it hits an extremely long unbroken token).
- Reload took ~29s (vs ~1.5s normally) for just this one field.
- After reload, the field's content did not survive -- came back empty/different, where the SAME scenario with a plain non-markdown field (tried with "Title") was clean: no console error, ~1.5s reload, full value intact.

So this is specific to markdown rendering of an extreme single-token value, not to storage -- the edit DID land correctly in IndexedDB (confirmed by reading it back before reload); the loss happens on the markdown-render path during the next render/reload.

Severity is probably low in practice -- real content this large in one field with zero whitespace is an unusual edge case, not normal usage -- but worth a look since it's a silent content-loss bug once triggered, with no visible error to the user. Didn't investigate the renderer's actual code path for this (out of scope for #187), just isolated that it's markdown-specific via the A/B above.

Root-caused and fixed. renderMarkdownInline bare-email regex, /[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9-]+(?:.[A-Za-z0-9-]+)+/g, catastrophically backtracks against a long run of local-part-shaped characters with no "@" anywhere: every ordinary alnum char is both a valid match char for the unbounded + AND a valid restart position for the same expensive backtrack, so a failed match at one offset repeats in full at the next -- O(n^2). Confirmed empirically: 50K characters alone hangs well past a minute; the real 6MB case is the same mechanism at scale. That matches your Firefox InternalError exactly (SpideryMonkey surfaces pathological backtracking as that specific error, not just a hang).

Bounded the local-part quantifier to 64 chars (RFC 5321s own local-part limit, so every real address still matches) -- restores linear-time scanning, confirmed 1.4s at the full 6MB size. Checked the adjacent Matrix-id regex for the same shape -- not vulnerable, its mandatory leading @ is excluded from its own body class so it cannot restart into the same expensive backtrack.

Fixed in wigwag-core.js, synced into wigwag.html, a timeout-based unit test added (fails if the bound ever regresses) plus a real-UI Playwright test reproducing the exact field-edit-and-reload scenario. Committed 952ba77, full suite clean (1078 passed, 2 pre-existing unrelated flakes, independently re-verified including one via git stash).

Still open from the original report: exactly how a user would end up with a single 6MB no-whitespace value in a real field is unusual -- the fix makes it safe regardless of how it got there, so Im not chasing that origin question further unless you have a concrete real-world case in mind.

history.value: Bulk-link issues from a multi-line paste (design_handoff_bulk_link_issues/bulk_issues.zip)

history.text:
Plan, posted before implementation starts.

Spec: design_handoff_bulk_link_issues/Bulk Link Issues.dc.html + its README (from bulk_issues.zip). Today, pasting a single Jira key/GitHub URL/Salesforce record URL/wigwag link into the add-item bar links one row's title to it; anything else becomes plain text. This extends that same per-line matching to a multi-line paste, with a review/breakdown step first and duplicate detection against the whole project.

Two corrections to the design brief found during exploration, both already resolved:
- No "locked title" mechanism exists today for a linked title (isFieldLocked/lockTitle are about the separate Bound-source rule system, confirmed in buildTextCell) -- not a blocker, bulk-created rows reuse the exact same apply*LinkToField calls as today, so whatever rendering already applies carries over for free.
- The "should other fields pre-fill from the linked issue" open question: confirmed applyGithubLinkToField/applyJiraLinkToField/applySalesforceLinkToField/applyWigwagLinkToField each already call applyLinkedRules/applyLiveLinkedRules themselves (the existing Bound-source auto-population) -- since bulk creation reuses these unchanged per line, bound fields populate automatically with zero new code.

Mobile phone viewport is explicitly out of scope -- the design brief's own frame set (1a-1d) only covers desktop + the Matrix-widget variant.

Implementation:
1. Extract addIssue's per-line matching/creation logic into a new createIssueFromText(text), with addIssue becoming a one-line requireAttribution wrapper around it -- lets bulk-creation gate attribution ONCE for the whole batch, not once per row.
2. New onAddItemPaste handler on both add-item-input and widget-add-item-input (neither has any paste handler today) -- reads clipboardData directly, preventDefault()s and switches into a new "N lines pasted" preview state when the paste has more than one non-empty line; single-line paste is completely unaffected.
3. New buildBulkPasteViewModel(lines, state) pure function (recomputed fresh every render, same pattern as the existing buildMergeGateViewModel for the merge-review modal) -- runs the same match precedence as createIssueFromText, classifies each line as linked/unlinked/duplicate (duplicate via a new refsMatch() helper against every existing issue's already-hydrated fieldRefs, or exact title match for unlinked lines -- no such cross-issue dedup helper exists yet, this is genuinely new code).
4. New breakdown modal (own state/testids, following the merge-review modal's established bespoke-modal pattern, NOT the single-message confirmAction) -- three outcome groups with two "Show list" expansions, Cancel/Add-N footer.
5. Widget variant: the add-row grows a trailing summary clause; tapping it opens an itemised popover as a 6th computeAnchor() call site (fully generic utility, this is the established per-site pattern already used by 5 other popovers in the file).

New test file tests/bulk-paste-issues.spec.js, using the same real-clipboard-paste pattern already established by h.pasteText (not .fill(), which never fires a paste event). Full suite run before committing, checked against the known baseline flakes.

Done and committed (3400380).

Implemented per the plan posted earlier: createIssueFromText extracted out of addIssue, new onAddItemPaste handler on both add-item-input and widget-add-item-input (neither had one before), classification/dedup logic (classifyBulkPasteLines/buildBulkPasteViewModel, recomputed fresh every render like the merge-gate), a new breakdown modal following the merge-review modal's bespoke pattern, and the widget's collapsed summary + popover (6th computeAnchor call site).

One real bug found and fixed during testing -- not a template quirk, a genuine mistake in my own first patch: the widget's new conditional branches ate the outer !isSelecting wrapper's own closing tag, silently nesting the row-selection bulk-action-bar inside it so it became unreachable while selecting rows. Caught via two real widget-body-4a.spec.js regressions, confirmed against a safe git-show baseline (passed there, failed on my change) before fixing -- not dismissed as a flake.

Confirmed bound-field auto-population (a field with a Bound-source rule, pulling from the newly-linked remote data) already works for bulk-created rows with zero new code -- applyGithubLinkToField/etc. already call applyLinkedRules/applyLiveLinkedRules themselves, and bulk creation reuses those exact functions unchanged. Verified directly in a real browser: a bulk-linked GitHub issue correctly got a derived "Type" field value from the fetched data.

Also added "Show list" -> "Hide list" once expanded, per a follow-up request mid-build -- same dynamic-label convention the merge modal's own timeline toggle already uses.

New tests/bulk-paste-issues.spec.js (7 tests) + a new h.pasteMultilineIntoAddItem test helper. Full suite: 1024 passed, 1 pre-existing baseline flake, no regressions.

Mobile phone viewport stays out of scope, as the design brief's own frame set (1a-1d) only ever covered desktop + the Matrix-widget variant.
