history.value: Revertible merges and refreshes via deletion, plus field-type immutability

history.text:
Plan, posted before implementation starts. This started as "bundle refreshes into something revertible like real merges already are" and, through genuine back-and-forth, ended up revising how "Back out this update" itself works for BOTH merges and refreshes.

Core conclusion: both should be revertible by literally DELETING the specific entries they introduced -- not appending a corrective entry (today's mechanism), not redacting in place. This is safe specifically because mergeLog is already local-only and never exported (confirmed: tests/merge-provenance.spec.js asserts this directly) -- the "looks like it never existed" resurrection risk real issue-deletion tombstoning exists to prevent (tracker #149) is about something absent from a SHARED channel being silently reintroduced by a replay that doesn't know it was deliberately removed. A local-only action was never shared in the first place. A future re-merge of the same original source isn't a silent resurrection either -- dedup is presence-based, so it just goes through the full review gate again, visibly.

Also concluded: revert works UNCONDITIONALLY, any age, no gate on "has this been shared elsewhere since" (deliberately rejected as unbuildable -- wigwag can know its own push/export completed, never whether anything was actually received downstream; that's a user-education problem, not a technical one, deferred separately) -- and no per-field "has this changed since" safety check either, since that check only ever protected against APPEND-based clobbering (a new entry is always "latest" by construction); deletion of a non-latest, already-superseded entry is inert on current derived state either way, so there's no failure mode left to guard against.

Plan:
1. Field type immutability: lock deriveFieldDefs's `type` to the field's FIRST-ever definition entry, ignoring type in any later one (small, standalone, confirmed the UI already never offers changing it).
2. New latestEntryIdsByField(issue) helper + before/after diffing in both refreshField and applyComputedMerge/buildMergeIssueSummary -- captures derived/bound-field side effects automatically (confirmed neither path currently reverts those, since nothing re-triggers applyLinkedRules on a plain history mutation). Also fixes applyWigwagLinkToField's missing before/after check (it currently always appends, unlike the other three systems).
3. recordMergeLog's signature changes to take `source` directly (was derived internally from inboundInfo.envelope) -- one real-merge call site builds its own envelope source, a new refresh call site builds `{kind: 'refresh'}`. Same storage/cap/broadcast plumbing either way.
4. New unconditional-deletion revert function replacing rollbackMerge's append-based body -- every field in a record gets its resultEntryId entry deleted outright, always. fieldStillSafeToRevert/computeMergeRollbackEntries left in place but unused by this path.
5. Merge History panel: a refresh-kind display branch (no envelope/sig-glyph nonsense), live-resolved origin text per field, copy updates, revertedAt gating so an already-backed-out record can't be re-reverted.

Explicitly out of scope, filed as a SEPARATE future issue once this lands: typed history events, and snapshotting resolved field/option labels at signing time (the fix for label-rename drift -- ruled out "schema as of time T" as a fix, since it's just as vulnerable to merge-driven sortKey reshuffling as deriving from current schema is).

Shipped (417d297). All five plan items landed:

1. Field-type immutability: deriveFieldDefs locks `type` to the field's earliest definition entry, in both wigwag.html and wigwag-core.js.
2. latestEntryIdsByField(issue) added; refreshField/applyWigwagLinkToField and applyComputedMerge/buildMergeIssueSummary now diff before/after to bundle every field a merge or refresh actually touched -- confirmed via real-browser testing that a refresh which also recomputes a bound field (title linked to GitHub, type bound to it) bundles BOTH into the same record, and reverting deletes both and falls the derived field back correctly.
3. recordMergeLog takes an explicit source; a refresh now records {kind: 'refresh'}, a real merge keeps the existing envelope shape.
4. rollbackMerge rewritten to delete every entry a bundle introduced, unconditionally -- no more per-field 'changed since merge' refusal. Verified: reverting a field that's been edited again since is now a safe no-op (the superseded entry is tidied up, visible value untouched) rather than a hidden button.
5. Merge History panel: canRevert no longer hides the button just because something moved on (that was the OLD append-era safety gate fighting the new unconditional design -- found and fixed during verification, not in the original plan text); a refresh-kind record gets its own display branch (no envelope/hash chip, 'Refreshed N linked field(s)', refresh-appropriate provenance copy); confirm-dialog copy rewritten to describe deletion, not the old append behavior it was still describing.

Also added a distinct 'Backed out.' label for an already-reverted record instead of it looking identical to 'nothing was ever revertable'.

tests/merge-provenance.spec.js: both existing revert-flow tests updated for delete-based assertions (one of which exposed a test-baseline bug of my own, not an app bug -- buildRagOverlap gives local its own pre-merge edit before the merge happens, so the revert baseline has to be captured after that, not before); added a new test for a refresh's revertible bundle including derived-field capture.

Full suite: 1025 passed, 1 failed (mentions.spec.js:307, the confirmed pre-existing first-connect flake) -- no new failures.

Filing the deferred typed-events/label-snapshotting idea as its own issue now.

Follow-up shipped (ce2e460): refresh-bundle merge-log records are now genuinely signed with this identity's own key, the same way a real export/merge already is -- completing the original 'reframe refreshes as signed merges' framing this issue opened with.

bulkRefreshSelected builds a real signed envelope (buildExportEnvelope/verifyExportEnvelope/classifyExportProvenance/fingerprintPublicKey, unchanged, same ECDSA identity key used everywhere else) over just the entries the refresh actually introduced, not the whole project -- hashing/signing the full project on every refresh click would be real cost for no benefit. recordMergeLog no longer treats refresh as envelope-less; a refresh's source now carries the same envelope fields a real merge's does, tagged kind:'refresh'.

Merge History panel now shows a genuine 'signed' glyph and a real records/hash chip for a refresh, same as a real merge -- previously suppressed since there was nothing real to show. Revert is unaffected (it never looked at source for its deletion logic).

Verified via the real UI (data-sig-state="signed", a real content hash, revert still deletes exactly the attested entries) and a new assertion in tests/merge-provenance.spec.js. Full suite: 1024 passed, 2 failed -- the confirmed mentions.spec.js first-connect flake, and a NEW matrix-host.spec.js full-suite-only timing flake (re-verified 3/3 in isolation and 3/3 against git stash of this commit, confirmed unrelated/pre-existing, not a regression).

history.value: Typed history events + snapshot resolved field/option labels at signing time

history.text:
Surfaced while designing #196's revertible-merge/refresh deletion mechanism, but deliberately kept separate -- not a prerequisite for that work, and materially larger.

Two related gaps in the current history-entry model:

1. Typed history events: entries are narrative-only (text + value), so anything structured a feature wants to attach has nowhere principled to go. (Came up while confirming deletion-based revert only needs to know entry ids, nothing about entry typing -- which it doesn't, but the gap itself is real and will likely bite the next feature that wants structured per-entry data.)

2. Snapshotting resolved field/option labels at signing time: an entry's displayed text currently resolves against CURRENT fieldDefs/option labels, so a later rename retroactively changes how old entries read. Considered 'resolve against schema as of time T' as a fix and ruled it out -- it's just as vulnerable to merge-driven sortKey reshuffling as deriving from current schema is (a merge can insert an earlier-sortKey schema change after the fact, changing what 'as of time T' even means for an entry that's already been signed and sent). The real fix is snapshotting the resolved label INSIDE the entry at signing time, which needs the typed-events work above to have a principled place to put it.

Both need a real design pass of their own: migration story for existing untyped entries, what the signing payload shape change does to signature verification of already-signed history, and how much (if any) of this needs to be backward-compatible with the current JSONL format per docs/FORMAT.md.

history.value: Rework bulk refresh: rate-limit/failure tolerance, atomic merge-gated apply, visible progress

history.text:
Triggered by a real failure: a ~70-issue bulk refresh got stuck -- one issue stuck on 'Loading...' and the whole operation never completed. Plausible mechanism, not yet confirmed: bulkRefreshSelected/refreshRow run sequentially (one await per row, in a plain for loop), with no timeout, no retry, and no rate-limit handling on the underlying GitHub/Jira/Salesforce fetch -- a single hung or rate-limited request blocks every row behind it indefinitely, with no visible explanation to the user.

Tom's requirements for the rework (verbatim from chat):
- Make refresh processing tolerant of rate limits and failures (presumably: timeouts, retry/backoff, and a way to report a per-row failure instead of hanging forever).
- Make the whole thing atomic: PREPARE the refresh as a merge first (fetch everything, compute the bundle), then APPLY it as one step -- not today's partial-as-you-go behavior, where a failure partway through can leave some rows refreshed and others not with no clear boundary.
- Make progress visible: a non-modal progress bar while the fetch/prepare phase runs, not just cells silently flipping from 'Loading...' to resolved one by one with no sense of overall progress or whether it's stuck.
- Flow: select rows -> click Refresh -> non-modal progress bar while fetching/preparing -> when ready, a merge-style gate to review and apply (or decline).
- Threshold: refreshing exactly 1 row should NOT go through a merge gate (refresh it directly, like today) -- more than 1 row should bundle as a reviewable merge. (This also means the single-row and multi-row paths diverge more than they do today, where both already funnel through the same recordMergeLog/mergeIssueSummaries bundle -- tracker #196/#197's signed-envelope work -- just without a prepare/apply split or a review gate.)

Status: Tom is sharing this with Claude Design before implementation starts -- NOT ready to build yet. This issue exists to hold the requirements and the triggering bug report, not as a go-ahead. Leaving at Todo; will pick a plan back up once design input comes back.

Plan, posted before implementation starts.

Root cause confirmed in the actual code: refreshRow/bulkRefreshSelected run strictly sequentially with zero timeout anywhere (no AbortController/AbortSignal in the whole app) and zero rate-limit handling (no 403/429/Retry-After handling at all) -- a hung or rate-limited fetch blocks every row behind it indefinitely, and today's refresh applies each row's change live as it resolves, so a stuck batch leaves the grid genuinely half-updated.

Design decision confirmed with Tom during planning: the handoff's mockup showed per-issue Retry/Skip buttons INSIDE the merge-review modal. But that modal is all-or-nothing by an explicit prior decision baked into the code ('nothing here is ever a per-field choice'). Tom's call: keep the gate 100% unmodified -- all retry/backoff happens automatically during fetch, before anything is ever shown; a row still failing after retries is excluded from the merge and reported separately ('93 ready, 2 could not be fetched'), re-select + refresh again to retry.

Architecture:
1. New state.refreshJobs: {[projectId]: RefreshJob}, following the existing globalSearchOpen precedent (a state field deliberately excluded from switchProject's reset list) so a job survives navigating to a different project. The job's own fetch/compute pipeline operates against a docStore.getDoc(projectId) snapshot, never live state directly, so it works identically whether or not its project is active.
2. Split each apply*LinkToField's fetch-and-write into a pure stage* function (fetch + compute, returns {entries, failed}, writes nothing) plus the existing write logic reused unchanged at commit time. The recompute layer (applyLinkedRules/computeDerivedChangeEntries) is already pure -- confirmed directly in the code, no changes needed there.
3. Timeout (AbortController, ~15s) + automatic retry with backoff (up to 3 attempts) on 403/429/5xx/timeout; 404 fails fast. Sequential, not parallel -- parallelizing would make rate-limiting worse, and sequential-with-timeout already bounds the stuck-forever case.
4. 1 row: still applies directly (too fast to review), just through the new timeout/retry-wrapped fetch. 2+ rows: stage everything into a job first, touching nothing live, then synthesize the exact same pendingMerge shape previewMerge already builds and hand it to the completely unmodified merge gate (confirmPendingMerge/applyComputedMerge/cancelPendingMerge).
5. New BroadcastChannel message type (refresh-job-updated) so the job's progress reaches every open tab regardless of which project is active there. A header chip (new UI, global/non-project-scoped like the existing search icon) tracks it; the selection bar's existing two-sibling add-item/bulk-bar toggle gains a third progress state, gated on selection being present (not the job's lifetime) per the handoff's explicit correction. One job per project at a time.

Full plan with exact file:line references is in this session's plan file. Starting implementation now.

Shipped (c708b45). Built per the plan posted earlier, with two real bugs found and fixed via your own manual testing after the initial implementation.

Core mechanism: bulk refresh now fetches and computes everything into an in-memory job first -- nothing in the grid changes until every row has resolved (or been excluded after exhausting retries), then the existing merge-review gate takes over, completely unmodified except two small additive touches (the prose-entry write loop now threads fieldRef/origin through; the gate's settled-value preview reads a refresh row's own fetched value instead of the not-yet-patched mergedIssue.values). 1 row still applies directly, same as before, just through the new timeout/retry-wrapped fetch.

Rate-limit/failure tolerance: every fetch is wrapped in a timeout (fixes the actual stuck-forever bug) plus automatic retry with backoff on 403/429/5xx/timeout; 404 fails fast. A row still failing after retries is excluded from the merge and reported via the job summary, not logged to that issue's history -- your own explicit call, since the merge gate is all-or-nothing by a prior deliberate decision and extending it for per-row retry/skip (as the handoff's mockup showed) would have meant revising that.

New UI: the selection bar's existing add-item/bulk-bar toggle gains a third state (progress), gated on selection being present not the job's lifetime -- clearing the selection reverts the slot immediately while the job keeps running. A new header chip (global, survives navigation and project switching) tracks every job across every project, with a popover and 'Review' that jumps back to wherever a completed job is waiting.

Your own manual testing caught two real bugs my own verification missed, both fixed:
1. A bound field that also carries a copied fieldRef (Remedy, copy-field-bound to Issue) was being refreshed TWICE -- once as if independently linked, again via the derived-recompute diff. Fixed: bound fields are now excluded from the independent-refresh loop entirely.
2. The timeline's 'N edits across both copies' label always read '0 edits' for a refresh-sourced record, since it checked properties (localEntryIds/incomingEntryIds) that only a real cross-identity merge sets. Fixed to recognize a refresh-sourced row the same way the per-row edit count already did.

Both reproduced via the real UI matching your exact structure (GitHub-linked Issue, Remedy bound via copy-field) and covered by new durable tests.

Full suite: 1028 passed, 2 failed -- both confirmed pre-existing baseline flakes (mentions.spec.js first-connect, github-sync debounced-push pushCount), no new failures.

Follow-up fix: the bound-field cascade now settles fully from every trigger, not just refresh (per Tom's "do the full cascade" call).

Two real gaps found and fixed, both pre-existing (not specific to refresh):

1. computeBoundValue refused to re-run ANY rule whose linked source's fieldRef lacked the maximalist shape -- but a "copy field" fieldRef is ALWAYS the trimmed form, so this blocked any field bound to another bound field, even when the rule never reads source.* at all. Added ruleNeedsSourceData to detect that structurally; the conservative fallback now only applies when the rule genuinely needs live source data.

2. settleLinkedRules (built to settle a cascade to a fixed point) was refresh-only. Promoted it to a shared Layer-1 function and swapped it into all 9 call sites that recompute bound fields -- manual edits, every link type's resolve path, merge landing -- so a multi-hop chain cascades correctly regardless of trigger. The existing field-count bound still guarantees termination on a cyclic binding.

3. Found while reproducing Tom's live report directly: stageFieldRefresh's own "unchanged" check (root linked field's value+fieldRef vs before) was an early return that skipped the ENTIRE bound-field recompute, not just the root field's own entry. A link's title/key is often stable refresh-over-refresh while the status/labels data a bound rule actually reads changes constantly -- so a staged (2+ row) refresh of an already-stable link silently reported zero changes, even though live data had genuinely changed. Confirmed via git-stash A/B. The single-row direct-apply path never had this bug, which is why the single-row path worked for Tom but bulk didn't.

Covered by two new tests in row-selection.spec.js (two-hop cascade; unchanged-root-but-changed-live-data). Full suite: 1033 passed, 2 pre-existing flakes (appearance.spec.js dark-pin-reload, mentions.spec.js first-connect) confirmed unrelated via git-stash A/B. Committed as 92828de.

Second follow-up round, from live testing against Tom's real production data:

1. Merge gate reappearing after being accepted / Review pill stuck forever: confirmPendingMerge/cancelPendingMerge never cleared the matching refreshJobs entry, so switchProject's own "surface an unreviewed job" logic kept re-showing an already-decided job on every later project switch, and the header chip kept counting it. Fixed -- both now clear the job and broadcast that to other tabs. Confirmed via git-stash A/B.

2. Staged (2+ row) refresh updated a first-hop bound field (Remedy) but never cascaded to anything bound to IT (Status) -- even though refreshing the same row alone worked fully. Root cause: stageRefreshRow explicitly skipped any bound field in its own per-field loop (fix for an earlier "Remedy shown twice" bug), which also threw out the live-data cascade that refreshing a bound-but-ref-carrying field via its own ref provides -- the only thing that can feed a second-hop field needing live source data. Fixed by threading one accumulating issue through every linked field in a row, still fetching+cascading for a bound field with its own ref but suppressing its own duplicate entry. Also fixed a related bug where a staged refresh's derived writes never got the origin:'derived' marker logDerivedChanges always sets, which was causing the bound field to read as "unlocked"/unstable on every later render.

3. Serious one, caught directly from Tom's real exported issue JSON: an issue-type field bound via a HAND-WRITTEN rule that also carries its own independently-pasted/refreshed real link permanently loses that link on the very next edit to ANY field on the same issue. computeDerivedChangeEntries called computeBoundFieldRef for every bound field regardless of rule shape, but that function only manages a fieldRef for the row-based "copy field" builder -- for a hand-written rule it always returns null, which got written straight into history as "clear the fieldRef." Fixed: only a row-based rule's computed fieldRef is ever authoritative now; a hand-written rule never touches the field's existing fieldRef. Tom's real Remedy->ER-317 link was already lost to this before the fix landed -- re-linking it once live should stick this time.

Still open, pending Tom's call: a hand-written rule's live re-evaluation (via an active refresh) computing null never clears the field's existing text, by existing deliberate design (tracker #66) and a committed test (bind-issue-field.spec.js, "keeps its last resolved pill rather than being blanked"). Tom's live case (Remedy stuck on a stale "Guests" after a refresh, condition no longer matching) suggests this should distinguish "existing value was itself rule-derived, now stale -> clear it" from "existing value is a genuine manual override -> never touch it." Not implemented yet -- it changes a tested, intentional behavior, so waiting for explicit confirmation before touching it.

Full suite: 1036 passed, 3 pre-existing flakes (appearance.spec.js dark-pin-reload, mentions.spec.js first-connect, github-sync.spec.js pushCount) all independently confirmed unrelated. Committed as 3170a0f (this round) and 0ca1577/92828de (earlier tonight).

Third follow-up round, implementing Tom's explicit direction plus one more live-caught bug:

1. Confident-null clearing (per Tom's explicit spec): a bound field's rule should ALWAYS apply when genuinely evaluated against full/live data, including a confident null -- clearing the field and making it editable, not leaving stale text sitting there forever. Distinct from "couldn't evaluate at all" (not enough data, a broken rule expression), which stays hands-off as before. Critically, this only clears a value that was ITSELF previously computed by this same rule (origin:'derived', now stale) -- never a genuine manual entry, or a field no binding has touched yet. Found this distinction was necessary when three existing tests broke on a naive first pass (a manually-set, never-bound value must never be auto-cleared). computeBoundValue's own lock check got the matching refinement.

2. Found while verifying #1: a manual override into a freshly-unlocked field got immediately re-locked by the override itself -- logDerivedChanges was diffing against the issue's own just-written state with no way to tell "the rule computed this" from "this same commit already wrote this", mislabeling the override as derived. Fixed by excluding a commit's own field from its own derived-diff.

3. Investigated two live reports against Tom's real data:
   - "Merge gate popped back up after accepting it, Review pill stuck forever" -- confirmTl/cancelPendingMerge never cleared the matching refreshJobs entry, so switchProject's own "surface an unreviewed job" logic kept re-showing an already-decided job. Fixed, confirmed via git-stash A/B.
   - "Several issues stuck showing 'Loading...' forever, survives reload" -- fieldLoading (transient fetch-in-flight UI state) was never excluded from what persist() writes to disk, and nothing reset it on load. A tab closed mid-fetch (or any interruption before the completion handler's own setState ran) left it stuck true permanently. Fixed both ways (persist() never writes it; hydrateIssue resets it defensively), confirmed via git-stash A/B -- self-healing for Tom's already-stuck issues on their next load, no data surgery needed.

Also traced (not a new bug, confirms earlier fixes are working): Tom's real "Remedy" field lost its genuine Jira link back on Oct 11 to the computeDerivedChangeEntries bug fixed in the previous round -- confirmed from his own exported history. That field now just holds plain text; re-linking it is the only way to restore the real connection.

New tests in bound-value-panel.spec.js, row-selection.spec.js, and data-structures.spec.js. Full suite: 1040 passed, 2 pre-existing flakes (github-sync.spec.js pushCount, mentions.spec.js first-connect) confirmed unrelated via isolation/git-stash. Committed as 6b6c7be (this round), 3170a0f and 0ca1577 (earlier tonight).

history.value: Importing a project with zero issues was silently rejected

history.text:
Found and fixed. Root cause: handleApplyUpdateParsed (and two sibling room-mode import paths, onSubmitReceiveProject/onReceiveProjectFileChange) checked "!parsed.issues.length" alone as the "is this a valid tracker export" test. A file with real fields/name/comments but zero issues (an empty backlog, or one that's so far just project-level notes) tripped a misleading "Could not read that as a tracker export" alert and bailed out before ever reaching previewMerge/importParsedAsNewProject -- it wasn't a true no-op, it just looked like one.

Every other place this file parses a .jsonl (parseLocalFile, the GitHub-sync pull path, Connect Remote, the other room-mode intake checks) correctly uses "!parsed.fields && !parsed.issues.length" -- these three were the only call sites using the narrower, wrong check on its own. Fixed to match.

Confirmed via git-stash A/B: reproduces exactly on the old code. New test in data-structures.spec.js. Full suite clean (1042 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated flake). Committed as ed5c3b1.

history.value: Filtering in the Tauri desktop app blanks the whole table instead of filtering it

history.text:
Reported by Tom: typing into the filter box in the Tauri desktop app makes the whole issue table disappear (not just show zero matches as expected for a non-matching query) -- works fine in Firefox. Not yet reproduced directly: Playwright's bundled WebKit engine (same rendering family as Tauri's Linux WebKitGTK webview) can't launch in this sandbox (missing system libs -- libgtk-4, libavif, libx264, etc. -- and no root/apt access here to install them).

Investigated the pure filtering logic (issueValueMatchesFilter, computeColumnFilterExcludedIds, tokenizeFilterQuery, parseFilterQuery, issueMatchesFieldToken/Tokens, splitHighlightSegments, matchingIssuesByIdPrefix, fieldRefSearchText) and the render-time call site (~line 10946-10993 of the Component source) by hand:
- No modern JS syntax/APIs that a webview's JS engine might lack (no optional chaining/nullish coalescing near this code, no toSorted/toReversed/structuredClone/Object.groupBy/requestIdleCallback, no logical-assignment operators anywhere in Layer 1).
- No user input ever gets compiled into a RegExp -- all matching is plain .indexOf/.includes/.toLowerCase substring work, so a malformed filter string can't throw a regex error.
- columnFilters (the sticky checkbox column filters) are read/written through try/catch-guarded localStorage helpers and are a separate mechanism from the live filterQuery box Tom described -- ruled out as the cause of a live-typing blank-out.

So the pure filter computation looks engine-portable on inspection. That points toward something in the live DOM-update/render path itself (the custom x-dc/data-dc-script templating this app uses) behaving differently under WebKitGTK -- e.g. a render-scheduling or microtask-timing difference -- rather than a logic bug in the filter functions. That's a guess, not a finding; I don't have a way to get a real error out of an actual WebKitGTK webview from in here.

Next useful step needs Tom: open the Tauri app's webview devtools (if enabled in this build) or run the app with stderr visible, type a filter query, and see whether anything is actually thrown to the console at the moment the table blanks -- that would turn this from a guess into a real diagnosis.

Added the "devtools" Cargo feature to src-tauri/Cargo.toml (committed in 69c344c, alongside the notification fix) so devtools are reachable in a release build too -- right-click -> Inspect Element, after a rebuild. That's the fastest way to get a real console error out of the actual webview the next time this reproduces.

history.value: A field whose only change is rule-derived (origin:'derived') is invisible to the merge-diff, so sending it can report "no changes to merge"

history.text:
Fixed (commit 049e338). mergeIssuePair's touchedFields now looks at each field's full history (both origins) instead of reusing overlappingFields' derived-excluding filter -- a field whose only change is rule-derived (origin:'derived') now correctly registers as touched. overlappingFields itself is untouched, still correctly ignoring derived entries for its own authorship-conflict purpose.

This also exposed and fixed a second bug: buildMergeIssueSummary crashed on a null .id (TypeError: Cannot read properties of null) when a now-touched field had no non-derived entry on either side to pick a resultEntryId from -- same full-history fix applied there for latest/winner/resultEntryId, while the authorship-overlap display bookkeeping (localEntryIds/incomingEntryIds/outcome) stays scoped to authored entries, unchanged.

Verified via a disposable unit test directly against the real exported pure functions (reproduced the exact reported scenario: a local issue with no Remedy history vs. an incoming one with only a derived Remedy entry -- touchedFields now includes it, mergeHasRealChanges now true; confirmed the crash is fixed; confirmed two-sided derived disagreement still doesn't trip overlappingFields). Also ran every spec file touching this merge path (data-structures, interaction, milestones, project-notes, merge-provenance, matrix-host, row-selection, including #198's staged-refresh-job tests, which confirm a staged refresh already tags its own cascaded writes origin:derived the same way): 455 passed, 0 failures.

history.value: Tauri desktop app window doesn't fill the screen on launch

history.text:
Reported by Tom, alongside #203. Root cause: src-tauri/tauri.conf.json's window config only set a fixed width:1280/height:800 with no maximized flag -- on any display where that's not already the full resolution, the window simply opens smaller than the screen, by design of the default config, not a bug in the webview itself.

Fixed: added "maximized": true to the window config. The app now opens maximized (filling the available work area) on launch, still resizable afterward like before. Not yet verified against a real build (no GUI in this sandbox) -- straightforward, low-risk config change, but worth confirming on a rebuild.

Correction: Tom clarified this was never about window SIZE at launch -- it's that the add-item bar at the bottom of the table doesn't pin to the bottom of the window the way it does in a browser tab. The maximized:true fix (already committed) doesn't address this at all -- different mechanism entirely (window size vs. page content layout within whatever size the window actually is). Reopening.

The app root uses height:100vh; display:flex; flex-direction:column, with the table area as a flex child that grows to fill remaining space and the add-item bar as a fixed-height sibling below it -- standard "pinned footer" flex layout, same CSS a browser renders correctly. Best guess (unverified, no device to test): the Tauri webview's content area isn't tracking the window's real size -- i.e. it's correctly laid out for 100vh of SOME height, just not the actual current window height. That can happen when the webview widget doesn't get resized in sync with a window-size change, a known rough edge in some Tauri setups around setting "maximized": true in the static config (vs. calling window.maximize() programmatically in the Rust setup() hook after the window exists, which avoids a race with the webview's own resize listener attaching). Tauri's own docs don't confirm this as a known issue though -- genuinely unverified.

Asked Tom: does manually resizing the window (even un-maximize + drag an edge) make the bar jump to the new bottom? And which OS. That'll tell us whether this is a resize-propagation gap (fixable by moving the maximize call into Rust setup()) or something else entirely.

Resolved, not a bug: Tom confirmed the add-item bar correctly stays beneath the last entry rather than pinning to the window's bottom -- that's the deliberate, already-tested design (tests/interaction.spec.js:1478, 'a short list stays content-height'), not something to change. An app window being conceptually different from a web page re: viewport-filling is a bigger question Tom's deliberately leaving alone for now.

No code change needed here beyond the maximized:true revert (commit 79699ad) already covers the one real change this thread produced. The actual remaining bug Tom spotted along the way -- column-edit menus not extending past the add-item bar -- is a distinct issue, filed separately.

history.value: Column drag-and-drop doesn't work in the Tauri desktop app

history.text:
Reported by Tom, alongside #202. Column headers, kanban cards, and rule-builder rows all use the native HTML5 Drag and Drop API (draggable="true" + dragstart/dragover/drop + dataTransfer), which works fine in Chromium and Firefox.

Likely root cause: WebKit (Safari, and the WKWebView/WebKitGTK Tauri embeds) only auto-enables native OS-level dragging for a handful of element types by default -- images, links, text selections. A plain <div draggable="true"> (exactly what every one of these is) needs the WebKit-specific -webkit-user-drag: element CSS property set explicitly, or dragstart never fires at all at the native level even though the HTML attribute and JS handlers are all correct -- a long-documented WebKit quirk, not specific to this app's code.

Fixed: added '[draggable="true"] { -webkit-user-drag: element; }' to wigwag.html's global stylesheet, covering every draggable element in the app (column headers, kanban cards, rule-builder rows) in one rule, since they all hit the same gap. Inert in Chromium/Firefox (an unrecognized-effect vendor property there), so no risk to the existing behavior -- full suite unaffected.

Not yet verified against a real WebKit build (same limitation as #200 -- no GUI/WebKit libs in this sandbox). This is the standard, well-documented fix for this exact symptom, but needs confirming on a rebuild. If it turns out NOT to fix it, #200's open ask (check the Tauri devtools console at the moment of the broken interaction) is the next step here too.

Negative result from Tom: the -webkit-user-drag CSS fix did NOT solve this on his real Mac -- still can't reorder columns via drag-and-drop.

Re-checked the actual JS logic (dragStart/dragOverCol/dropCol) directly -- preventDefault() IS correctly called in dragOverCol (required for drop to fire at all, per the HTML5 DnD spec), dataTransfer.setData/getData use matching 'text/plain' keys, the column-order splice logic looks correct and is exercised by passing tests. Nothing else obviously wrong from reading the code alone.

Given two different guesses (-webkit-user-drag, then ruling out a missing preventDefault) have both come back clean/unhelpful, I don't have a third blind guess worth trying. This needs the real devtools console output from the actual failure -- Tom now has devtools reachable (earlier Cargo feature addition). Next step: open devtools, try the drag, see if anything is thrown or logged at all during the attempt (dragstart never firing at all vs. firing but drop never landing are different bugs with different fixes).

history.value: Column-edit context menus don't extend past the add-item bar (Tauri desktop app)

history.text:
Reported by Tom: column-edit context menus (the sort/freeze/wrap/group/hide/delete dropdown, and the title-column menu) stop short of the add-item bar at the bottom of the window instead of extending past/over it -- in the Tauri desktop app at least, not yet confirmed whether this also happens in a real browser.

These menus use position:fixed + the existing computeAnchor() helper (wigwag.html, the same anchor-measurement logic #185/column-menu-overflow-fix.md's flip-toward-more-space fix already uses elsewhere). computeAnchor measures available space using window.innerHeight when there's no enclosing slideover -- exactly the same value the page's own height:100vh root layout relies on.

Working theory, ties this together with #203's drag-and-drop gap and the add-item-bar discussion on #202: if window.innerHeight (or however Tauri's webview reports/tracks its own visible height) doesn't match the window's REAL visible height, that would explain both symptoms at once -- page content laid out short of the true bottom, AND menu max-height/flip calculations capped using the same too-small number, so a menu stops well above where it could otherwise safely extend.

Asked Tom to check directly (devtools are reachable now via the earlier devtools Cargo feature): open the Tauri app's devtools console and run `window.innerHeight`, compare against the window's actual visible pixel height. If that number is wrong, the fix belongs in how Tauri reports/updates it, not in wigwag.html's CSS/JS -- if it's correct, this needs a fresh look at computeAnchor's own logic instead. Not yet confirmed either way -- no real WebKit engine available in this sandbox to test against directly (same limitation as #200/#203).

history.value: Tauri desktop: auto-update (check, prompt, download, in-place upgrade)

history.text:
Scoping pass (no implementation yet) -- Tom asked whether we could add automatic update detection + prompt + download + in-place upgrade to the Tauri desktop app.

THE ONE REAL BLOCKER: this repo's CI (.github/workflows/tauri-build.yml) deliberately never bumps tauri.conf.json's version -- its own comments explain why: every push to main rebuilds and republishes to a single rolling 'desktop-latest' release, no tag/bump step at all. An updater works by comparing the installed version against a manifest's advertised version and only prompting when it's actually newer -- with the version pinned forever, it would never fire. This needs solving FIRST. Cleanest fix consistent with the existing human-free push-to-release model: patch tauri.conf.json's version in CI to something auto-incrementing (e.g. 0.1.<github.run_number>) right before 'tauri build' runs, rather than reintroducing manual version-bump commits.

SIGNING: generate a dedicated updater keypair via 'tauri signer generate' (separate from the existing Apple code-signing cert, #180/#184). Public key goes straight into tauri.conf.json (not secret); private key + optional password become two new GitHub Actions repo secrets.

RUST/TAURI WIRING (mirrors the notification work from earlier today exactly): add tauri-plugin-updater AND tauri-plugin-process (relaunch lives in a separate plugin) to Cargo.toml, register both in main.rs, add their capabilities, set bundle.createUpdaterArtifacts:true + plugins.updater.{pubkey,endpoints} in tauri.conf.json. Confirmed by actually reading the plugins' real rollup build config (plugins-workspace repo, shared/rollup.config.js): both ship the same api-iife.js global-binding build notification/opener already use here, so window.__TAURI__.updater and window.__TAURI__.process.relaunch() will work the same zero-build-step way this app already relies on everywhere else -- no npm import, no architecture change, despite Tauri's own docs page implying otherwise (that page doesn't account for withGlobalTauri).

CI: tauri-apps/tauri-action (already in use) auto-generates the signed artifacts + update manifest once createUpdaterArtifacts + the signing secrets are present. The manifest can point at a plain releases/latest/download/... URL on the SAME rolling release this project already publishes to -- no new hosting needed. Needs one real dry-run push to confirm the exact asset name it produces, since that's exactly what tauri.conf.json's endpoints must reference.

FRONTEND (wigwag.html): background check() on launch (+ maybe periodic poll while running). NOT silent -- per Tom's own framing ('prompt to download... then if you say so') -- a dismissible banner ('Wigwag vX available -- Update & Restart' / 'Not now'), matching the existing settings-panel visual language. Confirm -> downloadAndInstall() with progress -> relaunch(). Maybe also a manual 'Check for updates' button, same diagnostic spirit as the existing 'Send test notification' button.

VERIFICATION: Playwright tests mocking window.__TAURI__.updater the same way tests/mentions.spec.js already mocks window.__TAURI__.notification -- fully testable from this sandbox. NOT verifiable here: the real signed-artifact round trip (real build, real signature check, real self-replace, real relaunch) -- genuinely needs Tom on a real Mac after a real CI release.

SUGGESTED ORDER: (1) versioning fix, blocking everything else, (2) signing keypair, (3) Rust/Tauri wiring, (4) CI changes + a real dry-run push to confirm the manifest URL, (5) frontend UX + tests, (6) Tom verifies the real end-to-end update on his Mac.

Not started -- Tom asked to scope this first, decide on implementation timing separately.

Implemented (commit 390c400) -- all of the plan from the earlier scoping comment, plus a correction: tauri-action's `appVersion` input turned out to be the right place for the auto-incrementing version (0.1.<github.run_number>), not a separate jq-based file patch -- cleaner, officially supported.

ONE THING I NEED FROM TOM: the real build can't sign anything until the updater's private key is in GitHub Actions secrets. It's sitting at .updater-keys/wigwag-updater.key in this checkout (gitignored, never committed -- generated with no password). Since /workspace is a bind mount of your own machine, open that file directly on your host (not through me) and paste its contents into two new repo secrets:
- TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY -- the full file contents
- TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD -- leave empty (no password was set)
Once those exist, the next push to main will produce a real signed build + latest.json on the rolling desktop-latest release.

KNOWN GAP (documented in the workflow's own comments too): only darwin-aarch64 is published in the updater manifest, since macos-latest GitHub runners are Apple Silicon-only -- an Intel Mac won't be offered this update at all, same limitation as today's single-architecture .dmg. Not a regression, just not solved by this pass.

Verified from this sandbox: cargo check compiles clean, the YAML is syntactically valid, the frontend banner (check -> prompt -> download -> install -> relaunch, plus error handling) works end-to-end against a mocked window.__TAURI__.updater/process in 7 new Playwright tests, and the full suite (1053 passed, 1 known pre-existing flake) shows no regression from the new banner markup sitting in the primary render path. NOT verified: the real signed-artifact round trip end to end -- genuinely needs a real CI release (once the secrets are in) and a real Mac, there's no way around that from here.

Follow-up committed (f49a837): real per-push versioned GitHub Releases (desktop-v0.1.<run number>, make_latest:true keeps the stable /latest/download/ links working) instead of one rolling overwritten release, plus an always-visible installed-app-version display in the footer (not just inside the conditional update banner) so 'am I actually up to date' is checkable at any time. Full suite: 1055 passed, 2 known pre-existing flakes, no new regressions.

Also: confirmed with Tom that the repeated '0.1.15 is available' he was seeing wasn't a comparison bug -- it's because nothing newer had actually been pushed since the build that produced that manifest (I'd been committing locally in this sandbox but can't push myself -- no SSH egress from this container, same restriction as everything else here; Tom pushes from his own machine against the same checkout). Once he pushes this commit, a genuinely newer version will build and we'll find out whether a real Update & Restart correctly lands on it.

Found and fixed the real bug behind Tom's '0.1.16 is available (you're on 0.1.0)' report (commit b759698). tauri-action's appVersion input -- which I'd been relying on for the auto-incrementing version since the original implementation -- turned out to be a no-op for this project: reading tauri-action's own source (build.ts), it only applies appVersion via initProject (init-project.ts is the ONE place that actually does config.version = appVersion), and build.ts only calls initProject when no src-tauri/ directory exists yet -- i.e. only when tauri-action is scaffolding a brand new project itself. This repo already has a real, committed src-tauri/, so that path never ran. Every real build silently kept the committed tauri.conf.json version (0.1.0) untouched, while my own hand-built latest.json (built independently, from the same intended version number) kept advancing on its own -- hence the mismatch: the manifest said something newer existed, but the installed binary never actually BECAME that version no matter how many times it 'updated', so it just kept reoffering an ever-newer version forever.

Fixed by patching src-tauri/tauri.conf.json's version directly via jq in a plain CI step before tauri-action runs, instead of depending on appVersion at all. This is the normal, direct way Tauri resolves its own version at build time -- no dependency on tauri-action's scaffold-only behavior. Verified the exact jq command against a real copy of the file: only the version field changes, everything else byte-for-byte identical.

This needed Tom's own live report to actually find -- there was no way to catch this from this sandbox, since it only manifests as a real build's real embedded version, which nothing here can produce or inspect. Next real push should finally show the installed app's own version (footer: 'App 0.1.X') actually advancing after an update, not stuck at 0.1.0.

Fixed (commit 79bdabd) two more real bugs Tom hit live:

1. 'Update failed / The signature verification failed', with no way to dismiss it. Root cause: latest.json's download URLs used releases/latest/download/... -- a moving target resolving to whatever's CURRENTLY flagged latest at download time, not whenever the manifest was actually fetched. Given how fast releases have been landing tonight, a newer release becoming latest in the gap between fetch and click would mean downloading a DIFFERENT artifact than the one the held signature was computed for -- exactly what a signature mismatch means. Pinned to each release's own immutable tag instead (releases/download/desktop-v<version>/...).

2. The error banner had showActions unconditionally false, hiding every button -- confirmed as a real bug in my own code, not a guess. Fixed: error state now offers 'Try again' (re-runs the check) and 'Dismiss', reusing the same fields/markup the normal case already has. checkForUpdate() also now resets updatePhase on every fresh check so a stale error can't keep masking a later success.

Two new tests cover both directly. Full suite: 1058 passed, 1 known pre-existing flake, no new regressions. Ready for Tom to push and re-test.

Added a manual "Check for updates" link in the footer, per Tom's request -- checkForUpdate() already existed but was only ever invoked automatically on mount, with no on-demand affordance. Commit 37a5e9b, full suite clean (1077 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated flake).

history.value: Restarting the Tauri desktop app loses column-order/hidden-field layout preferences

history.text:
Reported by Tom while testing the new auto-updater: after the app restarts, hidden fields come back (hiddenFieldIds resets) and column order resets too -- these are both plain localStorage-backed preferences (HIDDEN_FIELDS_KEY, COLUMN_ORDER_KEY), nothing to do with project data itself.

Noticed specifically during update-triggered restarts (Update & Restart -> relaunch()), so there are two different possible causes with two different fixes:
1. ANY app restart loses this (plain quit + reopen, nothing to do with the updater) -- would point at something about how Tauri's WKWebView persists localStorage across launches in general, unrelated to tracker #205's new work.
2. ONLY an update-triggered restart loses it (a normal quit+reopen is fine) -- would point at something specific to the self-replace/relaunch() mechanism itself -- e.g. the new .app bundle ending up at a path or identity WebKit treats as a different persistent-storage container from the old one.

Asked Tom to check which one it actually is. Not yet investigated further -- need that answer first, and this is pure native-webview storage behavior I have no way to reproduce or verify from this sandbox either way.

Tom confirmed: a plain restart (not specifically an update-triggered one) still loses it. So this rules out the relaunch()/self-replace mechanism as the cause -- it's not specific to tracker #205's new work, it reproduces on an ordinary quit+reopen too. Narrows it to either (a) Tauri's WKWebView localStorage persistence in general, or (b) something in wigwag's own boot sequence that resets just these two keys specifically (note it's apparently JUST hiddenFieldIds/column order, not the whole project/identity data -- if it were a wholesale storage-persistence failure we'd expect to lose projects too, which isn't reported). Investigating the second angle now, since it's the one actually within reach from this sandbox.

Root cause found and fixed, diagnosed live with Tom via several rounds of targeted console-logging on real Tauri builds (no way to reproduce this in the sandbox otherwise -- it's pure timing).

Root cause: componentDidUpdate calls six per-project persist functions (persistColumnWidths, persistColumnOrder, persistHiddenFieldIds, persistColumnFilters, persistSort, persistColumnWrap) UNCONDITIONALLY on every render. But componentDidMount's own async side effects (the notification-permission check, window.__TAURI__.app.getVersion(), the update check) can resolve and trigger a render BEFORE runBootSequence's own async tail (finishBootSequenceAsync -> loadPersistedAsync) has corrected these fields from storage. If that happens, an early render persists the constructor's still-default value (e.g. hiddenFieldIds: []) under the already-resolved project id, clobbering whatever was correctly saved last session -- before the real load ever gets a chance to read it. Confirmed directly from a real console trace: the bad persistHiddenFieldIds write landed BEFORE loadPersistedAsync's own ENTRY log even fired on the same boot.

This happens on literally every boot, not 'after a while' or 'on update restarts specifically' -- it's just timing-dependent on whether one of those componentDidMount async calls happens to resolve before loadPersistedAsync finishes, which is why it looked inconsistent.

The fix was already half-written into the codebase: persist() (the main project-doc persister) already guards against exactly this with . The six per-project preference functions above just never got the same guard when they were split out of the doc into their own per-device keys (see persistHiddenFieldIds's own 'Live incident 2026-09-28' comment for when that split happened). Added the identical guard to all six.

Verified: real hide-reload-confirm smoke test now survives correctly; full regression suite running, will confirm clean before this is considered Done.

Correction to the comment above -- a shell quoting accident ate the actual guard snippet. The exact line persist() already has, now also added to all six per-project functions: if (s.localDocLoading || s.roomModeBootstrapping) return;

Committed: 42a9c47. Full regression suite passed clean (1071 passed, one pre-existing unrelated flake). Please do a final real-build verification on your end (push, rebuild, repeat the hide-a-field-then-restart test a few times) before I mark this Done -- I can't verify the actual fix against a real Tauri boot from this sandbox, only that the guard logic is correct and nothing else regressed.
Confirmed by Tom on a real build: table layout (hidden fields, column order) now survives an app restart. Closing this out.

history.value: Connected Sources (Phase 1): generic custom connectors for linking issues to any external system

history.text:
Implementing per the design handoff Tom shared (connected_source_2.zip, 'Connected Sources.dc.html'): user-defined custom connectors to any external system -- a name/glyph/color, one or more regex patterns that recognize a pasted id/URL, and a pasted JS macro (async (id, credential) => ({title, url, state, labels, assignee, extra})) that fetches + shapes the data. Runs inside the Tauri app so fetch hits any API directly, no CORS restriction and no separate proxy process needed (unlike the existing Jira/Salesforce proxies).

Scope for this pass, agreed with Tom: Phase 1 only -- net-new custom connectors, the existing GitHub/Jira/Salesforce dispatch/fetch logic is untouched, zero regression risk there. Credentials go into the real OS keychain (keyring crate), not localStorage.

Progress so far:
- Rust side DONE and committed (b63e4d8): connected_source_fetch (reqwest, no URL-scope restriction) + 3 keychain commands (set/get/delete credential), verified via a real cargo build.
- Pure data model DONE in wigwag-core.js (uncommitted, mid-verification): CONNECTED_SOURCES_KEY, slugifyConnectorKey, pickConnectorFields, compileConnectorMacro, plus additive branches in buildSource/applyLiveLinkedRules/sourceRefHasFullData. 9 new unit tests, all passing (256/256 total).
- Also found + fixed a real, pre-existing drift between wigwag-core.js and wigwag.html's inlined copy (they'd been hand-synced and quietly diverged -- 7 genuine gaps found via a full symbol-name diff). Built a real sync script (sync-wigwag-core.js) instead of hand-copying again, per Tom's own suggestion mid-session. While re-running it I also caught a latent landmine: wigwag-core.js had a literal raw NUL byte inside a string literal (entry.id + '\0' + entry.sortKey, meant as the escape sequence, not a real control byte) -- harmless to V8 but binary-unsafe for text tooling (even grep silently skips the file). Fixed to the proper '\0' escape. Full regression suite re-running now against the corrected file before this gets committed.
- Not started yet: the Settings UI for adding/editing a connector -- Phase 1 ships without an in-app creation flow; a connector can only be seeded via localStorage for now (documented in the plan and in the drafted test file). Dispatch integration (paste-recognition + conflict picker) and chip rendering are drafted as patch scripts but not yet applied to wigwag.html -- queued right behind the suite re-run.

Full plan: /home/dev/.claude/plans/encapsulated-waddling-gizmo.md

Step 0 (the wigwag-core.js sync) is committed: be3f4ba.

Running the real sync for the first time surfaced something more serious than expected: wigwag-core.js had quietly drifted from wigwag.html's hand-patched copy on 10 real, already-shipped bug fixes, not just the handful of missing functions I'd found in an earlier name-based diff pass. A full body-level diff (comparing every shared top-level declaration's exact text) found and fixed all 10, including the exact fix behind tracker #201 (no changes to merge) and a hand-written-rule-loses-its-own-pasted-link bug that a real regression test (tests/bind-issue-field.spec.js:219) actually caught failing when I ran the naive sync -- confirmed as a genuine regression via git-stash-compare (passes at HEAD, failed with the stale logic). Full writeup is in the commit message.

Also landed in the same commit: the Connected Sources pure-logic data model in wigwag-core.js (CONNECTED_SOURCES_KEY, slugifyConnectorKey, pickConnectorFields, compileConnectorMacro, buildSource/applyLiveLinkedRules/sourceRefHasFullData branches), 9 new unit tests, 256/256 passing.

Full regression suite: 1058 passed, 1 failed -- tests/mentions.spec.js's first-connect test, confirmed via git-stash-compare to fail identically at HEAD (pre-existing, unrelated flake).

Next: apply the drafted (already self-reviewed) dispatch-integration and chip-rendering patches to wigwag.html's Layer 2, add the durable Playwright test file, run the full suite again, commit.

Layer 2 (dispatch integration + chip rendering) is committed: 91371d2.

Paste-recognition, the macro engine's Component-side runtime, applyConnectorLinkToField (mirrors applyGithubLinkToField), the refreshField branch, the pattern-conflict picker, and chip rendering are all in. tests/connected-sources.spec.js (new, 6 tests) passes against the real app.

Caught two real bugs during verification, before either reached a test: (1) the Component script's own destructure-from-window.WigwagCore block was never updated with the new exports, so CONNECTED_SOURCES_KEY was silently undefined and loadConnectedSources()'s own try/catch swallowed the resulting error -- every connector silently failed to load with zero visible error; (2) my own test fixture used an id shape that collides with the existing built-in Jira key regex, so dispatch correctly (by design) took the Jira branch instead -- confirms 'built-ins always win' is working, not a bug. Full writeup in the commit message.

Full regression suite: 1064 passed, same one pre-existing mentions.spec.js flake as last time (confirmed unrelated via git-stash-compare).

Remaining for Phase 1, explicitly deferred and not started: the Settings UI for adding/editing a connector through the app itself -- for now a connector can only be seeded by writing directly to localStorage (see the test file's own seedConnector helper). That's the one major piece left before this is usable without devtools.

Settings UI landed, then a scope decision with Tom reversed part of it in the same commit (b9b685f):

Settings -> Connected sources (add/edit form: Identity/Credential/Patterns/Macro/Test panels, list view with the 3 built-ins read-only + custom connectors) is built and working.

But walking through where credentials for a custom connector can actually live surfaced a real problem: outside Tauri, there's no standard way to reach a real OS keychain (navigator.credentials is for login, not arbitrary API tokens; a local-companion-process alternative was considered and rejected -- doesn't save you from running a process, and fights Chrome's Private Network Access policy). Confirmed in code: outside Tauri, a typed credential is just dropped -- never stored -- while the UI still claims 'Connected'.

Decided: Connected Sources does not exist as a feature outside the real Tauri app at all -- not in wigwag.work/app, localhost:, or a plain file:// open. Gated via the existing isTauriConnectorRuntime() check at every entry point (paste-dispatch, the Settings nav entry on both desktop and mobile, the refresh/picker path). Pure rendering of already-linked data (chips, rule evaluation) stays unconditional -- a field linked from the real app still displays correctly if later viewed from a browser.

This also fixed two real regressions the unconditional Settings entry had just caused (mobile.spec.js expecting exactly 4 settings sections). Full suite: 1071 passed, one known unrelated flake.

Remaining for Phase 1: nothing else identified. The feature is now internally consistent -- usable end-to-end inside Tauri (data model, dispatch, macro engine, chip rendering, Settings UI, real Rust-backed fetch+keychain), cleanly absent everywhere else.

Fixed the real-world Jira/connector pattern collision Tom hit while testing: jiraKeyMatch now requires a configured jiraProxySecret before claiming a pasted pattern at all (not jiraProxyUrl, which has an always-truthy hardcoded placeholder default and so is useless as a 'configured' signal). An unconfigured Jira now falls through exactly as if the string never looked like a Jira key, so a custom connector's own colliding pattern gets a real chance. Covers all three dispatch call sites in one place (jiraKeyMatch itself). Committed as 9d13003, full suite clean (1073 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated flake).

Also fixed separately: the Settings Test-output box could grow tall enough to push Save out of reach with a large macro result -- capped its height (committed 057181f), full suite re-verified clean after the fact.

Filed #208 for the broader, still-open UX gap: even with this fix, a *configured* built-in can still shadow a connector's pattern, with zero feedback surfaced about which system actually claimed a given paste. Not scoped yet, just captured so it isn't lost.

Fixed two real bugs Tom hit testing against Jira via a custom connector: (1) direct field-edit chip rendering fell through to a GitHub-shaped catch-all (undefined/undefined#undefined, wrong icon) -- buildTextCells own separate ref-dispatch chain had never been taught about connector refs, only boundRefParts had. (2) add-item-bar paste never checked custom connectors at all, only commitEdit did. Also finished the glyph-badge markup across all 5 ref-icon template spots, which was computed but never actually rendered anywhere. Committed 9d14580, full suite clean (1079 passed, 3 pre-existing unrelated flakes, independently re-verified). Filed #209 for the one related gap not fixed here (bulk-paste preview classification).

Progress update: Jira/Salesforce built-in linking is retired off the jira-proxy.js/salesforce-proxy.js bridges and onto the same in-process connector/keychain mechanism (Tauri-only), per Tom's own call. ensureBuiltinConnectors seeds __builtin_jira/__builtin_salesforce for every user; all dispatch (paste, refresh, bulk paste) redirects to them unconditionally now -- the old migratedMatch fallback-to-a-matching-custom-connector special case (219dd95a) is fully retired, not just bypassed. Settings UI: editing Jira/Salesforce now opens the same full editor a custom connector gets, shown disabled (not hidden) outside Tauri. GitHub's own migration + Settings unification is deferred to a separate follow-up commit (its dispatch still works unauthenticated in any browser today, so it's a bigger-feeling behavioral change worth isolating). Along the way fixed several real gaps this exposed: buildSource/applyLiveLinkedRules extra-flattening, isRefLocallyLive's reachability check, fieldRefSearchText's missing connector branch, xlsxFieldHref's missing salesforce/connector branch, and classifyBulkPasteLines/refsMatch's connector-ref gap (separately tracked and closed as 54e36073). Full suite: 1112/1119 passing, remaining 7 all confirmed pre-existing baseline flakes or load-dependent (clean in isolation).

history.value: Paste-dispatch collision with a built-in gives no feedback about which system claimed the pattern

history.text:
Spun out of #207 (Connected Sources). Tom hit this live: a custom connector's own pattern can legitimately collide with a built-in's reserved shape (e.g. Jira's PROJ-123 key regex) -- commitEdit's dispatch order is GitHub -> Jira -> Salesforce -> wigwag -> custom connectors, built-ins always win by design, so the paste silently took the built-in's branch and failed/produced a confusing result, with zero UI indication of *why* -- you just see the wrong (or failing) outcome with no clue another system claimed the pattern first.

Immediate symptom (Jira specifically, unconfigured) is being fixed separately right now: jiraKeyMatch will stop claiming a pattern at all once Jira has no configured proxy secret, so an unconfigured Jira falls through to custom connectors exactly as if the string never looked like a Jira key.

This issue is the broader, still-open UX gap: even with that fix, a *configured* built-in can still shadow a connector's pattern, and when any collision happens there's currently no feedback surfaced anywhere (no history entry, no inline hint) telling the user which system actually claimed their paste. Worth a small affordance -- e.g. a one-line 'matched as a Jira key, not your Linear connector' hint near the field, or in the resulting history entry -- so a collision is debuggable instead of silently mysterious. Not scoped/designed yet; filing so it doesn't evaporate.

history.value: Custom connectors: bulk-paste preview classification and refsMatch dedup dont know about connector refs

history.text:
Found while fixing two live-reported custom-connector bugs (direct-field-edit chip rendering and add-item-bar dispatch, both now fixed). classifyBulkPasteLines (the bulk-paste REVIEW preview) checks github/jira/salesforce/wigwag only -- a connector-matching line gets classified unlinked in the preview, even though confirmBulkPaste calls createIssueFromText per line at confirm time, which now does resolve connectors correctly. So the preview undercounts linked/shows the wrong bucket, but the actual created rows are fine.

refsMatch (cross-issue duplicate-ref equality, used by both bulk-paste dedup and createIssueFromTexts own duplicate check elsewhere) also has no system === connector case -- falls through its own implicit false, meaning two connector-linked issues with the SAME matchedId would never be detected as duplicates in bulk-paste.

Not fixed in this pass -- scoped out to keep the live-reported bugs turnaround fast. Needs: a connector branch in classifyBulkPasteLines (mirroring createIssueFromTexts own dispatch order -- customConnectorMatches checked last, after all 4 built-ins) and in refsMatch (compare connectorId + matchedId).

Fixed. classifyBulkPasteLines now checks customConnectorMatches last (same dispatch order as createIssueFromText), and refsMatch has a system:'connector' case comparing connectorId+matchedId. Covered by a new test in connected-sources.spec.js (bulk-paste preview classifies a real custom connector match as linked, and dedupes a repeat of an already-linked id). Found this while working on the Jira/Salesforce built-in retirement -- refsMatch's own connector branch turned out to be needed there too, for the exact same reason.

history.value: hydrateIssue + the values/fieldRefs/fieldLoading strip does not perfectly round-trip an issues JSON shape

history.text:
Found while investigating Tom's feels sluggish report, chasing tracker #131 (persist() fan-out). Attempted a reference-equality gate on persist() so it skips redundant disk writes when nothing persist-relevant changed -- this directly exposed and reliably reproduced a REAL infinite cross-tab broadcast ping-pong (tests/cross-tab-sync.spec.js:112 went from a rare once-under-load flake to 4/5 failures in isolation). Reverted that specific gate (kept a separate, unrelated, verified-safe measureTableOverflow gate from the same pass).

Root cause traced via direct instrumentation (hooking BroadcastChannel.postMessage): after tab B adopts tab A's broadcast via _applyRemoteDocUpdate, tab B's own next persist() recomputes a doc from s.issues (which _applyRemoteDocUpdate hydrated via hydrateIssue) via the standard outgoingIssues = s.issues.map(({values, fieldRefs, fieldLoading, ...rest}) => rest) strip -- this produced a BYTE-DIFFERENT JSON (confirmed: oscillated stably between exactly two lengths, 17524 and 17198, repeatedly) compared to what was originally received/authored, even though the content should be semantically identical. Each tab, receiving the OTHER's slightly-different recomputed shape, recomputes its OWN again-different shape and bounces it back -- forever.

This is a LATENT, pre-existing issue independent of my gate -- the gate just changed exactly when persist() runs relative to other renders, turning a previously-self-limiting (or just rare) oscillation into a reliable one. The real fix is making hydrateIssue (or whatever it's doing differently on a second pass) genuinely idempotent against its own stripped output, so hydrate-then-strip-then-hydrate-then-strip converges to a stable fixed point immediately rather than toggling. Not root-caused at the hydrateIssue-internals level yet -- that's the next step for whoever picks this up. Recommend treating this as blocking for ANY future persist()-frequency optimization (tracker #131), not just a cosmetic byte-diff curiosity.

history.value: Bound-field redesign: merge-notice detection no longer reliably excludes derived-value divergence

history.text:
Found as a side effect of the bound-field visibility redesign (overnight work, same session as #207/#206/connected-sources, etc).

That redesign deliberately stops writing origin:'derived' on new history entries (per Tom's own call: provenance of a field's value shouldn't live in the exported/signed file at all -- see docs/FORMAT.md's updated 'Bound-field visibility' section for the full design). A local-only store (LOCAL_DERIVED_ENTRY_IDS_KEY) now tracks this device's own derive history instead.

Side effect: mergeIssuePair / buildMergeIssueSummary / buildMergePreviewViewModel (and one more site, computeSquashedHistory-adjacent) all still check 'h.origin !== "derived"' to decide whether two merging copies' divergent values for a field are a genuine human-authorship overlap (show a merge notice) or just two independent rule recomputations that self-heal once applyLinkedRules re-runs (no notice -- this is the tracker #201/fa3a34c2-era behavior). That check is now permanently blind to any NEWLY-derived entry from either side, since new entries never carry the tag any more.

Worst case: two devices independently re-deriving the same bound field to different answers, then merging, can now surface a spurious 'both changed this' notice where the old behavior correctly suppressed it. This is a UI/notice-accuracy issue only -- the actual merged DATA is still correct either way (newest-sortKey-wins, then applyLinkedRules re-runs against the merged result regardless of the notice).

Why not fixed as part of the same pass: the local side COULD in principle recognize its own just-derived entries via the new local record, but that record is local-only by design -- it has no way to know whether the INCOMING side's divergent entry was itself derived or hand-typed there. There's no longer a portable, symmetric signal available to answer this correctly for both sides at once. A real fix needs its own design thought (e.g.: accept the incoming-side blind spot and only suppress when the LOCAL side can prove its own value was last-known-derived; or decide the UI copy for a merge notice should just stop implying authorship and describe it more neutrally; or something else) -- didn't want to guess under time pressure at 3am on something that only affects a secondary notice, not correctness.

Not currently covered by any failing test: the one existing test for this (data-structures.spec.js:916, 'a bound/derived field never surfaces as a conflict and recomputes fresh after merge') hardcodes origin:'derived' directly into its fixture, so it doesn't exercise a value actually derived through the real app's current (tag-free) commit path -- that's the gap. A new test driving a REAL derive-then-merge end-to-end (not a hardcoded fixture) would be the right way to confirm this before fixing it.

history.value: Bound-field visibility redesign: local-record-based display, always editable

history.text:
Full writeup. This started from a chat question ("how do bound fields represent when disconnected from their originating instance?") and turned into a full redesign after live feedback -- summarizing the whole arc here since there was no tracker issue for it until now.

ORIGINAL PROBLEM: a bound field stayed visually "locked" (non-editable) even on a device that could never verify or refresh the binding (no Jira/Salesforce proxy configured, no matching connector, or outside Tauri). Root cause: computeBoundValue's history-trust fallback (added for #112/b564316d) trusted the last derived history entry when the persisted ref lacked full data -- since history syncs across devices, a field locked by ONE device with the connector stayed permanently locked on every OTHER device that never could and never will have it, with zero path to recovery. Tom's words: "From the perspective of the person editing without the configured bound source, this is just a baffling hindrance."

FINAL DESIGN (settled over several rounds with Tom):
- A field is only ever editable-with-an-icon (never non-editable) -- isFieldLocked is deleted entirely. Bulk-set-field no longer skips "locked" rows, kanban drag is unconditional, every select/multiselect/text cell is always clickable.
- The bound/override icon (same link glyph as before, plus a new ! for override) is decided PURELY by a local-only record -- new store LOCAL_DERIVED_ENTRY_IDS_KEY, shaped {projectId: {issueId: {colId: entryId}}}, modeled directly on the merge log's own "store entry ids only, never content, never exported" discipline. No icon at all = never locally derived here (first-time, foreign-synced, or legacy). Link icon = this device's own last derived write still matches current. ! = it doesn't match any more (almost always a manual override).
- A manual override survives the ROUTINE resettle that runs after every edit, but NOT an explicit live refresh -- a genuine fresh sync is allowed to land on top unresisted, per Tom's own correction ("we wouldn't want to resist a connected source change landing on top of a manually overridden value").
- Provenance (derived vs typed, and from where) no longer appears in exported/signed history at all -- new entries drop origin:'derived' and the "(derived from state of X in column Y)" narrative entirely. Tom: "none of this providence makes it into exported copies of the data... it's not necessary for this data to be part of the signed payload." Already-signed historical entries keep whatever origin they were signed with (origin isn't part of a fresh entry's signablePayload, so this is safe either way).
- Mobile's field-detail isBound now requires the same local-record match as desktop (used to be just !!def.linkedSourceId).

THREE REAL BUGS found and fixed during verification against the full regression suite (each confirmed via git-stash-compare before treating as a real regression, not a pre-existing flake):

1. My own first implementation of applyLinkedRules's override guard was too strict -- it blocked ANY write whenever a prior history entry already existed at all, not just when this device's own local record proved a genuine override. That broke first-time rule binding over pre-existing data (binding a brand new rule to a field with old seed data should still take effect immediately). Fixed to only block when bindState is specifically 'overridden'. Separately, applyLiveLinkedRules's confident-empty clearing check was still reading the now-retired origin:'derived' tag -- silently broken the moment new entries stopped carrying it, since it would never match again. Both paths now use the local record instead.

2. Over-corrected on ref-chip gating: I applied the new "local reachability" check (isRefLocallyLive) to EVERY ref chip, not just the bound-value glyph. A directly-pasted or already-resolved Jira/Salesforce/GitHub/connector reference used to render unconditionally -- it's portable, already-resolved data (its own title/url baked in), nothing to do with a live rule binding. Gating it broke ref display outright on any device without a configured proxy secret, confirmed against 4+ real test failures (copy-as-markdown, issue-field, interaction, external-auth specs). Reverted that gate entirely (and the now-dead isRefLocallyLive Component wrapper) -- reachability now only ever gates the WRITE side (computeBoundValue/applyLinkedRules/applyLiveLinkedRules), never display.

3. Subtlest one: a merge bringing in history with an artificially-future sortKey (a test fixture simulating a collaborator's clock being 'ahead') used to have NO visible effect on what displayed, because the OLD buildTextCell bypassed history-latest-wins for a bound field entirely -- it live-recomputed from the source ref on every render, regardless of what any history entry said. Retiring that bypass (a deliberate, necessary part of this redesign) means display now honestly depends on write ordering -- which exposed that nextSortKey() was never seeded from loaded/merged data at all, purely wall-clock from component mount. A fresh post-merge recompute could end up sorting BEFORE the incoming entry it was supposed to supersede. Fixed by seeding _lastSortKey from the merged history's own max sortKey in applyMergedIssues. This is a real, previously-latent bug in the sortKey mechanism itself, just never triggered before since nothing depended on it for bound fields specifically.

Also fixed along the way: buildBulkBar's informational note/icon (for a field some selected rows currently derive from a linked issue) was gated in the MARKUP on a `locked` flag the JS side had already hardcoded to always-false when the whole "locked" concept was softened -- so it silently never rendered at all, while the plain chevron always did. Added a real hasDerivedNote flag and fixed the gating.

TEST COVERAGE: folded 2 disposable smoke tests into bound-value-panel.spec.js (reachability gates the glyph, not mere configuration) and row-selection.spec.js (bulk-set no longer skips a bound row); added kanban drag-on-a-bound-grouping-field coverage. Rewrote 8 pre-existing tests whose assertions baked in the old locked/unlocked model (bind-issue-field, select-fields x2, narrower-columns, kanban-grouping, bulk-paste-issues's removed-narrative-text check, plus mobile's isBound test) to match the new model.

KNOWN RESIDUAL GAP, filed separately as #214 (7333e8ea): mergeIssuePair/buildMergeIssueSummary/buildMergePreviewViewModel still check origin!=='derived' to decide whether two merging copies' divergent bound-field values are a genuine human-authorship overlap (surface a merge notice) or just two independent recomputations that self-heal. That check is now permanently blind to any NEWLY-derived entry from either side. UI/notice-accuracy only, not a data-correctness issue (the actual merged data is correct regardless) -- not fixed here, needs its own design thought since there's no portable signal left to distinguish a foreign derived value from a foreign manual edit.

VERIFICATION: full suite run twice (first run caught bugs 2 and 3 above; second run after fixing them was clean). 1098 passed both times; every failure cross-checked via isolation + git-stash-compare against a clean HEAD -- all confirmed pre-existing (github-sync.spec.js's debounced-push and reconnect-merge flakes, mentions.spec.js's first-connect flake, cross-tab-sync and merge-provenance's full-suite-load-only flakes). Committed as 3e535cb.
