history.text:
Done, committed as bec50b3 (plus a related rule-builder fix as 7e9c908, see below).

Tom's ask: split two concepts that had been mixed in Settings -- 'connected data sources' (other tracker systems wigwag references/pulls state from: Jira, GitHub, Salesforce, custom connectors) vs 'remote data stores' (where project data itself persists outside this device: GitHub repo sync today, WebDAV later).

NEW NAV ORDER: Identity, Connected data sources, Remote data stores, Notifications. Same count (4) in every runtime, just regrouped/renamed.

CONNECTED DATA SOURCES unifies three previously-separate surfaces:
- GitHub/Jira/Salesforce (previously read-only 'Built-in' rows with no Edit action) are now REAL editable rows -- Tom's explicit call: 'there's really not a lot of benefit in having the built-in options' stay un-editable from the same list custom connectors use. Editing one opens the same connector-form-overlay/modal shell a custom connector uses, but with a credential-only body (just Proxy URL + Secret) -- no Identity/Patterns/Macro/Test, no Delete, since a built-in can't be renamed/scripted/removed.
- The old 'Integrations' page's Jira/Salesforce/GitHub-proxy fields moved into their built-in's new modal. Google Drive's proxy fields (a link-renderer, not a data source) moved into the Connected data sources page as its own small section below the list.
- Custom connectors stay Tauri-only (no keychain/unrestricted fetch outside it) -- but the SECTION itself no longer is, since Jira/Salesforce/GitHub-proxy/Google Drive all already work in a plain browser.

history.text:
Fixed in 13b84d0.

Root cause (Tom's own diagnosis, confirmed in code): a field originally linked via the built-in Jira connector, then migrated to a custom connector matching the same key shape after Jira's proxy secret was cleared (the established way Tom disables a built-in -- see external-auth.spec.js's own comment on this), kept refreshing through the dead built-in on every refresh. refreshField dispatched purely off the field's stored (historical, immutable) fieldRef.system, never re-checking whether that system was still configured or whether a connector now matched the same identifier.

Two fixes:
1. refreshField now re-resolves jira/salesforce refs against the currently configured custom connectors whenever the built-in's own secret is unconfigured (jiraProxySecret/salesforceProxySecret -- not the proxy URL, which carries a harmless localhost default and stays truthy regardless). Self-healing: once the connector fetch succeeds it writes a fresh system:'connector' ref, so every later refresh takes the ordinary connector branch with no special case needed. A still-configured Jira link is unaffected even when an unrelated custom connector's pattern happens to overlap the same shape.
2. withRetry was also retrying a synchronous 'no proxy URL configured' error 3x with exponential backoff (~7s wasted) because that error has no .status and was indistinguishable from a real network rejection. fetchJiraData/fetchSalesforceData now mark it nonRetryable so it fails fast instead.

history.text:

history.text:
# Migration plan: tracker format v2

(Drafted in chat; could not be filed as a real tracker issue tonight —
`wigwag-agent.js`'s "Claude" GitHub identity still shows `token expired`,
same as earlier this session. This should move into the real tracker
once that's refreshed, per this project's own convention. Companion to
`docs/FORMAT_V2.md`, which has the full target shape — this is just the
"how do we get there" plan.)

## Stance

One real tracker instance exists today (Tom's, one Tauri app). Brutal,
one-time migration: rewrite the one real file once, then delete every
v1-specific code path — no permanent dual-format support anywhere.
Every stage below writes v2-only code from the start; nothing is kept
"just in case."

## Grounding (from a full-codebase survey, not guesswork)

- **wigwag-core.js** carries the overwhelming majority of the real
  logic: 6 signing functions, derivation (`deriveIssueValues`/
  `deriveIssueFieldRefs`/`latestEntryForField`/`issueActivitySortKeys`/
  `hydrateIssue`/`backfillIssueHistoryFromValues`), merge
  (`mergeIssuePair`/`computeIssueMerge`/`entryKey`/`commentKey`/
  `mergeCommentStreams`), parse (`parseJsonl`), squash/export
  (`squashHistory`).
- **`buildSource`/`normalizeRef`/`sourceRefHasFullData`** are a real
  *behavioral* change, not a rename: dropping `fetchedVia` means "which
  system does this ref belong to" flips from trusting a stored pointer
  to live URL-pattern matching — the same resolution `connectorMatches`
  already does for paste/refresh dispatch.
- **`src/wigwag-app.js`**: 68 raw `.history`/`.fieldRefs`/
  `.commentStreams` references, 14 `appendSignedHistory` call sites, 13
  `.num` references, field/option id generation (`'f_' + Date.now()`,
  `'opt_' + Date.now()`).
- **`wigwag-cli.js`** does **not** delegate to wigwag-core.js for writes
  — it hand-constructs entries itself (old shape) and does its own
  `.num` bookkeeping. Needs a full rewrite in lockstep with
  wigwag-core.js, not an afterthought.
- **`wigwag-client.js`/`wigwag-agent.js`**: write paths already go
  through the real browser UI (per this project's own design) — only
  their *read-back* logic (confirming a write landed, reporting state)
  touches raw issue shape and needs updating.
- **GitHub sync** (`pullGithubFile`/`pushGithubFile`/etc.): moves whole
  file bytes, never parses issue shape. Unaffected.
- **Tests**: 19 of 51 spec files hand-construct raw `history:`/
  `fieldRefs:`/`commentStreams:`/`.num` fixtures and need rewriting.
  Heaviest: `data-structures.spec.js`, `matrix-host.spec.js`,
  `interaction.spec.js`.
- **`docs/FORMAT.md`**: full rewrite (promote `FORMAT_V2.md` once
  shipped). `docs/EDITING.md`: untouched (build-pipeline doc, not format).

## Clarified during design (not just "same as v1 minus some fields")

- A bound/derived field's value is an ordinary write, authored by
  whichever device computed it — **no special-cased conflict check**.
  Last-`sortKey`-wins resolves a disagreement here exactly like any
  other field-edit conflict. This removes a whole special case from
  `mergeIssuePair` (today's `origin !== 'derived'` filter), not just a
  field.

## Staged sequence

Each stage independently verifiable via the existing Playwright suite
before moving on — same discipline this project already uses for staged
work (never edit/rebuild mid-run).

1. **Signing layer first** (wigwag-core.js) — everything downstream
   depends on the final entry shape. Rewrite `signablePayload`/
   `signableProjectPayload`/`redactedPayload`/`redactedProjectPayload`/
   `signableCommentPayload`/`redactedCommentPayload` for the new entry
   fields (`id, actor, value, sortKey` — no `text`/`time`/`origin`/
   separate `email`); `verifyPayload`/`signWithKey` for `alg`-aware,
   base64url signatures; introduce the `sig: {alg, full, redacted}`
   wrapper.
2. **Derivation** (wigwag-core.js) — rewrite `deriveIssueValues`,
   retire `deriveIssueFieldRefs` as a separate function (folded into
   value resolution now that `fieldRef` isn't a sibling key),
   `latestEntryForField`, `issueActivitySortKeys`, `hydrateIssue`,
   `backfillIssueHistoryFromValues` to read `issue.fields[id].history`
   directly — no more filtering a flat array by `.field`.
   `migrateLegacyComments` retires entirely (no more separate
   `commentStreams` section to migrate into).
3. **Live system resolution** (wigwag-core.js) — rewrite `buildSource`/
   `normalizeRef`/`sourceRefHasFullData` to resolve "which system does
   this ref belong to" from the ref's own shape/URL pattern live, not a
   stored `fetchedVia`. This is the one stage that's a real behavior
   change, not a mechanical shape update — needs its own careful test
   pass.
4. **Merge** (wigwag-core.js) — rewrite `mergeIssuePair`/
   `computeIssueMerge`/`entryKey`/`commentKey`/`unionByKey` for the new
   shape; drop the `origin !== 'derived'` special case entirely (see
   "Clarified during design" above); `mergeCommentStreams` retires,
   since comment-stream fields now merge through the exact same
   per-field union logic as everything else; drop all `num` generation.
5. **Squash/export/parse** (wigwag-core.js) — rewrite `squashHistory`
   for the new entry shape; add the new `_comment`-generation function
   (export-time only, per `FORMAT_V2.md`'s own rule — never stored,
   never read on import); rewrite `parseJsonl`'s `keyRef` rehydration
   to walk `fields[*].history`.
6. **App call sites** (src/wigwag-app.js) — rewrite `appendSignedHistory`
   itself and its 14 call sites for the new signature; rewrite field/
   option id generation to the `type__name`/label-slug scheme with
   collision-suffix-on-collision; update every direct `.history`/
   `.fieldRefs`/`.commentStreams`/`.num` reference (68 + 13 sites per
   the survey).
7. **wigwag-cli.js** — full rewrite in lockstep with stages 1-2 (it
   duplicates write logic rather than delegating to wigwag-core.js, so
   it can't just follow along passively).
8. **wigwag-client.js / wigwag-agent.js** — update read-back logic only
   (reporting a write's result back to the caller); no write-path
   changes needed, per the survey.
9. **docs/FORMAT.md** — full rewrite, promoting `FORMAT_V2.md`'s content
   and retiring the "draft" framing once the above has actually shipped.
10. **Tests** — rewrite the 19 spec files with hand-built raw fixtures;
    full suite run against every stage, not just at the end.
11. **The actual one-time migration** — a standalone script that reads
    Tom's real `tracker.jsonl` (v1) and emits the v2 shape: every field
    (including currently-opaque `f_.../opt_...` ids) gets a fresh
    `type__name`/slug id derived from its current label; `commentStreams`
    folds into `fields`; `num`/`origin`/`time`/duplicate `actor|email`/
    `fetchedVia` are dropped; signatures move to the new `{alg, full,
    redacted}` shape (note: existing v1 signatures can't be algorithm-
    tagged retroactively without re-signing — needs its own decision,
    not resolved here). Run once, verify against the real file, commit.
12. **Delete v1-specific code** — given the brutal-migration stance,
    there should be nothing v1-specific left to delete by this point;
    this step is really "confirm nothing was kept as a safety net that
    shouldn't have been."

## Open items carried over from `FORMAT_V2.md` (unresolved, need a decision before coding, not during)

- Custom-connector `matchedId`, post-`fetchedVia`-removal.
- The wigwag-internal ref's own fold-into-`value` shape.
- Exact collision-suffix algorithm for field/option slugs.
- **New, surfaced by stage 11**: can't retroactively tag old signatures
  with `alg` without re-signing, since the algorithm identifier wasn't
  part of what was signed originally — needs its own explicit call
  (re-sign everything during migration using the current identity? Keep
  old signatures verifiable under an implied legacy algorithm forever,
  even post-"brutal migration"? Not decided.)

Merging a v2-format file onto a stale v1-shaped local project can corrupt data

history.text:
Found live during the v1->v2 offline migration work (tracker issue 3212e2ff): mergeIssuePair/computeIssueMerge (wigwag-core.js) assume both sides of a merge are already v2-shaped (issue.fields[colId].history). A real session hit the mismatched case directly: a browser still had a stale, pre-migration (v1-shaped: flat issue.history + issue.commentStreams, no issue.fields at all) copy of a project loaded, then imported a freshly-migrated v2 file for the same project id. handleImportParsed treated this as an update and merged rather than doing a clean import -- the result showed a real, previously-edited comment as a bare '-- redacted --' placeholder, with the actual text gone from the UI entirely.

Loading the same migrated file fresh (no stale local copy to merge against) renders correctly -- confirmed in-session. So the migration output itself was fine; the corruption was specifically in merging across format versions.

Not yet root-caused inside mergeIssuePair/computeIssueMerge itself -- haven't traced exactly which step mishandles a v1-shaped side. Worth either: (a) a formatVersion/shape check that refuses to merge (or falls back to treating the v1 side as empty/replaced rather than unioned) when the two sides aren't structurally comparable, or (b) at minimum, detecting this case and warning the user before merging rather than silently producing a result that looks like real content was redacted.

Related, still-open gap from the same incident response: wigwag-client.js's connect() has a formatVersion safety check that currently fails OPEN on an inconclusive remote read, not closed -- flagged separately, not yet fixed. This issue is about the local merge path specifically, not that one.

history.value: GitHub access: embrace repo-scoped PATs, smooth provisioning + expiry UX

history.text:
Plan for this issue (full detail in chat/plan file, summarizing before starting implementation per project convention):

Replaces github_scoping.zip's original three-tier design (app-level GitHub identity via device-code OAuth + OS keychain, shared across connectors, plus a wigwag-enforced per-project repo allow-list). That design was revised after live discussion:

1. Classic GitHub OAuth Apps cannot be scoped to specific repos at all (verified against GitHub's own docs) -- rules out device-code/standard OAuth entirely.
2. GitHub Apps can do real per-repo scoping, but only via a backend holding the App's private key -- which isn't "a server that might get hacked," it's standing, continuous capability: that key alone can mint a working token for ANY installation of the app, for any user, with no re-consent. Categorically worse than wigwag's current trust model (nothing it operates ever touches a credential). Considered and rejected running this via a wigwag.work backend for exactly this reason.
3. Fine-grained Personal Access Tokens are the only mechanism that gets both real per-repo scoping AND zero standing third-party access, since the user creates and holds the token themselves with no wigwag-operated infrastructure ever in the loop.

So: embrace fine-grained PATs as the one credential mechanism, for both GitHub connector enrichment and project sync's existing githubTokenOverride field. No new Rust code, no new keychain namespace, no shared identity concept -- just making PAT provisioning and expiry/renewal painless:

- Deep-link "Create a token on GitHub" into GitHub's pre-fillable fine-grained PAT creation page (name/description/permissions/expiry are pre-fillable via query params, confirmed; repo selection is not, which is fine -- that should stay a conscious manual step).
- After a credential is saved, confirm what it can actually see via one GET /user/repos call through the existing unrestricted connected_source_fetch Tauri relay -- catches a wrong repo-selection mistake immediately.
- Reuse that confirmed repo list to disambiguate a bare #123 paste when a connector's token covers more than one repo.
- On a 401 from any GitHub-kind fetch (enrichment or sync), stop retrying and surface a clear CTA pointing at the fine-grained token LIST page (github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens, not the creation page) with copy to click Regenerate on the named token -- preserves repo scope and just refreshes expiry, instead of recreating from scratch.

Sequencing note: issue c23bd3b5 (migrate GitHub off its dedicated credential modal onto the shared connector editor, deleting fetchGithubData/openBuiltinSourceForm) is still Todo and unscheduled. Confirmed with Tom: this work proceeds now against the current GitHub-specific modal/fetchGithubData; c23bd3b5, whenever it happens, carries the provisioning link/confirmation-fetch/401-handling logic forward into the unified editor.

Five staged commits: (1) token-creation deep-link helper + UI on both the connector credential field and githubTokenOverride, (2) post-save confirmation fetch + repo list display, (3) bare #N disambiguation against a connector's confirmed repos, (4) reactive 401 handling with a regenerate-token CTA, (5) docs/copy pass + full regression.

Done -- 7 commits total, all independently verified with real tests, full regression green throughout.

Core redesign (5 commits):
1. Deep-link token-creation UI: githubTokenCreationUrl/parseGithubShortId/GITHUB_TOKEN_LIST_URL in wigwag-core.js, plus "Create a token on GitHub" links on the builtin GitHub connector's credential field and project sync's token-override field -- pre-filled with the minimum permissions each needs (issues:read for enrichment, contents:write for sync) via GitHub's own pre-fillable fine-grained PAT creation URL.
2. Confirmation fetch: after a new GitHub credential is saved, one real GET /user/repos call (via the existing connected_source_fetch relay, no new Rust code) confirms what it can actually see, shown on the connector row.
3. Bare "#N" disambiguation: resolves only against the connector's own confirmed-repos list from step 2.
4. Reactive 401 handling: both sync (pull/push) and enrichment refresh distinguish a rejected credential from a generic failure. Sync's status indicator shows a clear tooltip and, on click, opens the token LIST page (not the creation page) so the existing token can be regenerated -- preserves its repo scope.
5. Copy pass: the three credential-entry points (builtin connector, per-project sync override, identity-level default token) now actively recommend a fine-grained, repo-scoped PAT over a classic broad one.

Follow-up work, discussed and agreed with Tom after the core redesign shipped:
6. Removed the identity-level "Sign in with GitHub" OAuth flow entirely (signInWithGithub, the message-handshake listener, bridges/github-oauth-proxy.js, its npm script). It was a classic OAuth App authorization-code flow -- exactly the credential mechanism this redesign ruled out for being structurally incapable of per-repo scoping -- sitting right next to copy now telling people not to use that kind of token. Decided to KEEP the identity-level default token field itself (unlike OAuth sign-in, it's just storage, not a structurally-broken mechanism, and removing it would be more disruptive for anyone currently relying on it for working sync).
7. Since that field is being kept, gave it the same treatment the connector/sync-override fields already had: a "Create a token on GitHub" deep-link, and a confirmation fetch -- shown as a repo COUNT rather than a full list (this token is explicitly the broad, shared one). Both the connector and identity-level confirmation now also read GitHub's own real GitHub-Authentication-Token-Expiration response header (confirmed real via live research, not a guess) off the same call, so the UI shows the actual expiry GitHub reports, no new request needed. This meaningfully improves on commit 4's earlier "reactive, not proactive" expiry decision, since reading GitHub's own authoritative answer sidesteps the two problems that ruled out proactive tracking back then (guessing what the user picked, or asking them to redundantly re-enter it).

Also found and fixed, unrelated to the redesign itself but blocking all tracker interaction from this environment: wigwag-client.js's format-safety check (fetchRemoteFormatVersion) was hitting a real ENOBUFS -- its curl fallback had no maxBuffer override (Node defaults to 1MB), and tracker.jsonl has grown past that. Looked like network flakiness for several retries before the real cause showed up: plain curl to the exact same URL always succeeded; only the execFileSync path inside the safety check failed, deterministically, every time. Fixed with a 64MB maxBuffer.

Separately (not part of this issue): did real diagnostic work on the window-title boot bug using a newly-provisioned virtual display (Xvfb/fluxbox/xdotool, added to .devcontainer/Dockerfile) to actually run the built Linux Tauri binary and read its real OS-level window title -- confirmed the existing fix works correctly there. Still open whether it holds on macOS, which this sandbox can't test.

history.value: Project switcher: group projects into a folder tree by name prefix

history.text:
Plan for this issue (design handoff folders.zip, reviewed with Tom before starting):

Follow-up fix (feabf2c): Tom reported the hover highlight was glitchy. Root cause confirmed empirically (elementFromPoint sampled across a real row) -- the tree-line/icon/label overlay elements (z-index:1) sat on top of the highlight pill (z-index:0, the one actually carrying the hover behavior) with no pointer-events:none, so the browser delivered mouse events to whichever layer was topmost at each pixel rather than the pill underneath. Fixed by adding pointer-events:none to every decorative overlay; new regression test samples hover at 5 points across a row's full width to catch this class of bug specifically.
